desc: Cost-Effectiveness Analysis Review and Human-Centered Design Support for Routine Immunization Demand
full: Request for technical assistance to conduct a comprehensive review and provide guidance on the cost-effectiveness analysis for Human-Centered Design interventions aimed at improving routine immunization demand in woredas with high number of zero-dose and under-immunized communities. The support will ensure methodological rigor, alignment with global standards, and usability of findings for decision-making and scale-up. Objectives Technical Review Assess the conceptual and methodological soundness of the proposed cost-effectiveness analysis. Ensure alignment with recognized global standards and best practices for CEA in public health and demand-generation interventions. Methodological Strengthening Provide recommendations on appropriate costing approaches, outcome measures, comparators, and analytic frameworks tailored to HCD for RI demand. Ensure integration of both behavioral and health system outcomes where applicable. Improved Analytical Design Validate assumptions, data sources, and modeling approaches. Identify gaps and propose feasible, context-appropriate adjustments. Decision-Making Utility Ensure outputs are policy-relevant, interpretable, and actionable for programmatic and investment decisions. Capacity Strengthening Provide guidance and learning opportunities for ECO teams to better understand and apply cost-effectiveness analysis in similar contexts. Expected Deliverables Detailed feedback on the concept note, including strengths, gaps, and prioritized recommendations. Suggested analytical model, including costing structure, outcome indicators, timeline and perspectives etc. Practical guidance on conducting CEA for HCD-driven RI demand interventions. Online comments and suggested revisions for immediate improvement. Walkthrough of recommendations and discussion with ECO team and relevant stakeholders. Other Global Practices to Involve SBC-immunization team should be involved to ensure that behavioral pathways, demand-side outcomes, and HCD-specific intervention effects are appropriately reflected in the analysis. Health Economics or Public Finance teams may be engaged to provide specialized expertise in cost-effectiveness methodologies, economic modeling, and interpretation of results for policy and investment decisions. Immunization or health programme specialists may contribute to validating routine immunization indicators, assessing programmatic feasibility, and ensuring alignment with RI goals and standards. Office of Innovation or HCD experts may be consulted to ensure that the analysis accurately captures the iterative and user-centered nature of HCD processes and appropriately values design-driven interventions. Strategic Accelerators for High-Quality and Accelerated Results Existing global guidance and standardized cost-effectiveness analysis frameworks, such as those developed by WHO and UNICEF, should be leveraged to ensure methodological consistency while avoiding delays associated with developing new approaches. Rapid and pragmatic analytical methods, including simplified decision-tree models or light-touch analyses, should be applied where appropriate to balance analytical rigor with timeliness, particularly in data-constrained settings. An iterative review approach should be adopted, involving an initial rapid technical review followed by more in-depth feedback, to ensure timely progress while maintaining quality. Cross-country learning and evidence from similar HCD or SBC for RI interventions should be incorporated to inform assumptions, benchmarks, and interpretation of results. Embedded capacity strengthening approaches, such as joint working sessions or technical clinics, should be implemented to simultaneously build local capacity while advancing the analytical work.

desc: Healthcare Waste Management Strategy and Action Plan Finalization Support for Cambodia
full: Description Cambodia's Ministry of Health (MoH), with UNICEF support, has developed a draft Healthcare Waste Management (HCWM) Strategy and 5-Year Action Plan (2025–2029) grounded in a nationwide HCWM situational assessment conducted in 2024. The strategy articulates five strategic objectives covering legal/regulatory strengthening, capacity building, facility-level waste handling, treatment and disposal, and data/monitoring systems, with a costed action plan totalling approximately USD 4.17 million across short- and medium-term activities. The strategy and costed action plan are at an advanced draft stage (v06 and v04 respectively) and require technical finalization before submission for MoH endorsement. UNICEF Cambodia is seeking technical assistance, including an in-country visit to facilitate a stakeholder finalization workshop in Phnom Penh, to consolidate outstanding technical, financial, and policy inputs and bring the documents to a state ready for official government review and adoption. Objectives / Expectations Review and quality-assure the draft HCWM Strategy (v06) against international standards (WHO, Basel Convention, Stockholm Convention, SDGs, One Health) and the findings of the 2024 national HCWM assessment, identifying any remaining gaps, inconsistencies, or areas requiring strengthening. Review and validate the costed Action Plan (v04) , including cost assumptions, activity sequencing, responsible entity assignments, and financing logic — ensuring coherence across all five strategic objectives and alignment with government budget cycles and partner programming. Facilitate a multi-stakeholder finalization workshop in Phnom Penh with MoH (Department of Hospital Services), Ministry of Environment, Provincial Health Departments, development partners (UNICEF, WHO, others), and relevant NGOs to: - Present and discuss the final draft strategy and action plan - Consolidate feedback and resolve outstanding content decisions - Build stakeholder ownership ahead of formal endorsement Incorporate workshop outputs into a revised, finalization-ready version of both the Strategy and Action Plan documents. Support UNICEF Cambodia and MoH in preparing a brief dissemination/endorsement pathway, including recommended next steps for formal government approval.

desc: Adolescent Mental Health Programme Design and Technical Quality Assurance Support for China
full: UNICEF China is working with the National Center for Mental Health, under the guidance of the National Health Commission, to advance the adolescent mental health workstreams included in the 2026–2027 UNICEF China–NHC Rolling Work Plan. These include: (1) technical adaptation and possible piloting of EASE and BLOOM as low-intensity psychological support tools for children and adolescents; and (2) localization and possible integration of MMAPP as a measurement, monitoring and evidence-generation tool for adolescent mental health. Technical assistance is requested from UNICEF global/regional colleagues to support the overall design, sequencing and technical quality assurance of these workstreams. The support would help UNICEF China and national counterparts clarify how EASE, BLOOM and MMAPP should be positioned in the China context, how they should be sequenced, and what technical, ethical, safeguarding, quality assurance and implementation requirements need to be addressed before adaptation, piloting or wider use. For EASE and BLOOM, support is requested to guide the technical orientation, adaptation and implementation planning process, including clarification of target age groups and target populations, training duration and modality, possible use of blended online/offline training, requirements for trainers and supervisors, participant identification and recruitment approaches that avoid stigma or labelling, and arrangements for supervision, referral, safeguarding and quality assurance. Particular guidance is needed on how to manage BLOOM, given that the tool is still under development/piloting globally and may require careful handling of materials, version control and sharing conditions. For MMAPP, support is requested to review the draft China workplan and provide guidance on translation, cultural adaptation, cognitive testing, pre-testing, ethical/safeguarding considerations, sensitive modules such as suicidality-related items, and the feasibility of linking MMAPP with existing or planned adolescent mental health monitoring, survey or data platforms in China. The expected support may include written technical comments on draft workplans, participation in technical clarification calls with UNICEF China and national counterparts, advice on sequencing and implementation readiness, and guidance for preparing future expert consultations with the National Center for Mental Health and national expert teams. The technical assistance will help ensure that UNICEF China’s support to national counterparts is aligned with UNICEF global guidance, technically sound, ethically appropriate, and feasible within China’s health, education and monitoring systems.

desc: Transition Support for HSTP Portfolio – Health Section Leadership Gap
full: TA Hub Request Submission Title Transition Support for HSTP Portfolio – Health Section Leadership Gap Requesting Office UNICEF South Sudan Background & Justification The Health Systems Strengthening and Transformation Programme (HSTP) represents one of the largest and most strategic health portfolios in the Country Office, with significant government, donor, and partner engagement. Following the transition of the former Chief of Health (Joyce Mphaya) to COE and the abolition of the P5 Team Leader position due to funding constraints, the section is currently operating with a leadership gap at a critical period for programme implementation and stakeholder engagement. The incoming Chief of Health is scheduled to assume duty on 12 July 2026 . In the interim, there is a risk of: Disruption to implementation momentum Reduced quality of strategic engagement with government and partners Loss of institutional knowledge and continuity To mitigate these risks, this request seeks short-term deployment of Joyce Mphaya from 28 June for approximately three weeks to provide structured transition support, ensure continuity, and facilitate a smooth handover. Purpose of the TA Request To ensure seamless transition, program continuity, and sustained stakeholder engagement for the HSTP portfolio during the leadership gap period. Scope of Work The deployed TA (Joyce Mphaya) will provide senior-level leadership support across four key areas: Transition Management Prepare and deliver a structured transition and handover process Ensure incoming Chief of Health is fully briefed and oriented Programme Continuity Maintain oversight of ongoing HSTP implementation Track progress and ensure priority deliverables are not delayed Stakeholder Engagement Sustain engagement with key government, donor, and partner stakeholders Represent UNICEF in critical coordination platforms Team Leadership and Coordination Provide interim leadership and direction to the Health Section Align team around immediate priorities and deliverables Expected Outputs / Deliverables 1. Transition & Handover Package Comprehensive HSTP briefing dossier , including: Programme status (achievements, gaps, risks) Priority actions for next 3–6 months Stakeholder mapping and engagement plan Completed handover sessions with incoming Chief Documented decisions, risks, and action tracker 2. Programme Continuity Assurance Updated HSTP implementation dashboard/tracker Identification and follow-up of critical bottlenecks Short-term continuity plan to prevent disruptions 3. Stakeholder Engagement Participation in key government and donor coordination meetings Updated partner engagement and communication plan Strategic messaging to reinforce UNICEF leadership and continuity 4. Internal Team Alignment Interim team workplan (July–September) Clear delegation of responsibilities across team members Internal briefing notes to senior management on risks and priorities Expected Outcomes No interruption in HSTP implementation Strong continuity in government and partner engagement Incoming Chief of Health assumes role with full situational awareness Health team remains aligned, functional, and performance-oriented Duration 28 June – Approximately 3 weeks (covering transition period and onboarding of incoming Chief) Urgency Level High – Immediate support is required to prevent disruption to one of the largest and most critical programme portfolios. Strategic Accelerators The TA will leverage the following accelerators to maximize impact: Real-time data and dashboards for rapid decision-making Integrated PHC approach linking health, nutrition, and WASH Strengthened partner coordination around HSTP priorities Risk-informed programming to proactively manage disruptions Fast-track decision-making mechanisms for urgent actions Targeted capacity support to team to absorb leadership gap Value for Money / Strategic Importance This short-term TA will: Safeguard continuity of a high-value, high-visibility programme Reduce risks associated with leadership gaps Ensure sustained delivery of results for children Enable rapid and effective onboarding of new Chief of Health

desc: National Immunization Strategy Mid-Term Review and Gavi 6.0 Prioritization Support
full: The Ministry of Health of South Sudan is planning to conduct a Mid-Term Review (MTR) of the National Immunization Strategy (NIS) 2023–2027. The review aims to assess progress achieved to date, identify implementation gaps and challenges, and generate actionable recommendations to strengthen implementation during the remaining strategy period. This exercise is of significant strategic importance, as its findings will directly inform the development and prioritization of the Gavi 6.0 framework, ensuring that future investments are aligned with national priorities, emerging needs, and evidence-based programming. Given the complexity and importance of the review, specialized technical assistance is required to enhance the rigor, objectivity, and overall quality of the process. In this regard, UNICEF South Sudan, in collaboration with the Ministry of Health, is requesting support from the Centre of Excellence (CoE) to deploy Dr. Onome Dibosa Osadolor, Senior Health Specialist, to provide technical assistance during the mission. Dr. Osadolor’s extensive expertise in immunization systems strengthening and programme evaluation will be instrumental in ensuring a robust and credible review process. Her support will also contribute to the finalization of the Health System Strengthening (HSS) “Bridging the Gap” priorities. The mission is scheduled to take place from 7–9 July 2026. Given the limited timeframe and the critical outputs expected from the exercise, support through Gavi 6.0-funded technical assistance is justified to ensure the successful completion of the review and delivery of high-quality outcomes.

desc: Climate Change Curriculum Framework for upper secondary education
full: Tanzania is currently piloting a Climate Change Curriculum Framework for upper secondary education in three schools and is developing a Gender-Responsive Climate Education Curriculum Framework for primary and lower secondary education, aligned across levels. The framework aims to integrate climate science, sustainability, and resilience into learning, equipping children and adolescents with the knowledge, skills, and behaviors needed to respond to climate challenges, with potential to reach over 10 million learners. The TA is requested for the technical review of draft framework. Approximately US$9,500 is also requested to facilitate stakeholder review and validation workshops, including potential participation of education COE specialist, Carolin Wäldchen. These activities will convene the Ministry of Education, Science and Technology, the Tanzania Institute of Education, and technical experts to ensure technical quality, policy alignment, stakeholder ownership, and readiness for adoption. The TA is expected to strengthen the technical quality of the framework (including structured review of draft versions), ensure alignment with national policies and curriculum standards, build stakeholder consensus and ownership, and ensure coherence across education levels while accelerating readiness for implementation. Key deliverables include a technical review of draft framework(s), successful facilitation of 1–2 validation workshops, a validated curriculum framework, and documentation outlining stakeholder engagement and pathways to endorsement, alongside a brief note on implementation readiness. The request will benefit from engagement with global practices such as UNICEF's Green Rising movement for youth engagement in climate action, gender-responsive education frameworks (UNICEF/UNGEI), competency-based curriculum design approaches, and Education for Sustainable Development. Strategic accelerators include strong co-leadership from MoEST and TIE, leveraging lessons from the upper secondary pilot, early alignment with assessment systems, embedding gender considerations throughout, combining local and global expertise, and linking the framework to teacher training and digital learning resources.

desc: Technical Support for Learning Passport Implementation in Angola
full: TA Request: Technical Support for Learning Passport Implementation in Angola Short Description of the Request This request seeks Technical Assistance (TA) to support a comprehensive technical review, optimization, and scale-up of the Learning Passport platform in Angola. The TA will focus on strengthening platform performance, content alignment with the national curriculum, user engagement, and system sustainability. The objective is to ensure the Learning Passport effectively delivers inclusive, high-quality digital learning opportunities for children and adolescents, particularly the most vulnerable. Objectives / Expectations Platform Optimization and Technical Review Assess current Learning Passport configuration, functionality, and performance. Identify technical gaps and opportunities for improving usability, scalability, and offline access. Content Alignment and Quality Assurance Review existing content and ensure alignment with Angola’s national curriculum and language needs. Strengthen processes for content curation, adaptation, and quality control. User Experience and Engagement Analyze user data (if available) to identify engagement patterns and barriers. Recommend strategies to improve learner retention, accessibility, and inclusivity (gender, disability, rural access). Capacity Building and System Strengthening Support capacity development of government counterparts and partners on platform management, data use, and content administration. Enhance national ownership and sustainability of the platform. Strategic Positioning and Scale-Up Provide recommendations for scaling the Learning Passport within national systems. Strengthen integration with education sector priorities and digital learning strategies. Other Global Practices to be Involved To ensure a robust and high-quality response, the following global practices should be engaged: Education Programme Group (PG): Guidance on digital learning, curriculum alignment, and pedagogy. Office of Innovation (OoI): Expertise on Learning Passport platform optimization and digital product scaling. ICTD (Information and Communication Technology Division): Technical infrastructure, platform performance, and integration. Data & Analytics (DAPM / Data teams): User insights, monitoring, and learning analytics. Partnerships / Public Partnerships Division (PPD): Strategic engagement and resource mobilization support. Strategic Accelerators The following accelerators can help deliver faster, higher-quality results for children: Leverage Existing Learning Passport Global Tools: Reuse proven templates, governance models, and platform features already deployed in other countries. Cross-Country Learning: Apply lessons learned from other Learning Passport implementations (e.g., content strategies, engagement approaches). Rapid Content Digitization Pipelines: Use standardized processes and tools to accelerate curriculum digitization. Offline Access Solutions: Prioritize low-connectivity solutions (e.g., downloadable content, local servers) for equitable reach. Data-Driven Decision Making: Use real-time dashboards and analytics to continuously improve user experience and engagement. Public-Private Partnerships: Engage telecom providers and edtech partners to expand connectivity and platform access. User-Centered Design Approaches: Incorporate feedback from learners and teachers to ensure relevance and usability.

desc: CC4C: support and scale an integrated initiative focused on strengthening environmental school clubs and youth clubs
full: The country office requests technical assistance to support and scale an integrated initiative focused on strengthening environmental school clubs and youth clubs through a structured climate action curriculum. Specifically, under the Climate Collaboration for Children (CC4C) programme, the proposed support will focus on: (i) the development of a standardized module serving as a practical guide for the implementation of environmental club activities, ensuring continuous engagement throughout the school year; (ii) the design and deployment of a monitoring tool to track activities across approximately 90 environmental clubs, enabling regular follow-up and the provision of tailored support based on school-level inputs; and (iii) the strengthening of capacities of club facilitators to effectively deliver climate action activities. The initiative will be implemented in collaboration with RPEEBU (Réseau pour la Promotion Environnementale au Burundi), a nationwide network of about 120 school and university environmental clubs established in 2004. It aims at (re)-strengthening school initiatives by piloting a technically sound, financially sustainable model for environmental engagement, with a view to scaling up progressively to reach an even larger pool of schools across Burundi.

desc: Health Sector Transformation Project Oversight and Technical Support for South Sudan
full: The Health Section of the UNICEF South Sudan Country Office seeks technical support through the deployment of a Senior Health Specialist to oversee the implementation of the Health Sector Transformation Project (HSTP). The HSTP, which commenced on 1 July 2024 with funding from the Multi-Donor Trust Fund (MDTF), is a key platform for strengthening health systems, improving service delivery, and enhancing health outcomes in a fragile context. As the project enters Year 3 (July 2026 – June 2027), its final implementation phase. There is a critical need to accelerate delivery, consolidate gains, and ensure achievement of all planned outputs. The period from July to October 2026 marks a pivotal transition point, requiring intensified program execution, monitoring, and reporting. During this phase, the project will continue scaling up interventions in primary healthcare, maternal and child health, disease prevention, and health system strengthening. However, a significant capacity gap is anticipated within the Health Section at a time when strong technical leadership and oversight are essential. This gap poses risks to program continuity, quality assurance, coordination, and timely decision-making, and could undermine progress toward meeting donor requirements and achieving project targets by June 2027. To mitigate these risks and ensure successful project completion, the deployment of a Senior Health Specialist is essential. The Specialist will provide strategic oversight of MDTF-funded activities, strengthen partner coordination, and ensure high-quality monitoring, reporting, and adaptive program management. This role will also reinforce UNICEF’s surge capacity, enabling timely technical guidance, effective management of peak operational demands, and safeguarding the continuity and effectiveness of essential health services. Such strategic reinforcement is critical to maintaining momentum, achieving planned results, and ensuring the overall impact and integrity of the HSTP during this decisive implementation period.

desc: Request for Support – High-Level Multisectoral Technical Dialogue on Life Skills and Violence Prevention
full: Following Laura Salamanca’s guidance, we would like to explore the possibility of receiving support from the Adolescent Girls Hub for the High-Level Multisectoral Technical Dialogue: “Life Skills as a Strategic Lever for Violence Prevention among Adolescents and Young People,” which UNICEF Peru is organizing jointly with the Ministry of Women and Vulnerable Populations (MIMP) on June 16. The event aims to position life skills development and evidence generation as strategic components for violence prevention, as well as for the sustainability and scale-up of interventions targeting adolescents and young people. It will bring together senior authorities and technical teams from key government sectors, including the Ministries of Economy and Finance, Education, Health, Social Development and Inclusion, Labour, Production, and Culture, among other strategic stakeholders. As part of UNICEF Peru’s technical assistance to MIMP, we have supported the update of the Life Skills Facilitation Guide for the Empowered and Autonomous Women intervention, which corresponds to Product 13A of Peru’s Results-Based Budget Programme for the Reduction of Violence against Women. This process represents an important opportunity to promote the sustainability and scalability of lessons learned through UNICEF’s For and With Adolescents agenda. In particular, the updated guide incorporates concepts, methodologies, approaches and tools that were developed and validated through the +Poder Adolescente (More Power to Adolescents) programme, implemented with support from the Gender Thematic Fund for Adolescent Empowerment. Building on a pilot implementation jointly conducted with MIMP, these approaches are now being progressively integrated into a national public intervention targeting adolescent girls and young women living in poverty and vulnerable situations. This will allow methodologies originally developed by UNICEF to be implemented at scale through a government-funded programme, strengthening their long-term sustainability. Currently, the intervention reaches more than 4,000 adolescent girls and young women across all 24 regions of Peru , through 81 local governments and implementation districts , and is supported by an annual public budget of approximately USD 1.5 million . This makes the process a particularly valuable opportunity to institutionalize evidence-based approaches and progressively expand their reach and impact. In this context, and following Laura Salamanca’s guidance to connect this process with global evidence and experience, we would like to explore the possibility of having a colleague from the Hub—ideally Made or another Spanish-speaking colleague—participate in the session on international evidence on life skills and adolescent empowerment , scheduled from 9:50 a.m. to 10:20 a.m. (Peru time) .

desc: Cold Chain Equipment Circular Economy and End-of-Life Management Support for Mozambique
full: 1. Background The Republic of Korea (ROK) is a key UNICEF partner and supports the Expanded Program of Immunization (EPI) in Mozambique for the provision of support to the Government of Mozambique through the Ministry of Health (MISAU) to strengthen immunization systems, including the management of cold chain equipment (CCE) under the Expanded Programme on Immunization (EPI). As aging and obsolete refrigeration equipment reaches end-of-life, there is increasing concern regarding environmental risks, including improper disposal of refrigerants and hazardous components such as refrigerants, compressor oils, insulation foams, batteries, electronic components, metals, plastics and unsafe storage, dismantling or disposal practices. Gavi provides comprehensive guidance on managing EPI ageing and obsolete cold chain equipment, the Cold Chain Equipment Optimisation Platform (CCEOP). The CCEOP aims to improve the quality and accuracy of national cold chain equipment inventory (CCEOP) data, ensuring that governments can make informed decisions on vaccine distribution, storage, equipment maintenance, and repair. The Ministry of Health of Mozambique (MoH) has requested support from UNICEF to identify innovative and cost-effective solutions to mitigate environmental risks associated with the disposal of cold chain equipment. In response to this request, UNICEF, through the catalytic partnership with the Republic of Korea, aims to support MoH in implementing a pilot to mitigate these risks and align with Gavi guidelines and best international practices on the disposal of and mitigation of environmental risks associated with CCE. Together with MoH, UNICEF will implement an innovative pilot focused on establishing safe, environmentally sound, and circular end-of-life management pathways for safe disposal CCE. The pilot aims to promote circular economic approaches, including the reuse of parts, refurbishment, and responsible recycling of such products, while ensuring compliance with environmental standards. It will also generate evidence and operational insights to inform scalable national strategies. To inform this pilot, UNICEF seeks two (2) consultants (national and international) to support with initial groundwork to inform this pilot in the context of Mozambique. 2. Objective of the Assignment The overall objective of this consultancy is to support UNICEF Mozambique in the design and operationalization of environmentally sound and circular end-of-life management pathways for EPI cold chain equipment (CCE). Specifically, the assignment aims to: Review literature and guidelines/ best practices, and costs insights for the separation, disposable, reuse, refurbishment, recycling of EPI cold chain in other countries, particularly in SADC region, if any; Assess current landscape by conducting a mapping of the state of play of CCE in the health sector in selected health facilities after agreement with EPI/MoH based on budget aviability (what is the treatment of ageing and obsolete equipment, where is it taken to?); Mapping of different players in Mozambique and /or SADC region working on waste management (disposal, separation, reuse, refurbishment, recycling); Identify circular economy pathways (reuse, refurbishment, parts recovery, recycling) for EPI cold chain equipment currently used in Mozambique as well as establish linkages/ engagements with potential partners; Create and guide as an example the classification, Development of guidelines for classification, disposal and/ or reuse of CCE in the health sector; and development of recommendations including innovative solutions for refurbishment, reuse of parts or whole CCE equipment and establishment of partnerships with potential entities

desc: Country-Driven Adolescent Health Strategy Development, inc. Resource Landscape Analysis
full: UNICEF Côte d'Ivoire has expressed interest in receiving technical assistance from the Global Health Practice (MNCAH) Adolescent Health Team to develop a dedicated Adolescent Health Strategy that is action-oriented, country-driven and aligned with the Côte d'Ivoire Country Programme Document (CPD) 2026–2030. Building on nearly a decade of successful programming, strong government ownership and established multisectoral partnerships, the strategy will provide a clear roadmap to institutionalize, scale and sustain integrated adolescent health programming, while positioning adolescent health as a national development and investment priority. Recognizing the importance of balancing prevailing social norms with emerging adolescent health priorities, the strategy will adopt a holistic, life-course approach to adolescent health and well-being. It will prioritize interventions that respond to the evolving needs of adolescents, particularly younger adolescents (10–14 years) and girls, through age-appropriate, gender-responsive and culturally sensitive programming that strengthens adolescents' connection to health services, schools, communities and other support systems throughout adolescence. An integral component of the Adolescent Health Strategy will be a resource mobilization framework, aligned with the Country Office's broader resource mobilization efforts, to secure sustainable financing, strengthen strategic partnerships and support long-term programme scale- up. The framework will include: A comprehensive donor landscape analysis to identify strategic funding opportunities, emerging donors and alignment with donor priorities. A donor-ready capability statement highlighting UNICEF Côte d'Ivoire's comparative advantage, technical expertise, programmatic achievements and value proposition in adolescent health. A competitive landscape analysis to identify financing gaps, partnership opportunities and UNICEF's strategic positioning within the adolescent health financing landscape. A pipeline of three to five investment-ready concept notes, informed by the donor landscape analysis and aligned with donor priorities, funding appetite and the strategic priorities of the Côte d'Ivoire Country Programme Document (2026–2030). Together, these products will provide a practical roadmap for engaging development partners, diversifying financing sources and mobilizing sustainable investments to strengthen and institutionalize adolescent-responsive health systems. The Country Office envisions the strategy as a catalyst for consolidating existing gains, scaling proven innovations and positioning Côte d'Ivoire as a regional leader in integrated, adolescent-responsive programming and systems strengthening. Sustained investments and strategic partnerships will be essential to accelerate progress towards the ambitious adolescent health outcomes outlined in the 2026–2030 Country Programme, ensuring that no adolescent, particularly younger adolescents and girls, is left behind.

desc: Child-focused cash and social protection intervention within Palestine’s wider social protection framework
full: Dear Pamela, Ilija and Hashim, as part of UNICEF Palestine broader program review earlier this year, it was agreed to pivot away from MPCA as our main cash program and move towards a more UNICEF child-focused cash and social protection lens. This shift is a critical part of UNICEF State of Palestine’s evolving social protection framework and reflects the broader move from predominantly humanitarian cash assistance towards more transitional programming. The intention is to position the child cash grant as a core part of UNICEF’s program “offer” in Palestine: one that can respond to acute vulnerability while also contributing to longer-term system strengthening, national social protection reform, and more sustainable financing. The proposed child cash grant will aim to provide more targeted, regular and predictable cash support linked to services. It will be designed as part of an integrated and holistic package of support for the most vulnerable children and their families in both Gaza and the West Bank, with clear linkages to health and nutrition, child protection, education, WASH and other relevant services. In line with this direction, the Social Policy team is leading a technical review and is now designing the new program. A central part of this work will be to determine the most appropriate targeting approach and adequate and sustainable transfer value considering a wide range of financing sources. This will be critical design questions, as it will shape the caseload, service linkages, costing scenarios, implementation arrangements and overall positioning of the program. By introducing the Child Grant, we are aiming to a. Establish a clearer child-focused social protection intervention within Palestine’s wider social protection framework; b. Provide regular, predictable and more targeted support to vulnerable children and their families; c. Define the core design parameters of the grant, including target groups, transfer values, frequency, duration, caseload and geographic coverage; d. Develop realistic costing scenarios to support program planning, resource mobilization and scale-up; e. Strengthen the narrative around an integrated, child-focused package of services, helping UNICEF to access longer-term funding across humanitarian, transition, early recovery and development financing streams; and f. Integrate the program into the ongoing national social protection reform agenda to support sustainability, scalability and national ownership. UNICEF Palestine Social Policy is requesting the midterm technical assistance (recognizing L3) on refining the parameters of the child grant, support in it launch and promotion to secure financing. We would expect support from Social protection, Humanitarian Cash and PF4C in fragility CoE experts. best, Artur

Technical Support for the Conceptualization and Design of the Institute for the Rehabilitation and Reintegration of Juveniles in Conflict with the Law in Albania Background The Ministry of Justice of Albania is advancing plans to establish an Institute for the Rehabilitation and Reintegration of Juveniles in Conflict with the Law. (Please see the two documents attached to this request that represent the current vision of the Ministry of Justice regarding this institute). The proposed institution is intended to support the implementation of the Juvenile Criminal Justice Code and respond to the increasing use of diversion and alternative measures, with a focus on rehabilitation, reintegration, restorative justice, and the best interests of the child. UNICEF welcomes the Government's commitment to strengthening rehabilitation and reintegration mechanisms for children in conflict with the law. At the same time, it is important to ensure that the conceptualization and design of the Institute are fully aligned with international child rights standards and best practices, and that the model does not inadvertently create a new form of institutionalization or deprivation of liberty for children. Request We would like to request technical assistance from the Centre of Excellence to support the conceptualization and development of this new Institute. Specifically, the support would focus on: Reviewing the proposed institutional model against international standards and evidence-based practices in juvenile justice, child protection, rehabilitation and reintegration. Advising on how the Institute can function primarily as a rehabilitation, reintegration, capacity-building and coordination mechanism rather than as a residential or custodial institution. Identifying approaches that prioritise community-based and family-based services, including mechanisms for delivering rehabilitation and reintegration support through local systems and services whenever possible. Recommending governance, operational and service-delivery models that minimise the risk of institutionalisation and promote successful social reintegration of children. Providing guidance on multidisciplinary case management, psychosocial support, family strengthening, educational reintegration, vocational training and aftercare services. Sharing examples of successful international and regional models that have demonstrated positive outcomes for children in conflict with the law. Advising on the potential role of the Institute as a national centre for training, knowledge generation, research and quality assurance within the juvenile justice system. Supporting the development of a monitoring and evaluation framework, including indicators related to rehabilitation, reintegration, recidivism reduction, child well-being and social inclusion. Proposed Modality of Support Given the strategic importance of this initiative, UNICEF would welcome a combination of: Desk review of the available concept documents and supporting evidence - more information and documents may be shared, as needed); Virtual technical consultations with relevant national stakeholders; A possible in-country mission by a Centre of Excellence expert to engage with the Ministry of Justice, juvenile justice actors, child protection authorities and other stakeholders, and to provide tailored recommendations for the design and operationalisation of the Institute. Expected Outcome The support will contribute to the development of a child-centred, rights-based and evidence-informed model that strengthens rehabilitation and reintegration services for children in conflict with the law, promotes community-based alternatives, and aligns with international standards and best practices in juvenile justice.

desc: Gavi 6.0 Financial Analysis & NIS Costing tool TA – Haiti
full: Gavi 6.0 Financial Analysis & NIS Costing tool TA – Haiti UNICEF Haiti is seeking targeted technical assistance to support the financial analysis component of the Gavi 6.0 application, including envelope framing, prioritization (VPOP), and budget dialogue, as well as to respond to a specific Ministry of Health (MoH) request to strengthen national capacity on the use of the NIS costing tool. The request aligns with the national Gavi 6.0 roadmap, which identifies a gap in health economics expertise and the need for technical support to guide financial planning processes and facilitate decision-making. The TA will ensure that Haiti develops a robust, evidence-based, and realistic financial strategy for immunization, while also building sustainable national capacity to independently use and apply NIS costing tools for ongoing planning and budget discussions . 2. Objectives and Expected Outcomes Overall Objective Strengthen the financial analysis and cost-calculation components of Haiti’s Gavi 6.0 application, while developing sustainable national capacity in immunization cost calculation and financial planning using the NIS.costing tool Specific Objectives Technical Support for Gavi 6.0 Financial Analysis Support to NIS Costing Tool Use and Institutionalization Capacity Strengthening (Hands-on and Practical) Support to Data Consolidation, Analysis, and Interpretation Alignment with Gavi 6.0 Application Requirements 3. Expected Deliverables Deliver technical inputs and facilitation support for: Envelope framing discussions VPOP workshops and affordability analysis Finance sub-working group meetings Conduct hands-on training sessions on the NIS costing tool: Practical application using Haiti data Interpretation of results for decision-making Provide a complete and validated NIS costing tool: With documented assumptions Including basic scenario analysis (if feasible) Support to produce a financial analysis summary: Available resources vs. needs (gaps) Key trade-offs and prioritization recommendations Support data consolidation and validation for costing inputs Deliver clear inputs to the Gavi 6.0 application : Financial narrative contributions Costing tables and supporting evidence Share training materials and user guidance adapted to Haiti Prepare a short capacity strengthening summary: Key gaps identified Recommendations for continued support 4. Required Profile / Modality Health Economist / Immunization Financing Expert with: Experience in Gavi processes (Gavi 5.0/6.0, VPOP, or similar) Strong expertise in NIS costing tools or immunization costing methodologies Experience working with LMIC governments and partner coordination mechanisms Modality: Remote technical assistance (continuous support during application development) 6. Strategic Accelerators for Haiti Embedded TA in Key Decision Points “Learning by Doing” Capacity Strengthening Standardized Costing Templates + Country Adaptation Strong Link Between Costing and Prioritization Early Alignment with Ministry of Finance Integrated Data–Finance Approach 7. Key Risks to Address Lack of in-country health economist capacity. desc: VPOP Capacity Strengthening and Technical Support for Gavi 6.0 – Haiti
full: VPOP Capacity Strengthening and Technical Support for Gavi 6.0 – Haiti 1. Short Description of the Request UNICEF Haiti is seeking technical assistance to support the implementation of the Vaccine Prioritization and Optimization Process (VPOP) as part of the preparation of Haiti’s Gavi 6.0 application. The support will focus on strengthening the capacities of the National Immunization Technical Advisory Group (NITAG), the Expanded Programme on Immunization (EPI), the Technical Working Group (TWG), relevant Ministry of Health stakeholders, and UNICEF Haiti staff to effectively conduct the VPOP process, review and interpret evidence, assess vaccine affordability and impact, and generate evidence-based recommendations for decision-making. As the final Gavi 6.0 application package is expected to be finalized by November 2026, the VPOP exercise is a critical milestone during the first phase of application development. The requested assistance will ensure that Haiti conducts a robust, evidence-based, and country-owned prioritization process while simultaneously strengthening national and UNICEF capacities to sustain follow-up support throughout the remainder of the Gavi 6.0 application process. 2. Objectives General: Strengthen national capacity and technical expertise to successfully conduct the Vaccine Prioritization and Optimization Process (VPOP), generate evidence-based recommendations, and support the development of Haiti’s Gavi 6.0 application. Specific Objectives Provide technical support to the NITAG, EPI, Technical Working Group (TWG), and UNICEF Haiti throughout the planning and implementation of the Vaccine Prioritization and Optimization Process (VPOP). Strengthen the capacity of government counterparts, national technical committees, and UNICEF Haiti staff to apply VPOP methodologies, tools, and evidence-based decision-making approaches for vaccine prioritization. Support the review, analysis, and interpretation of epidemiological, programmatic, operational, and financial evidence required to inform vaccine prioritization and optimization decisions. Support to facilitate VPOP workshops, technical discussions, and consensus-building processes to support the identification and validation of priority vaccines and immunization investments. Strengthen UNICEF Haiti’s technical capacity to provide ongoing support and follow-up to national stakeholders throughout the Gavi 6.0 application development process and beyond. Strengthen linkages between vaccine prioritization, affordability analysis, health financing discussions, and programmatic planning to support realistic and sustainable investment decisions. 3. Expected Deliverables Support planning and implementation of VPOP workshops and technical meetings. Facilitate orientation and capacity-building sessions for NITAG, EPI, TWG, Ministry of Health counterparts, and UNICEF Haiti staff. Provide technical guidance on the application of VPOP methodology, tools, and prioritization frameworks. Support evidence reviews, analysis, synthesis, and presentation for VPOP discussions. Facilitate consensus-building discussions leading to validated vaccine prioritization recommendations. Support CO team to set of VPOP recommendations for integration into Haiti’s Gavi 6.0 application. Provide mentoring and on-the-job coaching to UNICEF Haiti and government counterparts to ensure continuity of support throughout the Gavi 6.0 application process. Develop practical guidance and reference materials that can be used by UNICEF Haiti and national stakeholders during subsequent stages of the application process. 4. Required Profile / Modality Profile Immunization expert with experience in: Gavi application processes, Gavi 5.0 and/or Gavi 6.0. Vaccine Prioritization and Optimization Process (VPOP). NITAG strengthening and evidence-to-recommendation frameworks. Immunization policy, strategy development, and vaccine introduction decision-making. Capacity strengthening and facilitation of multi-stakeholder technical discussions. Modality: Remote 6. Strategic Accelerators for Haiti Learning-by-Doing Capacity Strengthening Dual Capacity Transfer Early Engagement of NITAG and Technical Committees Integration with Financial Analysis Joint UNICEF–WHO/PAHO Technical Support Sustainability and Institutionalization 7. Key Risks to Address Tight timelines to generate recommendations that will inform the Gavi 6.0 application. Coordination challenges among NITAG, EPI, Ministry of Health, UNICEF, WHO/PAHO, and partners.

desc: Strategic Technical Assistance for School for Africa Reporting and Resource Mobilization – Burkina Faso
full: Strategic Technical Assistance for School for Africa Reporting and Resource Mobilization – Burkina Faso Background UNICEF Burkina Faso is currently implementing the School for Africa programme with the generous support of the Japan National Committee for UNICEF (Japanese NatCom) . The Country Office is finalizing the project reporting package, which is scheduled for submission within the coming week. At the same time, discussions are underway regarding a potential new phase of support to further advance education outcomes for children and adolescents in Burkina Faso. Given the strategic importance of this partnership and the opportunity to secure continued investment, the Country Office seeks technical assistance from the Centre of Excellence to strengthen both the quality of reporting and the positioning of future investment opportunities. Purpose of the Request To obtain expert support in maximizing the quality and strategic value of the current donor report and in preparing for engagement with the Japanese National Committee regarding a potential subsequent phase of the School for Africa programme. Requested Support The Country Office requests support in the following areas: Technical Review of the Donor Report Review the draft School for Africa progress/final report prior to submission. Assess the report's strategic narrative, evidence of results, presentation of impact, lessons learned, and alignment with donor expectations. Provide recommendations to strengthen the storytelling, results framing, and visibility of UNICEF's contribution and partnership value. Strategic Positioning for Future Funding Review the proposed concept and rationale for a potential next phase of the programme. Identify opportunities to strengthen the investment case based on demonstrated results, emerging needs, and alignment with donor priorities. Preparation for Donor Engagement Support the Country Office in preparing key messages, talking points, and advocacy arguments for discussions with the Japanese NatCom. Advise on how best to present achievements, future priorities, scalability, sustainability, and value for money. Provide strategic recommendations for structuring discussions aimed at securing continued support. Expected Deliverables Written comments and recommendations on the donor report. Strategic feedback on the proposed next phase of the School for Africa programme. A concise briefing package including key messages and talking points for engagement with the Japanese NatCom. Timeline Urgent priority: Review of donor report prior to submission within the next week. Support for donor engagement to follow immediately thereafter to inform ongoing discussions on future funding opportunities. Justification The School for Africa programme represents an important partnership and contributes significantly to improving equitable access to quality education for vulnerable children and adolescents in Burkina Faso. High-quality reporting and well-prepared donor engagement are critical to demonstrating results, maintaining donor confidence, and mobilizing resources for continued programme implementation and scale-up. The requested technical assistance would strengthen UNICEF Burkina Faso's capacity to effectively communicate achievements and position a compelling case for a new phase of investment under the School for Africa initiative.

desc: Vaccine Prioritization and Optimization Planning (VPOP) Workshop Facilitation and Technical Support for Cameroon
full: Demande d’assistance technique au Centre d’Excellence (CoE) Appui au 2ème Atelier National de Vaccine Prioritization and Optimization Planning (VPOP) Cameroun, 24–26 juillet 2026 Contexte Dans le cadre de la révision de sa Stratégie Nationale de Vaccination (SNV 2026–2030), le Cameroun a engagé le processus de Vaccine Prioritization and Optimization Planning (VPOP) , une approche développée par l'OMS, l'UNICEF et leurs partenaires afin d'appuyer les pays dans la priorisation, l'optimisation et le séquençage des investissements vaccinaux sur la base d'évidences scientifiques et des réalités de mise en œuvre. À l'issue de la session du GTCNV/NITAG tenue les 13 et 14 décembre 2025, sept vaccins ont été retenus comme prioritaires pour l'évaluation dans le cadre du processus VPOP : le vaccin contre l'hépatite B à la naissance, l'hexavalent, le vaccin multivalent contre la méningite, le vaccin oral contre le choléra, le vaccin contre la rage, le vaccin conjugué contre la typhoïde et le vaccin contre le virus respiratoire syncytial (VRS). Des groupes de travail ont été constitués pour conduire la collecte des données probantes nécessaires à l'analyse. Le processus VPOP se trouve actuellement dans sa Phase 2 : Évaluation et Optimisation , consacrée à la collecte, l'analyse et la synthèse des données probantes permettant d'élaborer des scénarios de priorisation et d'optimisation. Les travaux de collecte et de synthèse des preuves ont été réalisés et les principaux livrables ont été soumis au PEV et au GTCNV. Le deuxième atelier national VPOP, prévu du 24 au 26 juillet 2026 , a pour objectif de valider les résultats de cette phase, d'examiner les scénarios de priorisation et de séquençage, et de formuler des recommandations devant être intégrées dans les cadres stratégiques et budgétaires nationaux. Objet de la demande Le Programme Elargi de Vaccination (PEV) sollicite l'appui technique du Centre d'Excellence (CoE) pour accompagner l'organisation et la facilitation du deuxième atelier VPOP. Objectifs de l'assistance technique Le CoE apportera un appui technique pour : Faciliter l'examen des données probantes collectées pour les vaccins prioritaires ; Accompagner les discussions techniques autour des critères de priorisation et d'optimisation retenus ; Soutenir l'élaboration et la validation des scénarios de séquençage des introductions vaccinales ; Faciliter l'atteinte d'un consensus entre les parties prenantes ; Appuyer la formulation de recommandations stratégiques destinées au GTCNV, au PEV et au Ministère de la Santé Publique ; Contribuer à l'élaboration de la feuille de route VPOP devant alimenter la SNV 2026–2030 et les futures requêtes de financement. Résultats attendus À l'issue de l'atelier : Les résultats de la collecte et de la synthèse des preuves seront validés. Les options de priorisation et d'optimisation des vaccins seront examinées et classées. Des scénarios réalistes de séquençage des introductions vaccinales seront élaborés. Des recommandations consensuelles seront formulées par le GTCNV. Une feuille de route pour la mise en œuvre des décisions VPOP sera adoptée. Profil d'expertise souhaité Le CoE est invité à mobiliser une expertise dans les domaines suivants : Vaccination et introduction de nouveaux vaccins ; Économie de la santé et priorisation des investissements ; Analyse et synthèse des données probantes ; Planification stratégique des programmes de vaccination ; Facilitation de processus participatifs et de prise de décision fondée sur les évidences. Période de la mission Dates : 24–26 juillet 2026 Durée : 3 jours Lieu : Cameroun Justification L'accompagnement du CoE permettra de garantir un processus VPOP rigoureux, transparent et fondé sur les données probantes, en vue de soutenir les décisions nationales relatives à l'introduction, l'optimisation et le séquençage des vaccins prioritaires dans le contexte de la mise en œuvre de la Stratégie Nationale de Vaccination 2026–2030

desc: Support for Thematic PF4C/F4C Training Sessions for UNICEF Türkiye Staff
full: Support for Thematic PF4C/F4C Training Sessions for UNICEF Türkiye Staff Background: UNICEF Türkiye is planning a small set of thematic Public Finance for Children / Financing for Children training sessions for selected programme sections in June 2026. The aim is to strengthen internal capacity to better integrate PF4C/F4C approaches into sectoral programming, policy dialogue, investment cases, costing, resource mobilization and engagement with public finance processes. This request builds on the existing institutional contract between UNICEF and Genesis Analytics. The proposed support is directly aligned with the contract’s scope, particularly: evidence-based advocacy and policy dialogue; PF4C/PFM capacity building; child-responsive planning, budgeting and reporting; and financing strategies for child-related services and programmes. Objective : To provide UNICEF Türkiye staff with practical, sector-specific orientation on how PF4C/F4C concepts, tools and entry points can be applied in selected programme areas, with a focus on actionable use in ongoing and upcoming workstreams. Proposed scope of support : Support the preparation and delivery of up to three short online thematic training sessions, each lasting a maximum of half-a-day. The sessions would be tailored to the needs of UNICEF Türkiye sections, including: Child Protection and PF4C/F4C. Focus on financing child protection systems, costing service packages, linking evidence to budget dialogue, and strengthening arguments for adequate and sustainable financing. Education and PF4C/F4C : Focus on education financing, equity and efficiency in public spending, use of investment cases, and entry points for budget advocacy and sector financing dialogue. ECD/ECE and PF4C/F4C: Focus on financing early childhood development services, costing and investment case logic, cross-sectoral financing, and links to national and local planning and budgeting. 4. Key tasks - Hold a short preparatory discussion with UNICEF Türkiye to confirm the scope, audience and learning priorities. - Rapidly review relevant UNICEF PF4C/F4C thematic materials and Türkiye-specific priorities shared by the Country Office. - Prepare concise, practical session outlines and slide decks for each thematic session. - Deliver up to three online half-day trainings for UNICEF Türkiye staff. - Provide short follow-up notes summarizing key messages, practical recommendations 5. Expected deliverables: 1. Brief inception/preparation note or agreed session outline. 2. Three thematic PF4C/F4C training slide decks. 3. Delivery of up to three online half-day training sessions. 4. Short follow-up note summarizing key takeaways and suggested next steps. 6. Days/Duration: The assignment would require approximately 6–7 working days. - Preparation and coordination: 1 day - Tailoring materials and slide decks: 3 days - Delivery of three half-day online sessions: 1.5 days - Follow-up notes: 0.5–1 day 7. Timing: The delivery window is June 2026. 8. Coordination : UNICEF Türkiye will coordinate the internal audience, provide relevant country-specific materials, and agree on final thematic priorities with CoE/Global Practice.

desc: Support the Development of a Children and Youth Climate Declaration and Child-Centred Climate Policy Briefs for COP31 & ESA Regional Climate Advocacy
full: Technical Assistance to Support the Development of a Children and Youth Climate Declaration and Child-Centred Climate Policy Briefs for COP31 and East and Southern Africa Regional Climate Advocacy. UNICEF Uganda seeks technical assistance to support a child- and youth-centered participatory process evidence-based climate advocacy products in preparation for UNFCCC-COP31 and regional climate policy engagement. The ongoing nationwide consultations with children and young people, will synthesize priorities emerging from LCOY Uganda 2026 and related engagement processes, and produce a National Children and Youth Climate Declaration together with a strategic policy brief. The products will strengthen the integration of children's rights, climate resilience, and youth priorities into Uganda's national climate agenda, COP31 positioning, and East and Southern Africa Regional (ESAR) climate advocacy and pre-positioning processes. Objectives / Expected Results Objective 1 Support meaningful and representative participation of children and youth in climate policy processes through structured consultations and evidence generation. Expected Result A diverse and representative set of child and youth perspectives from Uganda and, where appropriate, ESAR countries, documented and synthesized into policy-relevant recommendations. Objective 2 Develop a high-quality Children and Youth Climate Declaration that articulates priorities, commitments and policy asks for national governments, regional bodies and UNFCCC- COP31 negotiators. Expected Result A consensus-based declaration endorsed through participatory processes and aligned with UNFCCC, ACE, child rights, adaptation, climate finance, loss and damage, and climate justice priorities. Objective 3 Produce evidence-based policy briefs that demonstrate the impacts of climate change on children and identify practical policy recommendations for national, regional and global action. Expected Result Policy briefs that strengthen child-responsive climate action and influence regional and global climate discussions ahead of COP31. Objective 4 Strengthen UNICEF's position as a leading advocate for child-responsive climate policy across Uganda and the ESAR region. Expected Result Children's priorities and evidence are reflected in regional climate advocacy products, strategic engagement opportunities, and COP31 preparations.

desc: Guidance and quality assurance on shock-responsive social protection (SRSP) framework
full: UNICEF Sri Lanka and WFP Sri Lanka are undertaking complementary household assessments during 2026 that present a unique opportunity to generate a joint analytical product on shock-responsive social protection (SRSP). WFP will conduct a nationwide household food security assessment covering approximately 15,000 households across 25 districts, while UNICEF will conduct a rapid telephone-based survey of approximately 1,500 households linked to the BRIGHT baseline, focusing on households with children. Although each agency will produce its own survey outputs, the proposed joint analysis will synthesize evidence from both datasets to assess the extent to which Sri Lanka's social protection system—particularly Aswesuma—is effectively reaching and protecting households affected by economic, climate, and other shocks. The Country Office seeks technical assistance to provide methodological guidance, technical review, and quality assurance of the analytical framework, findings, and policy recommendations, ensuring that the final product reflects global good practice in shock-responsive social protection and generates actionable recommendations for strengthening child-sensitive and adaptive social protection systems in Sri Lanka.

desc: Support CO-level engagement and strategic preparation for a new collaboration with the AI Hub for Social Protection
full: UNICEF Sri Lanka is seeking technical assistance to support country-level engagement and strategic preparation for a new collaboration with the AI Hub for Social Protection under the Digital Convergence Initiative. The partnership will begin with a two-day cross-sectoral workshop tentatively planned for October 2026, co-convened with government counterparts. The workshop will bring together senior policymakers and technical officials to explore the opportunities, risks, governance requirements, and practical applications of AI in social protection. Particular focus will be placed on two priority areas identified by the Government of Sri Lanka and partners: (i) vulnerability and targeting analytics, and (ii) climate- and shock-responsive social protection. The Country Office seeks technical assistance to support workshop preparation, strategic positioning, responsible AI governance discussions, use-case exploration, stakeholder engagement, and identification of a practical roadmap for follow-up collaboration that strengthens child-sensitive and shock-responsive social protection systems. This support will help ensure global good practice, alignment with UNICEF's digital transformation agenda, and a clear pathway toward responsible AI applications that improve outcomes for children. This request builds on the proposed workshop objectives of raising awareness, strengthening capacity on responsible AI, identifying priority use cases, and agreeing practical next steps for future collaboration.

The Government of Viet Nam is proposing amendment to the Penal Code, including decriminalization of the offence on organizing child marriage. UNICEF Viet Nam seeks urgent technical advice to assess the implication of this proposal from a child rights perspective and to inform UNICEF's contribution to a joint UN advocacy paper ahead of the National Assembly's consideration of the amendments. Objectives/expectations : Assess the potential implications of decriminalizing the offence on organizing child marriage, including its impact on prevention, deterrence, enforcement, and child protection outcomes. Provide comparative legal and policy analysis on how other countries address individuals who arrange, facilitate child marriage, including parents, guardians etc. Identify international standards, human rights obligations, and evidence- based practices relevant to criminalization and prevention of child marriage Advise on UNICE's position and advocacy messages regarding the proposed amendment. Support VCO in developing evidenc-based recommendations for engagement with government and for engagement and UN partners Expected Deliverable Rapid technical note (3–5 pages) analyzing the proposed decriminalization of the offence of organizing child marriage, including opportunities, risks, and implications for children's rights. Comparative review of selected countries' legal approaches to addressing the organization, facilitation, or promotion of child marriage. Compilation of relevant UNICEF and international guidance , including policy positions, advocacy materials, normative standards, and evidence on child marriage and legal responses. Key advocacy messages and recommendations for inclusion in UNICEF's and the joint UN position paper on the Penal Code amendments. Brief consultation/call with VCO to discuss findings and recommendations, if required.

Title Technical Assistance for the Development and Delivery of Parenting Education on Climate Change Short Description of the Request We would like to request technical assistance to strengthen our capacity to design, adapt and deliver parenting education interventions that address the impacts of climate change on children, families and communities. The support would help develop evidence-based training content, contextualized learning materials, and facilitation approaches that enable parents and caregivers to better protect, support and build resilience among children in the face of climate-related risks. Objectives / Expectations Strengthen technical content Support the integration of climate change, child rights, child well-being and resilience concepts into parenting education programmes. Ensure content is evidence-based and aligned with UNICEF guidance and global good practices. Develop and adapt training materials Review existing parenting education materials and identify opportunities to integrate climate-related topics. Develop or adapt training modules, facilitator guides and participant materials appropriate to the local context. Build facilitation capacity Strengthen the capacity of facilitators, trainers and implementing partners to deliver parenting education on climate change effectively. Promote participatory and community-based learning approaches. Support implementation planning Provide recommendations on roll-out strategies, monitoring indicators and quality assurance mechanisms. Identify opportunities for integration with community engagement, social behaviour change and child protection programming. Expected Deliverables Technical review of existing parenting education materials and curricula. Recommendations for integrating climate change and environmental resilience into parenting education programmes. Development/adaptation of training modules, facilitator guides and participant resources. Delivery of a Training of Trainers (ToT) session for facilitators and implementing partners. Practical implementation roadmap, including monitoring and learning indicators. Final technical report summarizing recommendations, tools and next steps. Relevant Global Practices to Involve Early Childhood Development (ECD) Social and Behaviour Change (SBC) Child Protection Education Climate, Energy, Environment and Disaster Risk Reduction (CEED) Adolescent Development and Participation (ADAP) (where youth engagement is relevant) Gender (to ensure inclusive and equitable approaches) Strategic Accelerators The following strategic accelerators could enhance impact and accelerate results for children: Integration of climate-resilient parenting messages into existing community platforms and services. Digital learning tools and blended training approaches for scale-up. Community engagement and social and behaviour change approaches to promote sustainable household practices. Cross-sectoral programming linking climate resilience, child protection, education and health. Partnerships with national climate institutions, academia and civil society organizations. Use of evidence, innovation and local knowledge to strengthen community resilience and child outcomes. Expected Result for Children Parents and caregivers will be better equipped to understand climate-related risks, support children's well-being, adopt resilient practices, and create safer and healthier environments for children affected by climate change.

desc: Vaccine Portfolio Optimization and Prioritization (VPOP) Technical Assistance for Cambodia’s National Immunization Strategy (2026–2030)

desc: UNICEF Gulf Area office is requesting support with addressing the below request from our key partner the Kingdom of Saudi Arabia on Early Learning.
full: Our partner, the Government of Saudi Arabia, is requesting expert insights on the impact of kindergarten enrollment and early childhood education and we are submitting this request to the COE. As part of their ongoing policy review, they are examining the relative contribution of kindergarten attendance to children's cognitive, social, and developmental outcomes. In particular, they are seeking to understand whether the greatest benefits are achieved through attendance in KG3 (age 5) alone, or whether earlier enrollment in KG1 (ages 3–4) and KG2 (ages 4–5) provides additional developmental and long-term educational advantages. We would be grateful to have a specialist assigned to prepare and share perspectives on the following questions in a joint online UNICEF-KSA session: 1. From a policy and measurement perspective, is it more appropriate to monitor kindergarten enrollment for children aged 3–5 or 4–5 ? What is considered international best practice? 2. Is attendance in KG3 (age 5) alone—or participation in kindergarten for at least 180 days prior to entry into primary school —generally sufficient to achieve the intended cognitive, developmental, and school-readiness outcomes? 3. What additional cognitive, developmental, or long-term educational benefits are associated with beginning kindergarten in KG1 (ages 3–4) rather than enrolling only in KG3 (age 5) ? 4. Are there international best practices or successful policy models that have demonstrated the greatest impact in maximizing the benefits of kindergarten participation across different age groups?

Short Description of Request Technical Assistance for Recruitment of Child Protection Officer (NO-A, Fixed-Term) – Access to Justice Unit The Türkiye Country Office Child Protection Section is seeking technical assistance to support the recruitment process for a Child Protection Officer (NO-A, Fixed-Term) who will lead the day-to-day implementation and coordination of the Access to Justice portfolio. The selected technical expert will support the end-to-end recruitment process to ensure the identification and selection of a highly qualified candidate with the required technical competencies in child justice, child protection systems strengthening, programme management, and partnership development. Objectives / Expectations The technical assistance will support the Child Protection Section in conducting a transparent, competitive, and competency-based recruitment process for the Child Protection Officer (NO-A) position. Specifically, the TA is expected to: Participate in interview preparation, including review and refinement of competency-based interview questions and technical exercises, if applicable. Serve as a technical panel member during interviews and contribute to the assessment of candidates. Provide technical analysis and recommendations on candidate suitability based on UNICEF competency requirements and programme needs. Support documentation of the recruitment process in line with UNICEF recruitment standards and procedures. Contribute to the identification of a candidate who demonstrates strong technical expertise, programme management skills, and stakeholder engagement capacities relevant to child justice and access to justice programming. Expected Deliverables Interview tools and assessment support Review and refine competency-based interview questions and technical assessment tools. Participate in interview panel discussions Final recruitment recommendation Support preparation of the final panel report and recommendation identifying the most suitable candidate for the position. Provide inputs to the final recruitment documentation and selection justification. Proposed Results Recruitment process completed in a timely and compliant manner. High-quality technical assessment of candidates. Selection of a qualified Child Protection Officer (NO-A) capable of managing UNICEF Türkiye's Access to Justice portfolio and supporting implementation of child justice-related interventions and partnerships. Enhanced objectivity and technical rigor throughout the recruitment process.

Objectives / Expectations The technical assistance is expected to support TCO in conducting a high-quality, transparent, and efficient recruitment process resulting in the selection of the best-qualified candidate. Specifically, the TA support will: Support the development and validation of technical assessment tools and competency-based interview questions. Participate in the technical screening and evaluation of applicants. Serve as technical reviewer/interview panel member during the recruitment process. Assess candidates' knowledge and experience in: Children on the Move programming; Child protection systems strengthening; Case management and referral mechanisms; Protection of unaccompanied and separated children; Migration governance and coordination; Humanitarian-development nexus programming; Partnership and stakeholder engagement. Provide technical recommendations on the suitability of candidates. Support documentation of recruitment outcomes and final recommendations in line with UNICEF recruitment standards. Expected Deliverables Deliverable 1: Recruitment Package Review Review Job Description and Vacancy Announcement. Recommend technical competencies, experience requirements, and assessment criteria specific to Children on the Move programming. Deliverable 2: Technical Assessment Framework Review technical written test and/or case study. Review competency-based interview questions. Establish evaluation and scoring criteria for candidate assessment. Deliverable 3: Interview Panel Participation Participate in technical interviews. Assess candidates against UNICEF competencies and Children on the Move technical requirements. Complete interview scoring and assessment documentation. Deliverable 4: Final Technical Recommendation Prepare a comparative technical assessment of shortlisted candidates. Identify strengths, risks, and overall suitability of candidates. Support final selection recommendation and recruitment documentation. Expected Results A transparent, efficient, and technically rigorous recruitment process. Timely recruitment of a highly qualified Children on the Move Officer (NOB). Strengthened UNICEF Türkiye capacity to deliver the Children on the Move agenda under the 2026–2030 Country Programme. Enhanced programme oversight, coordination, monitoring, and implementation support for refugee and migrant children.

It will also support UNICEF in identifying strategic opportunities to strengthen integration across sectors and delivery platforms, with particular attention to SRHR, HIV, GBV and mental health as well as nutrition, PHC, SBC, digital solutions, education, protection, and social protection.
