Assigned to : Maria Osbeck Request for Technical Support on Integration of Child- and Youth-Sensitive Priorities into NDC 3.0 Processes (Kazakhstan, Kyrgyzstan, Tajikistan, Turkmenistan, Uzbekistan) Under the Climate BMI, UNICEF supported the integration of child- and youth-sensitive priorities into the third generation of nationally determined contributions (NDC 3.0) across the five Central Asian countries. The work aimed to strengthen recognition of children and young people as a climate-vulnerable group and to position child-responsive investments within national climate commitments and implementation frameworks. Technical support included policy analysis, stakeholder consultations, development of child-sensitive narrative and sectoral content, identification and costing of priority investments, and engagement with national NDC drafting processes. Across the region, UNICEF-supported inputs resulted in the inclusion of child- and youth-responsive climate actions spanning education, health, WASH, social protection, youth engagement, climate-resilient infrastructure, and disaster risk reduction. The process also generated a regional pipeline of child-sensitive climate investment opportunities estimated at approximately USD 6.9 billion across the five countries. As of June 2026, Kazakhstan, Kyrgyzstan, and Uzbekistan have formally submitted updated NDCs to the UNFCCC with UNICEF-supported child-sensitive provisions reflected in the final documents. Drafting and/or finalization processes in Tajikistan and Turkmenistan remain ongoing, with UNICEF continuing to provide technical support as requested by national counterparts and country offices. Key considerations for successor UNICEF's comparative advantage established through the NDC process should be leveraged in subsequent climate policy engagements, including NAPs, Long-Term Strategies (LTS), sectoral plans, and climate finance proposals. Relationships established with national climate and sector ministries through the NDC process represent an important institutional asset and should be maintained where possible. International Consultant’s (Ivan Filiutsich) is valid till 30 September 2026 . Key Documents / Links NDC 3.0 Regional Folder International Consultant Deliverables SOP on NDC 3.0 Costing + Annexes Methodological Approach and Tools for Costed Investments in Child-Sensitive NDCs 3.0 Country NDCs (Published and Draft) Strategy for Leveraging Public Financing

desc: Support on Climate Resilient Schools and Child-Sensitive Infrastructure Programming
full: Assign to: Maria Osbeck, Climate CoE Request for Technical Support on Climate Resilient Schools and Child-Sensitive Infrastructure Programming Under the Climate BMI, UNICEF engaged an international consultant to develop the Climate Resilient Infrastructure workstream, focusing on energy efficiency, indoor air quality (IAQ), climate resilience, and sustainable infrastructure solutions for schools and health facilities across Central Asia. The workstream sought to define UNICEF's value proposition on climate-resilient facilities and establish a foundation for future infrastructure investments and climate finance mobilisation . Key achievements include the development of a regional framing document on Climate Resilient Schools, standardized energy and IAQ audit methodologies, technical guidance on infrastructure resilience and sustainability, quality assurance support for procurement and technical assessment processes, and development of advocacy and investment materials. The consultant also provided technical support to Country Offices undertaking energy and IAQ audits and related infrastructure assessments. Most core deliverables have been completed, with a limited number of technical assistance activities and administrative actions remaining . Key Considerations for Successor This is one of the most mature BMI workstreams, with most technical products already completed and available for immediate use by Country Offices. The standardized audit methodology represents an important regional public good and was used to support energy and IAQ assessments across multiple countries. The advocacy package, investment case, and technical guidance provide a strong foundation for future engagement with development banks, climate funds, and infrastructure financing partners. desc: Support on Development of the Regional Green School Platform (RGSP) Framework and Regional Cooperation Mechanism
full: Assign to: Maria Osbeck, Climate CoE Request for Technical Support on Development of the Regional Green School Platform (RGSP) Framework and Regional Cooperation Mechanism The Regional Green School Platform (RGSP) was developed under the Climate BMI as a regional mechanism to support climate-resilient, low-carbon, and child- centred education infrastructure and systems across Central Asia. The platform emerged from consultations with Country Offices, government counterparts, technical experts, and development partners, and was further advanced through preparations for the Regional Ecological Summit (RES). The RGSP is envisioned as a regional coordination and fund mobilisation mechanism that supports participating countries through development of common standards, technical guidance, knowledge exchange, project preparation, and resource mobilisation . During the reporting period, UNICEF coordinated the development of the RGSP concept, governance proposals, implementation roadmap, partnership outreach materials, and investment rationale. The platform received formal endorsement from Ministries of Education and Ministries of Environment/Ecology from the five Central Asian countries during the High-Level Session on Green Schools at RES in April 2026. The RGSP was subsequently reflected in the RES Declaration, providing a strong political foundation for future regional collaboration. A draft 6– 12 month operationalisation roadmap (action plan), 10-year Roadmap and 4-page Concept Note has been developed and circulated with COs for review. Initial engagement has also been initiated with potential financing and technical partners, including the Islamic Development Bank, GPE and other development partners. Important consideration for Successor The RGSP represents the most significant strategic outcome of the Climate BMI and is currently the primary vehicle through which BMI-generated knowledge products and partnerships can be translated into longer-term regional programming and investment. desc: Behavioural science prototyping for Continuity Counts Immunization Initiative
full: Technical Assistance Request Behavioural Science Prototype Design and Pilot – Continuity Counts Immunization Initiative, Afghanistan TA Title Behavioural Science Technical Assistance for Prototype Design, Pilot Testing and Learning Generation under the DEPTHS Approach for Continuity Counts Strategic Priority Immunization | Zero-dose Reduction | Immunization Continuity | Behavioural Science Innovation Background UNICEF Afghanistan SBC, in collaboration with Health and Polio programmes, has developed the Continuity Counts behavioural science initiative to address immunization dropout and improve completion of the vaccination schedule among children in high-risk districts. The initiative is grounded in UNICEF's DEPTHS behavioural science framework and has completed the initial evidence-generation phases, including problem definition and behavioural diagnosis. Findings indicate that immunization dropout is not solely a matter of acceptance; it is influenced by continuity barriers related to reminders, follow-up, trust, caregiver decision-making, mobility, competing priorities and service interactions. The next phase requires specialized behavioural science expertise to support the development, testing and refinement of behaviourally informed intervention prototypes prior to potential scale-up. The pilot is planned in two integrated service delivery high-risk districts in Hilmund and Kandahar province of South Region, where different behavioural and contextual drivers of immunization continuity can be assessed. Problem Statement Behavioural diagnosis findings have identified critical barriers affecting caregivers' ability to continue and complete the immunization journey after the first contact with services. However, the Afghanistan Country Office does not currently have dedicated in-country behavioural science expertise to translate findings into rigorously designed and tested interventions. The SBC team does have two newly recruitde staff- one NOC SBC Specialist and one IUNV- dedicated to Behavioural evidence portfolio. They require technical mentoring. However, the two staff will do the heavy lifting for field insights, stakeholders consultation, piloting etc. Technical assistance is therefore requested to support: Development of behaviourally informed intervention prototypes. Co-design workshops with programme teams and stakeholders. Development of behavioural hypotheses and testing frameworks. Pilot implementation design and learning systems. Evaluation of feasibility, acceptability and effectiveness of tested approaches. Recommendations for scale-up through routine immunization and community engagement systems. Objective To support UNICEF Afghanistan in designing, prototyping, piloting and evaluating behavioural interventions that strengthen immunization continuity and reduce dropout using the Prototype & Design and Test Hypotheses phases of the DEPTHS framework. Scope of Work 1. Prototype & Design Phase The Behavioural Science Specialist will: Review behavioural diagnosis findings and supporting evidence. Facilitate structured ideation and co-design sessions using DEPTHS tools. Translate behavioural barriers and enablers into actionable intervention concepts. Prioritize intervention options based on potential impact, feasibility, scalability and ethics. Develop low- and medium-fidelity prototypes for testing. Prepare theories of change and behavioural hypothesis statements. Develop a prototype testing framework and measurement plan. [DEPTHS Field Guide | PDF] Potential prototype areas may include: Caregiver reminder and continuity-support mechanisms. Trusted messenger approaches. Community-based follow-up systems. Behavioural nudges and planning supports. Adaptive communication and engagement approaches. Service interaction improvements that strengthen continuity across immunization visits. 2. Pilot Testing (Test Hypotheses Phase) The Specialist will: Design pilot methodology and implementation protocol. Define behavioural and operational indicators. Establish learning questions and success measures. Support implementation of pilot interventions within selected districts. Support rapid learning and adaptation processes. Facilitate analysis of pilot findings and behavioural outcomes. Generate recommendations for refinement and future scale-up. Expected Deliverables Workplan. Prototype design workshop package and facilitation materials. Behavioural intervention prototypes. Behavioural hypothesis matrix and theory of change. Pilot implementation protocol. Monitoring and learning framework. Pilot findings report including: Prototype performance User feedback synthesis Feasibility assessment Behavioural outcome findings Recommendations for adaptation and scale-up Final presentation and dissemination session for UNICEF Afghanistan and partners. Expected Results By the completion of the TA, UNICEF Afghanistan will have: Behaviourally informed intervention prototypes ready for implementation. Evidence on what works to improve immunization continuity. Practical lessons on reducing missed children and dropout. A tested behavioural science model that can inform future immunization programming. Scale-ready recommendations for integration within routine immunization systems and community engagement platforms. Why this TA is Strategic The Continuity Counts initiative is positioned as a proof-of-concept for applying behavioural science to immunization continuity challenges in Afghanistan. It will demonstrate how behavioural evidence can be translated into action through the full DEPTHS pathway—from diagnosis to testing and learning—while generating a scalable model for evidence-driven SBC programming. [Stronger P...Resources | SharePoint] Requested Expertise Applied Behavioural Scientist with demonstrated experience using UNICEF's DEPTHS framework or comparable behavioural design methodologies. Experience designing and testing health-related behavioural interventions. Expertise in prototype development, field experimentation and adaptive learning. Experience supporting UNICEF, UN agencies or development programmes in low-resource or humanitarian contexts. This version is structured to align with the June 2026 guidance on articulating high-quality SBC Technical Assistance requests for the CoE/REACH platform.

desc: Jordan crossborder CM for Syrian returnees
full: The JCO Child Protection programme needs support for the establishment and technical review of cross-border child protection case management mechanisms for refugee children and families departing host countries and returning to Syria under the Prospects of Durable Solutions programme. The support would provide technical guidance on operationalizing safe, ethical, and child-centred cross-border case management pathways, ensuring continuity of care, information sharing, referral systems, data protection, and interagency coordination across countries of asylum and Syria. The support should build on global child protection standards, UNICEF guidance, and emerging regional practices to strengthen durable solutions programming and protection outcomes for children. Expectation of TA from the CoE would be a regionally endorsed and operational cross-border child protection case management mechanism that ensures continuity of care, safe case transfer, and sustained protection support for refugee children and families returning to Syria, contributing to durable solutions and improved child protection outcomes across the return pathway.

Good morning, Alex and team, from Sweet Salone. As our office explores opportunities to advance disability inclusion in health, education, and innovation, we kindly request your support with the following areas: Early identification and screening of young children with disabilities: Could you kindly share any presentations, short videos, photographs, tools, or assistive devices that demonstrate approaches and best practices for the early identification and screening of children with disabilities? Disability inclusion in Community Health Worker training: Do you have any training materials, guidance notes, or curricula on disability inclusion that are suitable for use in training Community Health Workers? We would greatly appreciate any resources you can share. Integration of disability content into health worker training: We are interested in integrating disability-related modules into pre-service and in-service training for health workers. Could you share examples of curricula, modules, or lessons learned from similar initiatives? Integration of disability-inclusive curricula into teacher and health worker training institutions: We are exploring opportunities to integrate the Disability-Inclusive Child Protection Curriculum for Social Work or suitable parts of it into teacher training and health worker education programmes. Do you have disability inclusion training materials for teachers, nurses, or other health professionals that we could review and compare? We would also welcome any advice, practical experiences, or recommendations from similar efforts. Disability Inclusion in Innovation Work Practical experiences in disability-inclusive innovation: Could you share examples of innovative approaches, projects, or lessons learned in advancing disability inclusion through innovation? Sign language applications: UNICEF Innovation team has developed a sign-language application, Leh Wi Tok , for persons with hearing impairments using American Sign Language. Are there similar examples, resources, or lessons learned from the development and deployment of such digital accessibility solutions that you could share? Or may be we share the App for review? LEGO Braille Bricks programming: Do you have any experience, guidance, or examples of programmes utilizing LEGO Braille Bricks to support literacy, learning, and inclusion for children with visual impairments? Accessible Digital Learning Hubs: We are exploring ways to make university-based Digital Learning Hubs more disability-inclusive, including piloting a “Digital Learning Hub-in-a-Bag” model to improve access for persons with disabilities in communities. Could you kindly consult the Innovation Team or country offices with experience in this area and share relevant guidance, resources, or lessons learned on the design and implementation of similar initiatives, particularly for persons with visual impairments? We would especially appreciate information on effective accessibility features, disability inclusive education and awareness raising content, assistive technologies, and inclusive design approaches.

desc: Beneficiary Data Management Support (Online Gap Filling) for urgent BRS Programme Cash Assistance Payment
full: As discussed, Miye has been supporting Waleed while we work to recruit a National Officer position. The recruitment process is taking longer than anticipated, although we remain hopeful that the position will be filled soon. I greatly appreciate the precious support Miye has already provided. At present, his support is particularly critical, as Waleed had to leave unexpectedly due to a family emergency. As agreed, Miye can begin providing remote support. To facilitate this, I have requested the support of the Social Policy Officer from the Tombouctou Field Office, who will be in Bamako next week. He has worked closely with Waleed and has completed the HOPE training; with my guidance, he will be well positioned to collaborate effectively with Miye. As mentioned, we urgently need to accelerate three delayed payment cycles covering approximately 9,000 beneficiaries: January–February 2026 March–April 2026 May–June 2026 We also need to prepare for the launch of the 4th payment cycle (July–August 2026), which is scheduled for August. At the moment, Miye and I are reviewing and validating the beneficiary lists, as we have identified some inconsistencies in the data. Once the lists are stabilized and finalized, we will proceed with launching the first payment cycle. Below is an overview of the support we expect from Miye: Support beneficiary data management processes in HOPE, including registration, validation, deduplication, data cleaning, and maintenance of beneficiary records to ensure readiness for cash transfers. Provide technical support for beneficiary data uploads, payment plan preparation, reconciliation processes, and the resolution of data quality issues that could delay cash delivery. Generate reports from HOPE to support monitoring of payment cycles, beneficiary coverage, transfer status, and the identification of operational bottlenecks. Support troubleshooting during payment implementation, including the rapid review and correction of rejected records, payment exceptions, and beneficiary verification issues. Provide on-the-job coaching and capacity building to the Social Policy Officer on HOPE workflows, beneficiary data management standards, and cash transfer processes. Expected peak workload period - The highest workload is expected during July and August, as we work to implement the three delayed payment cycles while simultaneously preparing the July–August 2026 payment cycle. During this period, beneficiary lists will need to be finalized, validated, and uploaded within very tight operational deadlines. Significant support will also be required immediately after payment execution for reconciliation, issue resolution, and beneficiary feedback management.

desc: Human-Centered Design Evidence Generation, Scientific Publication and Knowledge Translation Support for Ethiopia
full: UNICEF Ethiopia would like to request technical assistance to support the development, strengthening, and publication of a series of manuscripts documenting lessons and evidence from Human-Centered Design applications in routine immunization, in HPV+ initiative among out-of-schoolgirls, and Mpox RCCE. The support will include technical guidance on manuscript development, strengthening methodological rigor where needed, identifying appropriate publication avenues, providing peer-review readiness support, and facilitating the overall publication process. The objective is to generate high-quality, publishable evidence that contributes to global learning on HCD, SBC, immunization, HPV, RCCE, implementation research, and health systems strengthening. Objectives / Expectations Objective 1: Strengthen the scientific quality and publishability of the manuscripts Expected Results Manuscripts meet the standards of peer-reviewed scientific journals. Methods, analysis, and reporting are strengthened and aligned with relevant reporting guidelines. Clear articulation of contributions to evidence and practice. Possible Deliverables Technical support on development and review of all five manuscripts. Written recommendations to strengthen methodology, analysis, and interpretation. Guidance on appropriate reporting standards depending on manuscript type. Editorial review and scientific writing support. Peer-review readiness assessment for each manuscript. Objective 2: Support manuscript development and completion Expected Results Developed manuscripts, reviewed and are finalized and ready for submission. Findings are translated into compelling evidence products relevant to global and country audiences. Possible Deliverables Detailed manuscript outlines and publication plans for each paper. Technical writing and co-author support. Review and refinement of abstracts, tables, figures, and discussion sections. Development of key messages and implications for policy and programming. Finalized submission-ready manuscripts. Objective 3: Identify appropriate publication and dissemination pathways Expected Results Publication opportunities are identified based on manuscript scope and audience. A publication strategy is developed to maximize visibility and uptake of findings. Possible Deliverables Journal mapping and publication landscape analysis. Recommendations for target journals and publication sequencing. Submission strategy including timelines and requirements. Dissemination plan including webinars, conference presentations, and knowledge products. Potential Publication Venues BMJ Global Health BMC Public Health Implementation Science Communications Global Health: Science and Practice (GHSP) Journal of Health Communication Frontiers in Public Health PLOS Global Public Health Human-Centered Design-focused implementation and innovation journals Objective 4: Strengthen evidence generation and learning on Human-Centered Design for UNICEF programming Expected Results Evidence contributes to global learning on HCD application in public health, immunization, and RCCE. Lessons are documented for replication and scale-up. Possible Deliverables Cross-manuscript synthesis highlighting key lessons and implications. Knowledge brief(s) summarizing evidence for policymakers and practitioners. Recommendations for scaling HCD-informed approaches within health systems and community engagement programming. Strategic learning agenda identifying future research priorities. Proposed Manuscripts and Expected Support Areas Applying Human-Centered Design to Routine Immunization: From Rapid Inquiry to Co-Creating Community Solutions (ready for write up) Implementation Research on the Application of Human-Centered Design for Routine Immunization in Ethiopia (ready for write up) Using Human-Centered Design for Mpox RCCE Among Marginalized Communities (ready for write up) Applying Human-Centered Design to Improve HPV Vaccination Uptake Among Out-of-School Girls in Afar Region: From Rapid Inquiry to Co-Creating Community Solutions (ready for write up) Cost-Effectiveness Analysis of Human-Centered Design-Informed Routine Immunization Interventions (in progress) Global Practices and Teams to Involve Primary Leads: SBC for Immunization team, Immunization Team, SBC M&E team Additional Contributors: RCCE and Health Emergencies Team for Mpox publication, Implementation Research Expert for implementation research publication, Health Economics Expert for the cost-effectiveness manuscript, and Innovation/Human-Centered Design Team. Strategic Accelerators The following UNICEF Strategic Plan accelerators could help maximize impact and accelerate results for children: 1. Data, Evidence and Knowledge Generate actionable evidence on HCD approaches. Inform policy, programming, and scaling decisions. Strengthen global evidence for community-centered approaches to immunization and RCCE. 2. Innovation Document and validate HCD as an innovative approach for improving service uptake and community engagement. Generate lessons for adaptation across contexts. 3. Community Engagement and SBC Strengthen community ownership and demand for essential services. Improve effectiveness of immunization and RCCE interventions. 4. Systems Strengthening Support integration of HCD approaches into existing health systems. Enhance sustainability and institutionalization of interventions. 5. Partnerships and Knowledge Sharing Promote learning across countries and regions. Facilitate dissemination through academic, practitioner, and policy networks. This technical assistance request seeks to mobilize high-level technical support for UNICEF China to assist the Government of China (specifically the China Disabled Persons' Federation and partner ministries) in designing, optimizing, and implementing the 3rd National Sample Survey of Persons with Disabilities (June 2026 – December 2028). Targeting a sample of 2.8 million people, this survey is a critical national exercise. UNICEF's intervention will focus on aligning the survey methodologies with international benchmarks, introducing the Washington Group child questionnaires, transitioning from a medical to a social model of assessment, and building local capacity to ensure high-quality, inclusive data that will ultimately refine policy interventions for children with disabilities. Objectives • Objective 1: International Alignment & Methodology Optimization To integrate international standards, specifically the Washington Group (WG) on Disability Statistics, into the national survey design, ensuring age-specific questionnaires (including the critical 0–2 age gap) are scientifically sound and localized. • Objective 2: Shift to a Social Model of Assessment To transition the national assessment framework from a purely medical, doctor-led model to a social support model that identifies functional barriers, environmental obstacles, and the core needs of children, distinguishing permanent disabilities from temporary developmental delays. • Objective 3: Technical Exchange & Capacity Building To establish a robust technical dialogue mechanism between national authorities and global experts, and to build the capacity of frontline enumerators and medical professionals for standardized, objective assessments. Potential asks/expectations from China Gov: 1. Technical Guidance Note on WG Localization: A comprehensive package detailing the adaptation of WG child questionnaires (0-2, 2-6, 7+ age groups), incorporating global case studies on localization, questionnaire simplification, and alignment with international statistical benchmarks. 2. Draft Screening Questionnaires & Standards (0-6 Years): Optimized, simplified screening tools that bridge the 0–2 age gap and establish clear, standardized developmental assessment criteria for early childhood. 3. Expert Consultation & Bilateral Seminars: A structured series of closed-door technical seminars and written peer-review mechanisms engaging global disability experts and Chinese government officials (CDPF: China Disabled Persons' Federation; NHC: National Health Commission; MCA: Ministry of Civil Affairs; NBS: National Bureau of Statistics). 4. Operational Training Toolkit & Capacity Building: A localized training curriculum and guidelines for frontline enumerators and medical professionals to standardize disability assessment, minimize regional variance, and accurately implement the social model of disability in the field. Global Practices to Involve: Direct engagement with the experts on WG questionnaires to review customized questionnaires and ensure alignment with global SDG reporting. To leverage global templates on child-functioning modules and cross-country validation experiences. To wxpolre integration of the International Classification of Functioning, Disability and Health standards, particularly for the 0-6 age group.

desc: SBC and Gender Immunization Intelligence System Strengthening Support for Somalia
full: Context / Challenge: Somalia currently lacks a harmonized system for routinely collecting, analysing and using SBC, demand-generation and gender-related immunization data. Indicators and tools used by different partners are fragmented, limiting the ability of the FMoH and EPI programme to assess behavioural and gender barriers, monitor intervention results and use evidence for timely programme adjustments. The ongoing development of the National Immunization Strategy and Gavi 6.0 presents an important opportunity to institutionalize an integrated, government-led SBC and Gender Immunization Intelligence approach within existing coordination and health information systems. Technical Assistance Requested: Technical assistance is requested from the Centre of Excellence to support the FMoH and partners to operationalize the integrated approach. This would include support to establish or strengthen the governance mechanism, conduct a country readiness assessment, facilitate stakeholder consultations, prioritize context-appropriate SBC and gender indicators, adapt the DHIS2 demand module, develop a phased implementation roadmap, and strengthen capacity for data collection, analysis, review and use for decision-making. Expected Output / Milestone: A validated country readiness assessment; an agreed governance and coordination mechanism; a prioritized set of context-appropriate SBC and gender immunization indicators; and a phased implementation roadmap outlining roles, timelines, resource requirements, capacity-building needs and steps for integration into DHIS2 and existing EPI review processes. Expected Outcome: Somalia will have a government-led, harmonized and sustainable system for routinely collecting, analysing and using SBC and gender immunization data. This will strengthen evidence-based planning, improve identification of behavioural and gender-related barriers, reduce fragmented partner reporting, and enable timely programme adjustments to improve immunization demand, equity and uptake.

Title: Technical assistance for the organisation and facilitation of Disability Inclusion Frontline Worker Training. Short Description: Technical assistance is requested to support the organisation, coordination, and facilitation of a Disability Inclusion Frontline Worker Training. The support will ensure effective planning, participant engagement, accessible and inclusive delivery and facilitation of learning sessio ns. The training aims to strengthen frontline workers' knowledge, attitudes, and practical skills to identify and address barriers faced by persons with disabilities and to promote disability-inclusive service delivery and programming. Objectives / Expectations Objective 1: Ensure Effective Planning and Organisation of the Training Expectations: Develop a detailed training plan and implementation timeline. Coordinate with relevant stakeholders and facilitators. Ensure training materials and processes are disability-inclusive and accessible. Objective 2: Facilitate High-Quality, Participatory Learning Expectations: Facilitate training sessions using adult learning methodologies. Promote active participation, discussion, and practical application of disability inclusion concepts. Adapt facilitation approaches to participants' needs and learning styles. Create a safe and inclusive learning environment that encourages reflection and peer learning. Objective 3: Strengthen Frontline Workers' Capacity on Disability Inclusion Expectations: Increase participants' understanding of disability inclusion principles and rights-based approaches. Enhance practical skills to identify barriers, make reasonable accommodations, and engage persons with disabilities effectively. Support participants in applying disability-inclusive practices within their daily work. Objective 4: Capture Learning and Provide Recommendations Expectations: Document key discussions, lessons learned, and agreed actions. Assess participant satisfaction and training effectiveness. Provide recommendations for future capacity-building efforts and follow-up actions. Expected Deliverables Deliverable 1: Training Preparation Detailed workplan and training agenda. Accessibility and inclusion checklist. Coordination with trainers, speakers, and relevant stakeholders. Deliverable 2: Training Facilitation Facilitation of the Disability Inclusion Frontline Worker Training. Delivery of interactive exercises, group work, and discussions. Adaptation of facilitation methods to ensure meaningful participation of all participants. Deliverable 3: Training Materials Review, adaptation, and/or preparation of facilitator guides, presentations, handouts, and supporting materials. Accessible versions of training materials, where required. Deliverable 4: Training Evaluation and Documentation Pre- and post-training assessment tools (if applicable). Consolidated participant feedback and evaluation results. Success Indicators Training delivered according to the agreed agenda and timeline. Accessibility considerations integrated into planning and facilitation. Participants demonstrate increased knowledge and confidence in applying disability-inclusive approaches. Positive participant satisfaction ratings.

desc: Technical assistance to support a joint country mission in reviewing, monitoring, and strengthening the quality of nationwide maternal nutrition services.
full: Technical Assistance through Joint Country Support Mission to Review, Monitor and Strengthen the Quality of Nationwide Scale-Up of Maternal Nutrition Services Including MMS under the GoB-World Bank-UNICEF Child Nutrition Fund (CNF) Match Financing Initiative Provide technical assistance through an in-country mission by the Centre of Excellence (CoE), and CNF Headquarters to review, monitor and assess the quality, coverage, implementation fidelity, and early results of the nationwide scale-up of quality maternal nutrition services, including Multiple Micronutrient Supplementation (MMS), under the Government of Bangladesh-World Bank-UNICEF Child Nutrition Fund (CNF) match financing mechanism. The mission will include field visits to selected implementation districts, consultations with government counterparts and development partners, assessment of service delivery platforms and monitoring systems, and identification of strategic opportunities to accelerate impact for women, newborns and children. The mission will generate actionable recommendations to strengthen implementation quality, scale-up readiness, sustainability and learning for global replication. Objectives / Expectations Objective 1: Assess Quality of Implementation Review the extent to which quality maternal nutrition interventions, including MMS, are being integrated and delivered according to national guidelines and implementation plans across different levels of the health system through stakeholders consultation and joint field visits. Objective 2: Review Readiness and Performance of National Scale-Up Assess the progress, enabling factors and bottlenecks associated with the nationwide scale-up supported through the GoB-World Bank-CNF match financing mechanism, with particular focus on governance, financing, supplies, service delivery and monitoring arrangements. Objective 3: Review Monitoring and Digital Systems Assess the availability, quality and use of e monitoring and digital information systems for tracking maternal nutrition services, MMS coverage, adherence tracking and supply chain performance. Objective 4: Identify Opportunities for Acceleration Identify strategic innovations, partnerships, and systems-strengthening actions that could accelerate quality maternal nutrition services and improve birth outcomes.

UNICEF Italy, in partnership with the Ministry of Justice, is implementing activities under the AMIF Fund PROTECT+ project aimed at strengthening protection and access to services for unaccompanied and vulnerable children. Within this framework, a specific workstream foresees the development of a “Documento di mappatura e analisi delle buone pratiche” through the collection, analysis and dissemination of practices and operational tools used within the juvenile justice system, with a particular focus on children's participation, the right to be heard, child hearings and child-friendly justice approaches. Technical assistance is requested to provide methodological guidance and technical review of this exercise, ensuring that the mapping framework, selection criteria and analytical approach are aligned with international standards, including the CRC, UNICEF's Justice for Children programming framework and relevant European child-friendly justice standards. The assistance should also help identify relevant international evidence, tools and comparable experiences that can strengthen the quality and relevance of the final analysis. The expected results are directly linked to the PROTECT+ project deliverables and include: (i) a strengthened methodology for the mapping exercise; (ii) the identification and analysis of promising practices and operational tools used by Juvenile Courts and justice actors; (iii) technical review and quality assurance of the draft mapping and analysis document; and (iv) production of a robust final knowledge product that can support dissemination seminars, policy dialogue and capacity building activities envisaged under the project. The support should ultimately contribute to the successful delivery of the project's key deliverable, namely the national mapping and analysis of good practices. The request would benefit from the involvement of the Child Protection Programme Group (Justice for Children), UNICEF Innocenti and ECARO Child Protection colleagues. Strategic accelerators include evidence generation, learning and knowledge management, child participation, cross-country exchange and systems strengthening. Together, these inputs will support the Ministry of Justice and UNICEF in generating actionable recommendations and scalable models that can strengthen child-friendly justice practices nationally and contribute to broader European learning and reform processes.

full: UNICEF Ecuador supported the integration of an intergenerational and child-sensitive approach during Ecuador’s most recent NDC update process. Building on this work, the Ministry of Environment, Water and Ecological Transition has requested UNICEF’s technical support for the development and update of broader climate policy instruments, including the National Climate Change Strategy , which is expected to be updated from its current 2012–2025 version towards a 2050 horizon . While the NDC process provided an important foundation, the current request goes beyond NDCs. The National Climate Change Strategy and related instruments are broader, long-term policy and planning frameworks. Therefore, the criteria and indicators used in the NDC process may not be directly transferable and need to be adapted to the nature of these instruments. UNICEF Ecuador has identified the UNICEF publication “Child-sensitive climate policies for every child ” as a strong methodological basis for this work. In particular, the four criteria proposed in the document — holistic and multisectoral, references, rights-based, and inclusive — could serve as a guiding framework to assess and strengthen child sensitivity in Ecuador’s climate policy instruments. Following initial exchanges with colleagues from the Children and Climate Resilience Global Practice, there is an opportunity to formalize technical assistance from regional and global colleagues to support an external review and adaptation of these criteria to the Ecuadorian context. This is particularly important given UNICEF Ecuador’s direct role in supporting the Government, as an external review would help ensure quality assurance, independence, and alignment with global and regional good practices. Requested Technical Assistance UNICEF Ecuador requests support from the Global and Regional teams to: Review the applicability of the UNICEF Child-Sensitive Climate Policies framework to broader climate policy instruments beyond NDCs, particularly the ENCC 2026–2050. Provide technical guidance on adapting the four child-sensitivity criteria to the Ecuadorian policy context. It includes the development or refine a set of metrics/indicators under the four criteria, drawing where relevant from the NDC child-sensitive framework, but adapting them for advocacy, policy review and evaluation purposes. Conduct an independent review of relevant climate policy instruments using the four criteria as an assessment framework. Expected Deliverables Technical guidance note (2–3 pages) outlining how the four child-sensitivity criteria can be applied to climate policy instruments beyond NDCs. Practical review checklist or assessment matrix based on the four UNICEF child-sensitivity criteria, which can be used by UNICEF Ecuador and government counterparts during the policy development process. These indicators may draw from the NDC framework but should be adjusted to the nature of long-term strategies and broader climate policy instruments. External technical review of the ENCC 2026–2050 (and, where feasible, other relevant policy instruments), identifying strengths and opportunities for strengthening child-sensitive and intergenerational approaches. Practical checklist or matrix A user-friendly checklist or assessment matrix that UNICEF Ecuador can use internally and with partners to review climate policy instruments through a child-sensitive lens.

desc: Technical support mission to Nigeria
full: Gender Equality Technical Support Mission to Nigeria Technical Expert Requested Denise Stuckenbruck Senior Adviser, Gender Equality (Health, Nutrition & WASH) Child Survival and Development Centre of Excellence Proposed Mission Dates 1-11 September 2026 (excludes travel time) Purpose of the Assignment UNICEF Nigeria Country Office requests Technical Assistance Hub support to facilitate an in-country mission by Denise Stuckenbruck from 1-11 September 2026. The mission will support the office's preparation for the 2028-2032 Country Programme and provide strategic gender equality expertise before, during, and following the first Strategic Moment of Reflection (SMR) . The assignment will help ensure that findings and recommendations emerging from the Gender Programme Review (GPR) are effectively reflected in programme strategies, SMR discussions, and the development of the next Country Programme. As a representative of UNICEF's global gender equality leadership and technical advisory capacity, Denise will provide strategic guidance on integrating gender equality and adolescent girls' empowerment priorities across sectors and strengthening alignment with UNICEF's corporate gender commitments. Justification Denise has been closely supporting UNICEF Nigeria's Gender Programme Review and has provided technical guidance throughout the process. Her in-country presence will enable direct engagement with senior management and programme teams to: Review and validate key Gender Programme Review findings and recommendations. Support the integration of GPR recommendations into sectoral and cross-sectoral programme strategies. Provide technical and strategic support during the first Strategic Moment of Reflection. Strengthen the positioning of gender equality and adolescent girls' empowerment within the emerging Country Programme framework. Support translation of SMR outcomes into actionable priorities for the 2028-2032 Country Programme. The mission is particularly timely given Nigeria's strategic importance within UNICEF's global gender equality agenda and its potential to accelerate results for adolescent girls and women at scale. Key Deliverables Strategic guidance provided to senior management and programme teams on integrating GPR recommendations into Country Programme development. Technical support to the first Strategic Moment of Reflection, including contributions to discussions on gender-intentional programming. Recommendations for strengthening gender equality and adolescent girls' empowerment priorities within the 2028-2032 Country Programme. Documentation of key actions and follow-up recommendations emerging from the SMR. Technical inputs on strengthening gender-intentional approaches within selected sector programmes. Additional Programmatic Support To maximize the value of the mission, Denise will also undertake a short support visit to the ASWA III initiative in Kaduna State to review progress on gender integration within WASH programming and identify lessons and promising practices that can inform broader organizational learning. She will further engage with Health and Nutrition colleagues to review ongoing gender equality and adolescent girls' empowerment initiatives and identify opportunities to strengthen cross-sectoral collaboration. Management Approval This request has been reviewed and approved by UNICEF Nigeria Country Office Senior Management , who strongly support Denise's participation in the Strategic Moment of Reflection and Country Programme development process. desc: provide specialized technical expertise and drafting to support the development of National Cybersecurity, Data Protection and Online Safety Standards and Guide
full: As part of the digital transformation agenda within the education sector and ongoing implementation of the Leaders in Teaching (LiT) programme (Mastercard Foundation funds to UNICEF) , the Ministry of Education and Sports (MoES) and UNICEF Uganda seek to strengthen cybersecurity, data protection and online safety across schools, Teacher Training Institutions (TTIs), TVET institutions, universities and digital learning platforms. While Uganda has a National Cybersecurity Strategy (uploaded) and an emerging ICT in Education Policy framework (attached), there remains a need for practical education-sector-specific standards and implementation guidance. Purpose of the TA To provide specialized technical expertise and drafting to support the development of National Cybersecurity, Data Protection and Online Safety Standards and Guidelines for the Education Sector in Uganda. Scope of Work The technical assistance will support: Review of relevant national policies, legislation, strategies and frameworks related to cybersecurity, data protection, ICT in Education and child online protection. Benchmarking of international and regional good practices and education-sector-specific standards, guidelines and frameworks. Development of a draft standards framework covering cybersecurity, data protection and online safety for education institutions. Development of practical implementation guidelines for schools, TTIs, TVET institutions, universities and other education institutions. Definition of institutional roles, responsibilities, accountability and governance arrangements. Support to stakeholder consultations, technical review and refinement of draft documents. Expected Outputs Draft National Cybersecurity, Data Protection and Online Safety Standards for the Education Sector. Draft implementation guidelines for education institutions. Defined roles and responsibilities for key actors across the education ecosystem. Finalized standards and guidelines incorporating stakeholder feedback. Expected Outcome Uganda's education sector has a practical, context-appropriate and implementable framework that establishes minimum cybersecurity, data protection and online safety requirements, strengthens safeguarding of learners and education data, and provides clear guidance for implementation across education institutions.

desc: CPD development products review - Tunisia
full: Subject: Request for Technical Review – UNICEF Tunisia Country Programme Document (CPD) 2027–2031 Dear colleagues, As part of the quality assurance process for the UNICEF Tunisia Country Programme Document (CPD) 2027–2031 , we would greatly appreciate your review of the enclosed CPD package, including the CPD, Programme Strategy Explanatory Notes (PSENs) comprising Theories of Change (ToCs), Results and Resources Plans (RRPs), and accompanying review matrix. The review package is available here: Review Package: TCO_CPD 2027-2031_Review Package Review Focus We would particularly welcome your views on: Executive Board sensitivity and strategic positioning Consistency with Strategic Moment of Reflection (SMR) decisions Quality and coherence of Theories of Change Convergence and causal linkages across outcomes and programme components Assumptions regarding UNICEF and partner contributions Adequacy, measurability and readiness of proposed indicators, including GMF indicators Timeline Please provide comments by 12 August 2026 . Feedback from Global Practice Groups, Cross-Sectoral Teams, Centres of Excellence and MENARO will be consolidated and addressed by the Country Office before final Regional Office review, Regional Director approval and submission to OSEB by 5 October 2026 . Comments may be provided either: Directly in the documents using tracked changes/comments; and/or As strategic observations and recommendations in the accompanying review matrix. We encourage reviewers to prioritize substantive and strategic observations over editorial comments. Background The proposed CPD has been developed drawing on: The Tunisia Evidence Synthesis (2025); The end-of-cycle review of the current programme; A country office-wide Visioning Exercise; Joint UN consultations undertaken for development of the UNSDCF 2027–2031 with Government, development partners, civil society, academia and other stakeholders; UNICEF-specific consultations with Government counterparts on the proposed programme architecture, results framework and strategic positioning, which are largely complete, with a final presentation and validation meeting with Government partners scheduled for the end of August 2026; The Strategic Moment of Reflection (SMR) conducted in January 2026 with the participation of the MENA Regional Director, Regional Office colleagues, Centres of Excellence and the Country Office, which helped define the strategic priorities, programme architecture and results structure. The current CPD 2021–2025 was extended through 2026 to enable alignment with the National Development Plan 2026–2030, the UNSDCF 2027–2031 and the above consultation processes. The new CPD reflects the strategic directions emerging from the SMR, including the principles of differentiation, focus, scale and impact, supported by a tiered prioritization methodology. Areas for Review 1. Strategic Positioning and Executive Board Readiness Please identify any language, positioning, assumptions or formulations that may raise concerns during Executive Board review, as well as areas where the rationale, evidence base or framing could be strengthened. 2. Consistency with the Strategic Moment of Reflection Please assess whether the CPD adequately reflects the strategic directions agreed during the SMR, including: Focus, differentiation, scale and impact; Strategic prioritization and selectivity; Convergence and cross-sectoral collaboration; Systems strengthening and pathways to scale; Upstream policy, governance and financing dimensions; The balance between continuity and innovation. 3. Alignment with UNICEF auditable and other organisational guidance Please review consistency with: The UNICEF Strategic Plan and Africa Strategy; Programme Strategy Explanatory Note guidance; Mandatory Theory of Change requirements; Results and Resources Plan requirements; Relevant Global Practice and Cross-Sectoral Team guidance. In particular, please assess whether outcome and output statements, results chains, assumptions and Theories of Change are coherent, evidence-based and sufficiently articulate causal pathways, including convergence across outcomes and programme components. 4. Adequacy of the Results Architecture and Measurement Framework Please review: Outcome and output logic; Consistency between the CPD, ToCs and RRPs; Adequacy and strategic value of proposed indicators; Indicator measurability and usefulness for accountability and learning; Readiness and methodological robustness of proposed GMF indicators, including definitions, methodologies, data sources and means of verification; Feasibility of establishing and tracking baselines and targets. 5. UNICEF Contribution and Partnerships Please assess whether the programme adequately articulates: UNICEF’s comparative advantage and contribution; The roles and expected contributions of Government and other partners; Key assumptions regarding partner engagement and capacity; Partnership strategies required to achieve results at scale. 6. Linkages Across Programme Components Please review whether the programme sufficiently captures: Convergence and synergies across programme components; Interdependencies and complementarities across outcomes; Opportunities for integrated programming and collective impact; Pathways through which combined sectoral interventions and UN joint programming contribute to higher-level change. Thank you in advance for your support and technical expertise in shaping UNICEF Tunisia’s next Country Programme. The Country Office looks forward to your comments and recommendations. With thanks and appreciation, UNICEF Tunisia Country Office

desc: Technical assistance for the development of a national stunting prevention strategy in Mexico
full: Technical assistance for the development of a national stunting prevention strategy in Mexico (Big Ticket Item). UNICEF Mexico is seeking technical support to develop a comprehensive, evidence-based strategy for the prevention of stunting, including the formulation of a Theory of Change tailored to the Mexican context and aligned with government priorities. Given the scale of the challenge—with an estimated 1.4 million children affected by chronic malnutrition—and the current opportunity to engage high-level government stakeholders, this represents a strategic investment with significant potential for impact. It would be highly beneficial to have the in-country support of a Spanish-speaking colleague from the Centre of Excellence who could participate in technical discussions with the Government of Mexico and provide continuity during the temporary deployment of the staff member leading this work, who will be on surge assignment in Venezuela until the end of August 2026. In addition, support for resource mobilization would be critical to leverage the strategy development process and secure the funding required for its implementation at scale.

desc: Technical assistance for the development of clinical guidelines for the inpatient management of severe acute malnutrition with medical complications.
full: Technical assistance for the development of clinical guidelines for the inpatient management of severe acute malnutrition with medical complications. UNICEF Mexico would appreciate technical support from the Centre of Excellence to strengthen the development of national clinical guidelines for the management of severe acute malnutrition with complications at hospital level. Specifically, we would welcome the provision of technical recommendations and key considerations prior to the drafting process, drawing on global evidence, WHO guidance, and country experiences. We would also highly value the CoE’s technical review of both the draft and final versions of the guidelines to ensure alignment with international standards and best practices. This support will contribute to improving the quality of care provided to children with severe acute malnutrition and to strengthening Mexico’s capacity to effectively manage SAM cases.

desc: Technical assistance for the review of dietary guidelines for children 0–4 years of age.
full: Technical assistance for the review of dietary guidelines for children 0–4 years of age. UNICEF Mexico would greatly appreciate technical support from the Centre of Excellence to review the draft national dietary guidelines for children aged 0–4 years. Specifically, we would welcome a technical review of the draft document to ensure alignment with the latest global evidence and international recommendations on infant and young child feeding, healthy diets, breastfeeding, complementary feeding, and the prevention of malnutrition in all its forms. The CoE’s feedback would help strengthen the scientific rigor, coherence, and practical relevance of the guidelines before their finalization and adoption. This support would contribute to ensuring that Mexico’s dietary guidance for young children reflects current best practices and promotes optimal nutrition, growth, and development during the critical first years of life.

desc: Technical Assistance to Support the Development of CPD
full: Title: Technical Assistance to Support the Development of a Continuing Professional Development (CPD) Content Evaluation Framework for ICT in Uganda Background The Ministry of Education and Sports (MoES) is strengthening the quality and effectiveness of ICT-related Continuing Professional Development (CPD) for teachers, lecturers, tutors, and education professionals. As the volume of digital learning and ICT training content expands, there is a need for a standardized framework to assess the quality, relevance, consistency, and effectiveness of CPD materials before deployment and scale-up. UNICEF is the partner under the Leaders in Teaching (LIT) Mastercard Foundation funded component to lead ICT integration in Uganda. UNICEF Uganda seeks technical assistance to support the development of a CPD Content Evaluation Framework that will provide clear criteria and tools for reviewing and quality assuring ICT-related CPD content across the education sector. Scope of Work The technical assistance will support: Review of existing national and international approaches to CPD content quality assurance. Development of a CPD Content Evaluation Framework for ICT-related professional development programmes. Development of evaluation criteria and quality assurance tools for reviewing CPD content. Definition of content review processes, roles, and responsibilities. Support for stakeholder consultations and validation of the framework. Expected Outputs Draft CPD Content Evaluation Framework for ICT. Content quality review criteria and scoring tools. Guidance on content review and approval processes. Final framework incorporating stakeholder feedback. Expected Outcome A standardized quality assurance framework is available to guide the review, validation, and continuous improvement of ICT-related CPD content, helping ensure that professional learning materials are accurate, clear, relevant, and effective in supporting educator capacity development.

desc: TA to develop a comprehensive costing framework for National ECD Policy
full: technical assistance to develop a comprehensive costing framework and implementation budget for the National Early Childhood Development (ECD) Policy. This support will commence in September , once the final draft of the policy is available for review and validation. Scope of Technical Assistance The selected consultant or technical partner will be expected to: Review Policy and Supporting Documentation Conduct a detailed review of the final draft National ECD Policy and all relevant supporting documents, including implementation plans, sector strategies, legislative frameworks, and existing ECD programmes. Assess policy priorities, strategic objectives, and proposed interventions to identify resource implications and costing requirements. Develop a Costing Methodology Design an appropriate methodology for costing the implementation of the National ECD Policy, aligned with national planning and budgeting processes. Identify cost drivers, assumptions, financing requirements, and implementation scenarios. Prepare a Comprehensive Costing Framework Estimate the financial resources required to implement the policy over the proposed implementation period. Provide detailed cost projections by strategic objective, programme area, responsible agency, and implementation phase. Identify recurrent and capital expenditure requirements. Provide Technical Guidance and Capacity Support Advise relevant stakeholders on costing approaches, assumptions, and methodologies. Facilitate consultations and validation sessions with government ministries, agencies, development partners, and other key stakeholders. Build capacity of designated personnel to understand and utilize the costing framework. Develop an ECD Financing and Investment Roadmap Produce a practical roadmap outlining the sequencing of implementation activities and associated financing needs. Identify potential funding sources, financing gaps, and resource mobilization opportunities. Recommend strategies for phased implementation based on available resources and priorities. Deliver Final Outputs Inception report outlining the methodology, workplan, and stakeholder engagement approach. Policy costing model and accompanying assumptions. Costed implementation framework and budget estimates. Financing and investment roadmap. Final technical report summarizing findings, recommendations, and next steps for implementation. Timing The technical assistance is expected to begin in September , following completion and availability of the final draft National Early Childhood Development Policy for review. The assignment should be structured to support timely integration of costing results into planning, budgeting, and implementation processes. Expected Outcome A robust, evidence-based costing and financing framework that provides Government and stakeholders with a clear understanding of the resources required for implementation of the National Early Childhood Development Policy, together with a practical roadmap for financing and phased execution.

desc: Social and Behavioral Insights and Community-Based Surveillance Systems Strengthening Support for Maldives
full: Technical Assistance to Strengthen National Capacity on Social and Behavioral Insights (SBI) and Community-Based Surveillance (CBS) in Maldives Background and Justification The Health Protection Agency (HPA), with support from UNICEF and WHO, is seeking technical assistance to institutionalize Social and Behavioral Insights (SBI) and Community-Based Surveillance (CBS) as routine functions within national health emergency preparedness, response, and health promotion systems. Currently, both functions are implemented in a fragmented and ad hoc manner, with limited standardized guidance, systems, or workforce capacity. Strengthening these capacities is essential to improve early detection of public health threats, enhance understanding of community behaviors and perceptions, strengthen risk communication and community engagement, and support evidence-based decision-making for both emergency response and long-term NCD prevention. The proposed technical assistance will support the development of national frameworks, SOPs, operational tools, training curricula, and monitoring systems aligned with WHO and UNICEF guidance and adapted to the Maldivian context. The work will contribute to strengthening IHR core capacities, community-centered surveillance, and the systematic use of behavioral data in public health programming. Purpose of the Assignment To provide technical expertise for the design, development, piloting, and institutionalization of national SBI and CBS systems within HPA, including the development of operational frameworks, SOPs, capacity-building packages, and monitoring systems. Scope of Technical Assistance Component 1: Community-Based Surveillance (CBS) Conduct situational analysis and mapping of existing community networks and surveillance mechanisms. Develop a national CBS framework. Develop CBS SOPs, reporting pathways, job aids, and digital reporting tools. Pilot test CBS approaches in selected atolls and refine tools based on findings. Component 2: Social and Behavioral Insights (SBI) Review and adapt global SBI tools and approaches for Maldives. Map SBI data flows and decision-making processes. Develop national SOPs and guidance on social listening, community feedback, behavioral assessments, infodemic management, and behavior change communication. Support validation and institutionalization within HPA systems. Component 3: Capacity Building Develop integrated SBI and CBS training curricula and materials. Conduct national Training of Trainers (TOT). Support cascade training at national and subnational levels. Conduct media and journalist sensitization sessions. Component 4: Monitoring and Evaluation Develop integrated monitoring and evaluation frameworks and indicators. Establish systems to monitor training coverage, implementation, and performance. Conduct periodic reviews and produce final evaluation findings and sustainability recommendations. Expected Deliverables Situational Analysis and Community Network Mapping Report. National CBS Framework. CBS SOPs, operational tools, and pilot report. SBI Desk Review Report. SBI Data Flow Protocols. National SBI SOP and technical guidance documents. Integrated SBI and CBS Training Package. National TOT completed. Subnational cascade trainings completed. Media sensitization sessions conducted. Integrated M&E Framework. Training coverage and monitoring reports. Final evaluation report and sustainability roadmap.

Request Title: Technical Assistance for Borneo Animation and Games Festival B2B Panel and Industry Orientation Session Description: Support is requested from Josianne Barron to review and provide technical and strategic feedback on the BAGFEST B2B panel and industry orientation session currently being developed by UNICEF Malaysia. Specifically, feedback is sought on: The draft B2B panel guide, including whether the proposed discussion questions are likely to resonate with gaming industry stakeholders and whether there are any important issues, trends, perspectives or emerging challenges that should be incorporated. The design and facilitation approach for the industry orientation session, including recommendations on how to make the session engaging and relevant for students, fresh graduates and aspiring professionals, while also ensuring value for current industry players should they participate. Possible interactive components, tools, surveys, group activities, role plays, or calls to action that could support participant engagement and contribute to the longer-term objective of building a cohort of industry stakeholders interested in advancing child rights and safer gaming environments. The feedback will be used to refine the content, format and stakeholder engagement strategy for both sessions ahead of BAGFEST. Also included a background document from an earlier consultation with industry by Content Forum.

Technical support is requested for a Policy Dialogue on “Protecting Children in the Digital Era,” tentatively scheduled for the morning of 20 or 21 August 2026 and co-organized by the Ministry of Justice under the EU Justice and Legal Empowerment in Viet Nam, phase II. The dialogue will convene government agencies, justice sector institutions, development partners, civil society organizations, and private sector stakeholders to discuss legal and policy priorities for strengthening child protection in the digital environment. Objectives / Expected Results Provide international expertise and comparative good practices on legal, regulatory, and institutional measures to prevent and respond to online harms against children, drawing on global evidence and lessons learned from other countries. Inform policy discussions in Viet Nam by identifying priority areas for strengthening laws, policies, implementation mechanisms, and multi-sectoral coordination to create a safer, healthier, and more child-friendly digital environment. Support UNICEF's strategic engagement and advocacy messages by providing technical inputs for UNICEF's opening and closing remarks, ensuring alignment with international child rights standards and emerging global trends. Contribute to a stronger policy dialogue outcome by highlighting actionable recommendations that can inform the implementation of the forthcoming National Program on Online Child Protection and Development (2026-2030) and broader legal reform efforts related to child protection in the digital environment. Expected Deliverables Deliverable 1: Technical preparation Review the draft agenda and background materials. Participate in preparatory discussions with UNICEF and partners as needed. Provide key technical messages and recommendations relevant to the policy dialogue. Deliverable 2: Panel participation Serve as a panelist during Session 1: Strengthening the Legal Framework – Building Safety Standards . Provide remarks addressing: International standards and good practices for protecting children online. Priority legal and policy measures that Viet Nam may consider to strengthen child online protection. Respond to questions from participants during the discussion and Q&A sessions. Deliverable 3: Support to UNICEF statements Provide inputs and suggested talking points for UNICEF Representative's opening remarks. Provide key messages and recommendations for UNICEF Representative's concluding remarks and proposed joint message, as needed. Deliverable 4: Post-event technical inputs Share a short note (1-2 pages) summarizing key international lessons, recommendations, and follow-up considerations emerging from the dialogue, if requested by UNICEF.

desc: Supporting Mexico CO with CEH technical assistance
full: As Mexico moves from policy development to implementation of its child environmental health and lead agenda, UNICEF Mexico would appreciate continued technical support from the CoE in four key areas. First, review and technical feedback on key products, including the National Strategy for the Prevention and Control of Lead Exposure 2026–2030, the Child Environmental Health (CEH) Framework for Mexico, SBC and risk communication materials, and implementation-related documents developed during Phase II. UNICEF Malaysia requests urgent technical assistance to undertake an expert review of UNICEF's draft submission to the Government of Malaysia's public consultation on the proposed Artificial Intelligence (AI) Governance Bill. The proposed Bill seeks to establish Malaysia's national legal framework for safe, responsible and innovation-enabling AI, including provisions on governance architecture, AI governance principles, risk management, incident reporting and regulatory sandboxes. UNICEF Malaysia is seeking a rapid technical review by colleagues with expertise in AI governance, digital rights, child rights in the digital environment, AI regulation, and emerging global AI legislative frameworks. The public consultation closes on 31 July 2026, and UNICEF Malaysia aims to finalize its submission before this deadline. We would therefore appreciate consolidated technical feedback by 30 July 2026.

desc: Support the development of a strategic UNICEF–League of Arab States (LAS) Action Plan by providing technical inputs on priority child rights issues.
full: Background: The League of Arab States (LAS) is a key regional partner for advancing the child rights agenda across the Middle East and North Africa. LAS offers an important platform for regional advocacy, policy dialogue, and engagement with Member States on issues affecting children. Recent discussions between MENARO and LAS have highlighted the opportunity to develop a new UNICEF–LAS Action Plan to guide future collaboration and ensure a more strategic, coordinated, and results-oriented partnership. This would build on previous cooperation frameworks while reflecting current regional priorities and UNICEF’s evolving organizational structure. The proposed Action Plan is expected to move beyond activity-based collaboration and focus on a limited number of strategic child rights priorities where LAS's convening power, political reach, and engagement with Member States can help accelerate progress at regional and national levels. Request: MENARO requests all Centres of Excellence (COEs) to provide inputs for inclusion in the proposed UNICEF–LAS Action Plan. Specifically, please identify: Priority child rights issues and areas where LAS can add value in advancing UNICEF priorities with Member States through advocacy, policy dialogue, regional coordination, and regional commitments. Potential activities or deliverables that could be jointly implemented with LAS. Suggested UNICEF focal point(s) for follow-up. Key Consideration: Inputs should focus on strategic issues where LAS engagement can influence policy, strengthen regional commitments, facilitate peer learning among Member States, or advance collective action on child rights priorities, rather than stand-alone technical activities.

desc: Technical Assistance for the Design, Deployment and Scale-up of an Indigenous Digital Learning Ecosystem in Ecuador
full: Technical Assistance for the Design, Deployment and Scale-up of an Indigenous Digital Learning Ecosystem in Ecuador Short Description of the Request UNICEF Ecuador requests technical assistance to design and implement a scalable digital learning ecosystem for indigenous and rural communities, starting with the Ai Cofán community in Dureno (Sucumbíos). The initiative seeks to leverage UNICEF's Learning Passport platform, offline learning capabilities, teacher professional development, localized indigenous educational content, and community learning spaces to improve equitable access to quality education in low-connectivity environments. The request will support the assessment, design, implementation planning, governance model, content strategy, offline architecture, monitoring framework, and identification of global good practices that can be adapted to the Ecuador context. desc: Reviewing and providing comments and recommendations on the draft report of “A Review and Analysis of Evidence on Children's Environmental Health in Armenia
full: Technical assistance for reviewing and providing comments and recommendations on the draft report of “A Review and Analysis of Evidence on Children's Environmental Health in Armenia” Background : Children in Armenia are exposed to a big number of environmental risks and hazards. Data of the Global Child Hazard Database shows that among others air pollution, heatwaves and droughts play crucial role affecting 98 per cent, 84 per cent and 64 per cent of children correspondingly. In addition, research by Pure Earth reported extremely high levels of heavy metals and toxic exposures in soil and playgrounds in mining-affected regions, with 57%-85% of all tested children aged 4 to 6 years-old suffering from elevated blood lead levels in some communities [1] . Still, there remains a systemic data gap linking environmental exposures to child health outcomes (e.g., morbidity and mortality by exposure type), with existing evidence coming primarily from small-scale or focused studies and NGO-led assessments rather than comprehensive national health surveillance systems. Armenia CO initiated a desk review and secondary analysis of existing data and evidence on children’s environmental health in Armenia, to identify main environmental and climate-related hazards and risk factors and exploring their potential implications for children’s health and paediatric health system, as well as to develop recommendations on (1) strengthening the resilience and capacity of the health system and families/communities to address child health challenges associated with an increasing burden of environmental risks and hazards, and (2) addressing the critical data and evidence gaps on children’s environmental health in Armenia that require further research and analysis to deepen the understanding of these issues or to fill existing data gaps. The contractor has provided the draft report. Technical assistance should cover the following needs/requirements: - review the draft report, including: (1) if all key environmental and climate-related risks and hazards [mentioned in the TOR] affecting children’s health are comprehensively analyzed; (2) if their impact to children’s health is comprehensively analyzed; (3) if their impact to pediatric health system is comprehensively analyzed; (4) if data gaps on any environmental and climate-related risk and hazard are identified and well justified. - review the recommendations provided in the draft in terms of their relevance to the identified risks and problems, feasibility, and effectiveness to address the identified problems - provide comments, suggestions, and recommendations on all sections of the report, as appropriate The link to the Draft Report and to the TOR of the Assignment is here: https://unicef-my.sharepoint.com/shared?listurl=https%3A%2F%2Funicef%2Dmy%2Esharepoint%2Ecom%2Fpersonal%2Fsshahbazyan%5Funicef%5Forg%2FDocuments&id=%2Fpersonal%2Fsshahbazyan%5Funicef%5Forg%2FDocuments%2FUNICEF%2FPA%5FH%26N%5FSona%2Fhealth%2FSales%20Order%20PO%2F2026%2FDesk%20Research%20Children%20Enviromental%20Health%2Ffor%20review&shareLink=1&ga=1 [1] https://www.pureearth.org/our-projects/country-project-pages/armenia/
