desc: National Critical Care Guidelines Review and Implementation Readiness Support for Eswatini
full: Title Technical Assistance for Expert Review and Finalization of National Critical Care Guidelines and Standards for Eswatini Short Description The Ministry of Health, through the Critical Care Technical Working Group, seeks technical assistance to conduct an independent expert review of the National Critical Care Service Provision Guidelines and National Critical Care Treatment Guidelines (Adult and Neonatal). The review will assess the technical quality, evidence base, alignment with global standards, feasibility of implementation within the Eswatini health system, and provide recommendations for finalization prior to national rollout. The assignment will support strengthening the quality, safety, and effectiveness of critical care services across all levels of care in Eswatini. [unicef-my....epoint.com] Objectives Overall Objective To strengthen the quality and implementation readiness of Eswatini's national critical care guidelines through an independent technical review and validation process. Specific Objectives Review the National Guidelines on the Provision of Critical Care Services in Eswatini and assess alignment with WHO and other internationally recognized critical care standards. Review the National Critical Care Treatment Guidelines (Adult and Neonatal) for clinical accuracy, evidence-based content, completeness, and applicability within the Eswatini context. Identify gaps, inconsistencies, and areas requiring strengthening, including service delivery, workforce, equipment, referral pathways, quality improvement, and patient safety considerations. Facilitate technical consultations with the Ministry of Health and Critical Care Technical Working Group to discuss findings and proposed revisions. Support incorporation of agreed recommendations and preparation of final guideline documents for endorsement and implementation. Expected Results National critical care service provision guidelines reviewed against international best practices. National adult and neonatal critical care treatment guidelines reviewed and strengthened. Practical recommendations developed to improve quality, feasibility, and implementation readiness. Consensus reached among key stakeholders on priority revisions. Finalized guideline documents ready for Ministry approval, dissemination, and implementation. Key Deliverables Inception Report Review methodology and workplan. Assessment framework and review criteria. Technical Review Report Detailed assessment of each guideline document. Benchmarking against current international standards and evidence. Identification of gaps and recommendations. Stakeholder Consultation/Validation Session Facilitation of a virtual or in-country review meeting with the Ministry of Health and TWG. Presentation of findings and recommendations. Revised Guideline Documents Annotated versions showing proposed amendments. Final clean versions incorporating agreed revisions. Final Assignment Report Summary of review process. Key changes made. Recommendations for dissemination, capacity building, monitoring, and implementation. Suggested Scope of Expertise Required Senior Critical Care Specialist (Adult ICU/HDU services). Neonatal/Pediatric Critical Care Specialist. Health Systems or Clinical Governance Expert with experience in guideline development and implementation. desc: Capacity building for Caribbean countries on climate resilient sanitation (CRS)
full: UNICEF ECA is supporting capacity building for Caribbean countries on climate resilient sanitation (CRS), as part of the Caribbean CRS cohort initiative. In partnership with the WB and the Caribbean Water and Wastewater Association (CWWA), a series of webinars have been planned for countries with some initial topics selected as indicated below. Technical assistance is being sought for the development of the webinar presentations and facilitation during the webinar, alongside WB colleagues. Topics are listed below. Climate ‑ resilient sanitation systems and risk assessment : Adaptation and mitigation for onsite, decentralized and sewered systems, including climate risk assessments for hurricanes, flooding and sea‑level rise. Policies, legislation and regulation for wastewater and sanitation services : Developing wastewater and sludge legislation, standards and regulatory frameworks, addressing institutional fragmentation, enforcement challenges and change management. Sanitation project development for finance and investment : From concept to bankable projects, including project structuring, donor identification, funding strategies and aligning sanitation investments with climate and development finance requirements. Sanitation data, monitoring and learning for better decision ‑ making : Data systems, tools and regional sources; data quality and monitoring; system assessments, research, case study repositories, best‑practice sharing and peer learning across countries.

desc: Technical Assistance for the Review and Development of an Updated Parenting Education Manual for Children Aged 0-8 Years in Bhutan
full: Technical Assistance for the Review and Development of an Updated Parenting Education Manual for Children Aged 0-8 Years in Bhutan UNICEF Bhutan would like to submit a TA request to seek technical assistance/guidance to review and update the existing Parenting Education Manual for children aged 0-8 years. The revised manual will build on the current UNICEF-MoESD parenting education resource ( National Parenting Education Manual | UNICEF Bhutan ) and integrate emerging evidence, priorities, and challenges affecting young children and caregivers in Bhutan. Age-specific guidance and easy-to-use reference tools should enable caregivers and frontline workers to provide responsive, developmentally appropriate support for children from birth to eight years.

Ending Child Marriage in Comoros: Transforming Social Norms and Increasing Participation Short Description of the Request UNICEF Comoros is seeking technical assistance to strengthen the design and implementation of a comprehensive social and behaviour change intervention to address harmful social norms that perpetuate child marriage. The programme aims to reach more than 50,000 adolescents and engage families, communities, religious leaders, educators, and local institutions through adolescent empowerment, community dialogue, faith-based engagement, and multimedia communication campaigns. Support is requested to ensure the programme reflects global evidence, incorporates innovative approaches, and aligns with best practices from the Global Programme to End Child Marriage. Objectives and Expectations Strengthen the evidence base and theory of change for social norm transformation interventions addressing child marriage in Comoros. Review and refine programme design, implementation modalities, targeting strategy, and results framework. Support development of a comprehensive SBC strategy integrating community engagement, digital innovation, adolescent participation, and faith-based approaches. Identify evidence-based interventions with the highest potential for catalytic impact and scalability. Strengthen monitoring, evaluation, learning, and knowledge management frameworks for measuring social norm change. Facilitate integration of child marriage prevention within broader child protection, gender equality, adolescent development, and education programming. Document lessons learned and promising practices from comparable country programmes that can be adapted to the Comorian context. Expected Deliverables Technical review and quality assurance report of the proposed intervention package. Refined theory of change and social norms pathway analysis. SBC strategy and implementation roadmap. Standardized adolescent club engagement package, including curriculum recommendations and participation standards. Guidance package for engagement of religious and traditional leaders. Community dialogue and social norms measurement toolkit. Monitoring and evaluation framework with indicators for behavioural and social norm change. Recommendations on digital engagement, social listening, youth-generated content, and community mobilization mechanisms. Resource mobilization package highlighting catalytic interventions, investment cases, and results projections for partners and donors. Knowledge brief summarizing international good practices and lessons applicable to island and culturally conservative contexts. Global Practices and Technical Teams to Involve Child Protection Global Practice (Ending Child Marriage and Harmful Practices). Social and Behaviour Change (SBC) Global Practice. Adolescent Development and Participation (ADAP). Gender Equality Programme Team. Education Programme Team. Data, Research, Evaluation and Learning specialists. Digital Communication and Innovation teams. Partnerships and Resource Mobilization teams. Regional SBC and Child Protection specialists from ESARO/ESAR. UNFPA technical experts on adolescent girls and harmful practices, where appropriate. Strategic Accelerators Behavioural insights and social norms research. Digital engagement platforms for adolescents and youth-led advocacy. Faith-based engagement approaches and partnerships with religious leaders. Community-driven social accountability mechanisms and scorecards. Youth-generated multimedia content and storytelling. Social listening and real-time feedback systems. Evidence generation and impact measurement. South-South learning exchanges with countries that have successfully reduced child marriage prevalence. Integration with broader adolescent empowerment, education, and economic empowerment initiatives. Strategic donor engagement and catalytic financing opportunities linked to the Global Programme to End Child Marriage. This TA would contribute directly to UNICEF Comoros' ambition to accelerate progress toward SDG 5.3 by transforming harmful social norms, strengthening community ownership, and empowering adolescents as agents of change against child marriage.

Technical Assistance Request to the TA Hub: Birth Registration and Right to Identity UNICEF Honduras requests technical assistance from the TA Hub and UNICEF global expertise on birth registration and the right to identity to support the strengthening of the national enrolment and identification process for children and adolescents. The assistance will help develop practical recommendations, safeguards and implementation strategies to ensure that the enrolment process for obtaining identity documents is child-sensitive, rights-based, inclusive and protective against abuse, exploitation, discrimination, data misuse and other potential risks. The request will also support national registration stakeholders, including the RNP and related child protection, education, social protection and local governance actors, to reach children and adolescents who are underrepresented, excluded from services or facing specific barriers to registration and identification. Objectives of the technical assistance Review the proposed enrolment process for children and adolescents and identify protection, safeguarding, inclusion and data privacy risks that may arise before, during and after registration. Develop a concise set of recommendations and minimum safeguards to ensure that the identity-document enrolment process is safe, child-friendly, non-discriminatory and aligned with international standards on birth registration, legal identity, child protection and data protection. Strengthen the capacity of registration stakeholders to identify and reach children and adolescents who are less represented in registration systems, including children out of school, children in alternative care or protection measures, children with disabilities, Indigenous children, children affected by migration or displacement, and children in remote or hard-to-reach communities. Provide practical guidance for integrating referral pathways, reporting mechanisms and coordination with child protection systems into the enrolment process, including links with SIGADENAH and local child rights structures. Expectations from the TA Hub and UNICEF specialist A rapid technical review of the current enrolment approach, training materials, field procedures and available safeguards from the perspective of birth registration, legal identity, child protection, inclusion and responsible data governance. A short package of prioritized recommendations that can be operationalized quickly by UNICEF, RNP and implementation partners during the 2026 enrolment process. Technical inputs to strengthen guidance for enumerators, supervisors and coordinators, including practical measures on informed consent and assent, safe interaction with children, confidentiality, prevention of sexual exploitation and abuse, disability inclusion, intercultural approaches and safe referral of protection concerns. A facilitated exchange with country, regional or global experiences that have successfully expanded birth registration and legal identity for excluded groups through health, education, social protection, local governance or mobile registration strategies. Potential outcomes A child safeguarding and inclusion checklist for registration and enrolment teams, including minimum actions before, during and after engagement with children and caregivers. A short technical note with recommended safeguards on child protection, PEAS, confidentiality, consent/assent, data minimization, privacy and safe handling of sensitive information, including biometric or identity-related data where applicable. A differentiated outreach strategy for underrepresented groups of children and adolescents, with practical actions to reduce barriers related to geography, language, disability, documentation gaps, family separation, protection measures, migration status or exclusion from school. An updated capacity-building package for RNP field teams, supervisors and partner institutions, including key messages, case scenarios, referral protocols and supervision tools. A set of rapid implementation priorities for UNICEF and partners to support quality assurance, monitoring and adaptation during the initial phases of enrolment.

desc: Operational Support for the National Measles Vaccination Campaign in Honduras
full: Technical Assistance for Operational Support for Measles Vaccination Campaign in Honduras The Ministry of Health, through the Expanded Programme on Immunization (EPI), is preparing a nationwide measles vaccination campaign in response to the accumulation of susceptible children and the heightened risk of measles outbreaks in the region. Previous analyses conducted by the EPI estimated that the number of susceptible children exceeds one birth cohort, prompting discussions on the need to implement a preventive campaign as soon as feasible. Vaccine availability has been confirmed, including 1.5 million doses of MMR vaccine and 270,000 doses of MR vaccine. Implementation of the campaign has been delayed due to the prioritization of the national routine immunization campaign conducted between May and June 2026, as well as increased vaccine hesitancy following reports of adverse events following immunization. Consequently, the EPI has postponed the measles campaign to october 2026 to allow sufficient time for preparation and implementation of risk communication and community engagement activities aimed at improving public confidence and vaccine acceptance. The TA request is focused on securing technical and financial assistance for the recruitment of a national consultant who will support the planning, implementation, monitoring, and reporting of the national measles vaccination campaign, with particular emphasis on Social and Behaviour Change (SBC) interventions to address vaccine hesitancy and improve campaign performance. Attached the ToRs prepared.

Title: Maldives CPD 2027-2031: Technical Review and Quality Assurance Support for Draft Country Programme Document Background UNICEF Maldives is preparing its Country Programme Document (CPD) 2027-2031. The Country Office requests technical assistance from the relevant Centres of Excellence (CoEs) to provide quality assurance and technical review of the draft CPD and associated results framework, ensuring strategic coherence, technical rigor, and alignment with UNICEF Strategic Plan priorities and programming excellence standards. The request forms part of the RO-cleared CPD roadmap and builds on previous consultations conducted through the Strategic Moment of Reflection (SMR), prioritization exercise, and subsequent programme design discussions. The draft CPD reflects the recommendations and agreements reached through these processes and is now at the stage where technical review and refinement are required prior to further internal and external consultation. Objective of Technical Assistance To obtain technical review and quality assurance support for the Maldives CPD 2027-2031 and Results and Resources Framework, with a focus on strengthening strategic positioning, clarity of articulation, internal coherence, results logic, and alignment with UNICEF programming principles and Strategic Plan priorities. desc: Technical Review and Facilitation Support for the Operationalisation of the Girls' Movement in Guinea
full: Technical Review and Facilitation Support for the Operationalisation of the Girls' Movement in Guinea: Background Following the National Girls' Consultations (2025) and Guinea's commitments under the West and Central Africa Girls' Summit and the Dakar Declaration , UNICEF Guinea is supporting the Government to institutionalise the Girls' Movement as a national platform for advancing adolescent girls' rights, leadership and meaningful participation. The proposed institutionalisation model aims to establish a sustainable, government-led mechanism that connects adolescent girls' priorities with national policies, planning processes and accountability systems while ensuring meaningful adolescent participation throughout the process. As a key milestone, UNICEF Guinea and the Ministry of Women, Family and Solidarities will organise a two-day National Co-Creation Workshop in September 2026 bringing together government institutions, adolescent girls, youth structures, civil society and development partners to jointly define the governance model, institutional anchorage, participation mechanisms and national roadmap for the Girls' Movement. The workshop has been designed as a genuine co-creation exercise rather than a validation meeting, requiring strong technical facilitation and expertise on adolescent participation methodologies. Purpose of the Technical Assistance The purpose of this TA is to provide strategic and technical support from the Gender and Adolescent Girls experts within the Centres of Excellence to strengthen the conceptualisation, technical quality and facilitation of the national co-creation process for the operationalisation of the Girls' Movement in Guinea. The support will ensure alignment with: UNICEF's Gender Equality and ADAP programming approaches; Standards for Meaningful Adolescent Participation; The Dakar Declaration; Regional Girls' Movement guidance and emerging learning from other country offices. Scope of Work The requested support includes: 1. Technical review Review and provide technical feedback on: Concept Note for the institutionalisation of the Girls' Movement; ToRs for the National Co-Creation Workshop; Proposed governance model; Theory of Change; Participation strategy for adolescent girls; Draft roadmap for operationalisation. 2. Conceptual support Provide technical guidance on: institutionalisation options; governance arrangements; accountability mechanisms; meaningful adolescent participation; multisectoral coordination; safeguarding and inclusion considerations; alignment with regional Girls' Movement approaches. 3. Workshop design Support refinement of: facilitation methodology; agenda and session flow; participatory methodologies; co-creation exercises; outputs expected from each working session; documentation approach. 4. Facilitation support Provide in-person facilitation during the September National Co-Creation Workshop, including: facilitating selected strategic sessions; supporting breakout group facilitation; ensuring high-quality participatory processes; supporting consensus-building among stakeholders; mentoring UNICEF Guinea staff during the facilitation process. 5. Post-workshop support Provide technical inputs to: workshop report; revised institutional model; roadmap; recommendations; next steps towards operationalisation. Expected Deliverables The CoE colleague(s) will provide: Technical review of the Concept Note and ToRs. Written recommendations for strengthening the workshop design. Final facilitation methodology. Technical facilitation of the National Co-Creation Workshop (in person). Post-workshop technical review of key outputs. Recommendations for operationalising the Girls' Movement following the workshop. Timeline Activity Timing Technical review of documents July-August 2026 Joint planning meetings August–September 2026 National Co-Creation Workshop September 2026 Post-workshop technical support September–October 2026 Requested Profile UNICEF colleague(s) from the Gender and Adolescent Girls Centres of Excellence with demonstrated experience in: Adolescent Girls Programming ADAP Meaningful Adolescent Participation Facilitation of participatory and co-creation processes Gender-transformative programming Institutional strengthening and governance Girls' Movement and/or Dakar Declaration implementation West and Central Africa regional programming (desirable) Justification This TA represents a strategic investment to ensure that the institutionalisation of the Girls' Movement in Guinea reflects regional good practice and UNICEF standards from the outset. As this workshop will define the Movement's governance architecture, participation mechanisms and implementation roadmap, high-quality technical facilitation is critical to building government ownership while preserving the integrity of a meaningful, girl-centred co-creation process. The involvement of the CoE will also facilitate cross-country learning and strengthen the scalability and sustainability of the initiative across the region.

UNICEF China seeks technical support from Global Practice on Economic and Social Policy to strengthen the design, implementation, interpretation, and policy translation of a research initiative examining the impact of AI on child and adolescent wellbeing in China. Led by Peking University in collaboration with UNICEF China and the Lancet Commission on Adolescent Health and Wellbeing, the research will generate large-scale evidence on how AI influences children's and adolescents' health, learning, cognitive development, mental wellbeing, safety, equity, and broader development outcomes. Policy translation support, including e.g., review of policy briefs; guidance on dissemination and policy engagement strategy; contribution to global communication and knowledge products; cross-regional knowledge-sharing sessions The requested support would help ensure that this study meets the highest international standards of scientific rigor, ethics, child safeguarding and policy relevance. desc: Mission to Kazakhstan
full: Programme Challenge Kazakhstan experienced major measles outbreaks in 2023 and 2024, with 15,111 and 28,147 reported cases, respectively. In response, the country strengthened routine immunization, conducted catch-up vaccination for children who missed scheduled doses, implemented supplementary immunization campaigns reaching 1.7 million children, and vaccinated 70,000 health workers. These efforts reduced reported cases to 4,250 in 2025. However, during the first six weeks of 2026, 3,012 measles cases were reported, indicating a rapid resurgence of transmission and the possible onset of a new outbreak. One possible contributing factor is that routine vaccination coverage may be overestimated. While administrative data report coverage above 95%, findings from the 2024 MICS survey indicate that only about 70% of children aged 24–35 months had received the MMR vaccine. This discrepancy suggests the presence of significant immunity gaps and highlights the need to assess immunization programme performance, surveillance systems, and outbreak response strategies to identify sustainable solutions for measles prevention and control. There is also a need to engage with national and subnational officials responsible for the immunization programme to better understand the factors contributing to recurring outbreaks, validate priority challenges, and identify technical assistance needs. These discussions will help define the scope and content of future support and inform how UNICEF and other international partners can most effectively assist the Government in strengthening immunization services, closing immunity gaps, and advancing measles elimination efforts.

desc: TA support in disability inclusion in earthquake response
full: Solicitud de apoyo técnico especializado para fortalecer la inclusión de la discapacidad en la respuesta y recuperación post terremoto en Venezuela Estimado equipo de Discapacidad Reciban un cordial saludo. La Oficina de UNICEF en Venezuela solicita el apoyo técnico de la División Global de Programas para fortalecer la integración de la inclusión de la discapacidad en la respuesta humanitaria y los procesos de recuperación tras los terremotos que afectaron al país el 24 de junio de 2026. Como parte del apoyo que UNICEF brinda a las poblaciones más afectadas, la oficina está promoviendo que las necesidades y derechos de los niños, niñas y adolescentes con discapacidad, así como de sus familias y cuidadores, sean abordados de manera sistemática en las evaluaciones, la planificación de la respuesta, la recuperación temprana y los procesos de reconstrucción. En este contexto, consideramos que el acompañamiento técnico especializado de la División Global de Programas contribuye y contribuirá significativamente a fortalecer la calidad, pertinencia e impacto de las intervenciones previstas. Agradeceríamos la posibilidad de contar con asistencia técnica remota en áreas prioritarias relacionadas con la acción humanitaria inclusiva, incluyendo la integración de la discapacidad en las evaluaciones de necesidades y recuperación, la transversalización de enfoques inclusivos en los distintos sectores de respuesta, el fortalecimiento de mecanismos accesibles de participación y rendición de cuentas, la coordinación con organizaciones de personas con discapacidad y la identificación de oportunidades para incorporar la inclusión de la discapacidad en las estrategias de recuperación y resiliencia. Asimismo, agradeceríamos explorar la factibilidad de una misión técnica a Venezuela por parte del punto focal regional de inclusión de la discapacidad, sujeta a disponibilidad y consideraciones operacionales. Consideramos que dicha misión podría aportar valor estratégico para fortalecer el apoyo a la oficina y sus socios, consolidar capacidades técnicas nacionales y contribuir a identificar oportunidades para una recuperación más inclusiva y equitativa. La Oficina de UNICEF en Venezuela valora altamente el liderazgo y la orientación técnica de la División Global de Programas y agradecerá cualquier apoyo que pueda brindarse para avanzar en una respuesta y recuperación centradas en los derechos de las personas con discapacidad, en consonancia con los compromisos institucionales de UNICEF y la Agenda 2030 para el Desarrollo Sostenible. Quedamos atentos a sus orientaciones y agradecemos de antemano su consideración. Atentamente, Mauricio Flores Colina Social Policy Officer UNICEF Venezuela

desc: UNICEF’s participation and CoE’s technical representation support in the 52nd COHSOD meeting
full: The Caribbean Community (CARICOM) Secretariat has convened the Fifty-Second Meeting of the Council for Human and Social Development (COHSOD) - Education on 12-13 August 2026 in Georgetown, Guyana. The CARICOM Secretariat extend ed an invitation for UNICEF to attend the Meeting. The main objective of the Meeting, which is being convened under the theme “ Educating for Life, Purpose, and Caribbean Progress, ” is to consider how to further optimise the region’s education system to equip learners with the competences that would enable individual and regional progress in a rapidly changing global environment. The CARICOM and COHSOD forum has consistently been an important platform for advancing the regional education transformation agenda , where UNICEF has supported discussions and technical exchanges around the CARICOM Human Resource Development (HRD) Strategy, foundational learning, literacy and numeracy, the Whole of Education Approach, teacher development, and broader education system transformation. Our participation in previous COHSOD meetings also helped strengthen UNICEF’s position as a trusted technical partner and contributed to the endorsement and follow-up of several regional education initiatives. Given this context, UNICEF’s participation and CoE’s technical representation support in the 52nd COHSOD meeting would provide an excellent opportunity to reinforce UNICEF’s support to CARICOM’s education agenda while also advancing conversations on adolescent learning, skills development, youth empowerment, and climate-responsive education.

Ministry of Health values highly the feedback provided and proposed improvements suggested. The Ministry of Health is currently in the process of finalizing the draft policy. In line with the recommendations already provided by Health GPD, MoH requested further technical assistance to finalize the policy and to formulate the necessary implementation architecture, governance arrangements and systems required for effective operationalization. Purpose of the technical assistance UNICEF Oman is requesting technical assistance from Health GPD to support the Ministry of Health in finalizing the National Child Health Policy. The support will focus on reviewing and addressing the technical recommendations already provided, strengthening the overall policy framing, and ensuring that the policy is accompanied by clear guidance on the systems, institutional arrangements and governance mechanisms required for implementation. Specific areas of support requested The requested technical assistance will include support to: • Review the consolidated comments and recommendations provided on the draft policy and advise on how they can be effectively addressed in the final version. • Provide technical guidance on the required system arrangements, coordination mechanisms, accountability structures and governance framework needed to support implementation of the policy. As a first step is to join a meeting with UNICEF Oman and the Ministry of Health to review comments, clarify key issues and agree on the next steps toward finalization. Proposed next step As an immediate next step, UNICEF Oman would appreciate the opportunity to convene a meeting with Health GPD colleagues to go through the comments and recommendations in detail, brainstorm the most practical way forward, and agree on the scope and modality of further technical assistance required to support MoH in finalizing the policy. Expected outputs The expected outputs of the requested technical assistance include: • Technical guidance on how to address the comments and recommendations provided on the draft National Child Health Policy. • Agreed next steps for supporting the Ministry of Health in finalizing the policy. • Recommendations on the system, institutional and governance arrangements required to enable effective implementation of the policy. • A strengthened final draft of the National Child Health Policy, reflecting Health GPD’s technical recommendations and aligned with UNICEF’s global guidance and good practice. Thank you for your continued support

T he high-level launch, jointly organized with the Government of Tajikistan, will bring together government counterparts, international financial institutions, development partners and UN agencies to position child protection as a shared development priority and build broad-based support for implementation of the newly adopted National Programme and its five-year Action Plan. As we shape the future Child Protection programme in the context of the new CPD, declining ODA, and an evolving development landscape, we would greatly benefit from technical guidance from the Child Protection Centre of Excellence to ensure alignment with UNICEF's corporate priorities, global child protection agenda, and emerging strategic directions. We are therefore requesting the engagement of the CoE to provide technical advice and strategic guidance on the design and positioning of the Child Protection programme and its structure within the new Country Programme Document. UNICEF Mexico seeks technical assistance to strengthen the implementation of its Climate Justice Agenda. The primary objective of this support is to provide specialized technical expertise on programmatic aspects of climate justice, while also supporting strategic donor engagement and resource mobilization efforts. The Climate Justice Agenda in Mexico is structured around two complementary workstreams: 1. Adolescent Development and Leadership Pillar This pillar aims to promote adolescents' legal awareness, knowledge, and empowerment, enabling them to advocate for and lead climate justice initiatives. The work focuses on strengthening youth participation, leadership, and agency in advancing climate justice and environmental rights. 2. Child Protection Pillar This pillar focuses on building the capacity of child protection stakeholders to understand and address the impacts of climate change on children and adolescents. It seeks to strengthen systems and professionals so they can effectively support climate justice outcomes and protect children's rights in the context of climate-related risks and vulnerabilities. Through this technical assistance, UNICEF Mexico aims to enhance the quality and effectiveness of its climate justice programming, strengthen evidence-based approaches, and expand partnerships and funding opportunities that support the achievement of its climate justice objectives.

desc: SRHR Routine Health Information Systems Assessment and Data Strengthening Support for Uganda
full: Background Uganda has made significant investments in strengthening its Routine Health Information Systems (RHIS), including the deployment of DHIS2 and digital health platforms to support data collection, reporting, and monitoring of health programmes. Despite these advances, challenges persist in the availability, quality, analysis, and use of Sexual and Reproductive Health and Rights (SRHR) data for programme planning, decision-making, accountability, and tracking progress towards national and global commitments. Under the European Union-funded RAISE SRHR Initiative, implemented through the 2gether 4 SRHR partnership of UNAIDS, UNFPA, UNICEF, and WHO, Uganda has been selected as one of the pilot countries to undertake a comprehensive assessment of its SRHR data ecosystem and develop a prioritized roadmap for strengthening routine health information systems. The initiative is guided by the guidelines for the use of routine health information data for SRHR programme decisions, which provide a structured framework for assessing and improving RHIS systems across four pillars: (i) RHIS system infrastructure and organization, (ii) data collection and quality, (iii) information use and decision-making, and (iv) indicators. To operationalize this initiative, the Ministry of Health, with support from UNICEF, WHO, UNFPA and UNAIDS, plans to convene a five-day national workshop bringing together key stakeholders from government, development partners, academia, civil society, among others to conduct a comprehensive RHIS assessment, identify gaps and bottlenecks, and develop a costed National SRHR data strengthening action plan. [ Purpose of the Request UNICEF Uganda seeks technical assistance from the Centre of Excellence to support the design, facilitation, and technical support of the national workshop and subsequent development of the costed evidence-based action plan for strengthening SRHR data systems in Uganda. Objectives of the Technical Assistance Support the Ministry of Health and partners to apply the RHIS assessment guidelines and tools to assess the status of Uganda’s SRHR data ecosystem across the four RHIS domains. Provide technical expertise to facilitate stakeholder review of assessment findings, identify key bottlenecks and strengths, and prioritize actions for strengthening SRHR data systems. Support the development of a realistic, costed, and implementable SRHR data strengthening action plan based on workshop outcomes and agreed priorities. Expected Deliverables The Centre of Excellence will support the following deliverables: Technical review and refinement of workshop methodology and materials. Technical guidance during assessment and prioritization exercises. Support to development of the costed national data strengthening action plan. Technical recommendations for implementation, support and monitoring under the RAISE SRHR project.

Technical Support to the Uzbekistan Country Office for the World Summit on Investing in Children's Wellbeing, Samarkand, October 2026 Short Description of the Request The Uzbekistan Country Office (CO) is seeking coordinated technical support from the Centres of Excellence (CoEs) for Child Protection and Migration, Economic and Social Policy, Early Childhood Development (ECD), Education and Health to support its role as co-organizer of the World Summit Investing in Children's Wellbeing: A Path Toward Sustainable and Just Development for Future Generations , to be held in Samarkand on 21-22 October 2026. The Summit represents a unique opportunity to position children's wellbeing as a central investment priority within national development agendas and international cooperation frameworks. Convened at a time when countries are addressing intersecting fiscal, demographic, climate and social challenges, the Summit is expected to bring together Heads of State, Ministers, development partners, international financial institutions, academia, civil society and young people to advance a shared agenda for strengthening outcomes for children through investment, systems strengthening and multi-sectoral action. The Summit will culminate in the adoption of the Samarkand Declaration on Investing in Children's Wellbeing, providing an opportunity to catalyze high-level commitments and shape future policy and financing priorities for children. The proposed programme includes an opening plenary and four thematic plenaries focused on child-sensitive social protection, integrated child protection systems, equitable and resilient child health systems, and investment in the early years through ECD and inclusive education. As a co-organizer, UNICEF has a unique opportunity to shape the global discourse on investing in children and ensure that Summit outcomes are technically robust, evidence-informed and aligned with UNICEF's strategic priorities. Given the Summit's inherently cross-sectoral nature, coordinated engagement across the relevant CoEs is critical. Support is requested to strengthen the technical quality, coherence and global relevance of the Summit's substantive content; identify transformative policy and financing solutions; showcase high-impact country experiences; support the engagement of influential speakers and thought leaders; and contribute to the development of a strong and actionable Samarkand Declaration. Beyond the event itself, the Summit offers an important platform to reinforce UNICEF's global thought leadership on investing in children, promote evidence-based approaches across sectors, and contribute to shaping a policy and financing agenda capable of influencing national reforms and investments well beyond 2026. Objectives / Expectations The technical assistance requested will support the CO to: Develop a coherent and compelling overarching narrative that positions investment in children's wellbeing as a foundation for sustainable, inclusive and equitable development. Ensure that the four thematic plenaries are underpinned by robust evidence, strong policy propositions, and actionable recommendations that can inform future national and global investments in children. Strengthen the opening plenary as a high-level platform that articulates the economic, social and human development case for investing in children and establishes a shared framework linking all thematic discussions. Curate a diverse set of innovative country experiences and influential leaders capable of demonstrating practical pathways for translating investment into measurable improvements in children's wellbeing at scale. Ensure that the Samarkand Declaration reflects global good practices, evidence-based policy priorities, and actionable commitments capable of driving progress at national and international levels. Strengthen UNICEF's visibility and thought leadership by positioning the organization at the centre of global discussions on financing, systems strengthening and integrated investments for children. Expected Deliverables A. Strategic Narrative and Positioning Technical inputs to the overarching Summit narrative, including key messages, framing and policy propositions that connect investments in social protection, child protection, health, ECD and education to improved outcomes for children. Technical inputs to the opening plenary, including evidence, framing questions, policy messages and recommendations for high-level speakers capable of advancing the Summit's central agenda. Technical review and substantive inputs to successive drafts of the Samarkand Declaration to ensure coherence, ambition, practicality and alignment with relevant global commitments and frameworks. B. Technical Content Development Technical review and refinement of the four thematic plenary concept notes, including objectives, policy questions, evidence, country examples and expected outcomes. Recommendations on innovative global and country-level experiences that demonstrate effective approaches to improving children's wellbeing through investment and systems strengthening. Recommended policy propositions and evidence-based messages that can inform discussions and Summit outcomes. C. Speaker Engagement and Quality Assurance Recommendations for high-level speakers, panellists and technical experts, including rationale linked to Summit objectives and thematic priorities. Targeted briefing points and technical inputs for selected speakers, where appropriate, to strengthen the quality and coherence of interventions. Cross-sectoral quality assurance of key Summit products and milestones to ensure consistency across the opening session, thematic plenaries, closing session and Samarkand Declaration. Proposed Approach The CO will lead and coordinate the substantive preparation process in collaboration with national counterparts, development partners and other Summit co-organizers. Designated focal points from the relevant CoEs will provide targeted strategic and technical support at key milestones throughout the preparation period. Support will include participation in agreed planning and technical discussions, review of draft materials, provision of evidence and policy inputs, recommendations on country experiences and speakers, and cross-sectoral quality assurance to support the development of a globally relevant and high-impact Summit agenda. Other Relevant Global Practices / Functions In addition to the identified CoEs, targeted engagement from ADAP and relevant partnerships, advocacy and communication functions would add value, particularly in relation to child and adolescent participation, strategic positioning, high-level stakeholder engagement, Summit communications and legacy planning. Strategic Accelerators The Summit contributes directly to key organizational accelerators, including: Financing for children and public investment in social sectors. Evidence generation and data-driven decision-making. Systems strengthening and integrated service delivery. Partnerships and global advocacy. Digital transformation and innovation where relevant. Child and adolescent participation in public policy dialogue. Results Expected By the conclusion of the technical assistance, the CO will have developed a coherent, evidence-based and globally informed substantive package for the World Summit, including a compelling overarching narrative, high-quality thematic plenaries, an impactful opening session, a strong roster of speakers and country examples, and a technically robust Samarkand Declaration. CoE engagement will strengthen the Summit's technical quality, policy relevance and cross-sectoral coherence, helping ensure that discussions generate practical solutions, actionable commitments and a compelling case for sustained investment in children's wellbeing. The Summit and its outcomes will contribute to elevating children's wellbeing within global development and financing discussions and reinforce UNICEF's leadership in advancing integrated investments and systems for children.

full: Technical Assistance for Advanced Analysis of SMART Survey Data and Triangulation with Other Nutrition Assessments UNICEF Syria Country Office is requesting technical assistance from the Center of Excellence (CoE) to conduct an in-depth comparative analysis of nutrition indicators from the 2023 and 2025 SMART surveys. The analysis will examine trends, disparities, and key changes in nutritional outcomes, with a particular focus on wasting and its potential drivers. The support will synthesize findings from SMART surveys and relevant complementary datasets into actionable evidence, strategic recommendations, and high-quality visualization products to inform programming, policy dialogue, and national efforts to reverse the trend of wasting prevalence. Objective 1: Generate a robust comparative analysis of nutrition trends Expected Results Comparative analysis of key nutrition indicators between SMART 2023 and SMART 2025. Identification of significant trends, changes, geographic disparities, and emerging concerns. Improved understanding of the evolution of wasting and other nutrition outcomes over time. Objective 2: Identify and interpret drivers of wasting Expected Results Examination of potential underlying causes and contributing factors using available survey and complementary assessment data. Identification of population groups and geographic areas at greatest risk. Enhanced evidence base for targeted programme interventions. Objective 3: Produce actionable evidence for decision-making Expected Results Clear synthesis of findings tailored to programme managers, policymakers, and partners. Evidence-based recommendations to inform strategic priorities, resource allocation, and programme adaptation. Practical guidance to support national efforts to reduce wasting prevalence. Objective 4: Improve communication and utilization of nutrition evidence Expected Results Development of user-friendly visual products and knowledge materials. Enhanced accessibility and uptake of findings among technical and non-technical audiences. Strengthened advocacy and decision-making through effective data visualization. Proposed Deliverables Deliverable 1: Comparative Analytical Report A comprehensive comparative analysis of SMART 2023 and SMART 2025 survey in addition to other surveys/assessment available, including: Trends and changes in key nutrition indicators. Geographic and population-level analysis. Identification of gaps and priority areas. Assessment of factors associated with wasting and other nutrition outcomes. Deliverable 2: Strategic Recommendations Brief A concise evidence-based brief that: Summarizes key findings. Identifies priority actions to address drivers of wasting. Provides strategic recommendations for UNICEF, government counterparts, and partners. Deliverable 3: Visualization and Communication Package A set of high-quality visualization products, including: Infographics. Data dashboards and/or scorecards. Presentation slides. Maps and trend visualizations. Deliverable 4: Executive Presentation of Findings Presentation to UNICEF Syria, government counterparts, and key stakeholders highlighting: Major findings. Programmatic implications. Recommended priority actions. Deliverable 5: Action-Oriented Guidance Note A practical guidance note outlining how findings can be translated into: Programme adjustments. Prioritization of interventions. Monitoring and targeting approaches. National actions to reverse wasting trends. Result for Children Generating actionable recommendations that accelerate efforts to reduce wasting and improve nutrition outcomes among the most vulnerable children and women in Syria.

desc: Support to Benin CO to prepare a proposal for the African Water Facility’s 2026 Grants, focusing on sanitation, climate resilience and systems strengthening
full: Following discussions held with the Direction Générale du Développement Urbain (DGDU) on last Friday, the Government of Benin expressed strong interest and a favorable opinion for submitting a proposal to the African Water Facility (AWF) 2026 Call for Proposals for Project Preparation Grants . The proposal should build on existing sector documents, notably the Programme National d'Investissement pour l’Hygiène et l’Assainissement de Base du Bénin (PNIHAB) and the climate rationale/ of the WASH sector in Benin . UNICEF Benin seeks technical assistance from the WASH Global Practice and relevant cross-sectoral experts to support the technical review and strengthening of the Government's proposed submission. The objective is to ensure alignment with AWF requirements, improve the investment readiness and bankability of the proposed intervention, and maximize opportunities to mobilize downstream financing for climate-resilient and inclusive WASH services. The AWF call specifically aims to support the preparation of high-impact water and sanitation investments that can attract future financing and accelerate sustainable sector development Additional Background / Context for the TA Hub Request Summary of consultation with DGDU (Friday): The DGDU expressed its interest and favorable opinion for a Benin submission to the AWF 2026 Call for Proposals. The Government and UNICEF country office intends to capitalize on existing sector planning and investment documents rather than develop a completely new concept. The proposal is expected to draw primarily on: The PNIHAB as the strategic investment framework for the sector ( 2026). The WASH sector climate rationale (2026) / highlighting climate vulnerabilities, resilience needs, and adaptation priorities. The national SMS capacity building roadmap (2024) Government counterparts requested support in reviewing the strategic positioning of the proposal and ensuring compliance with AWF preparation grant requirements. There is an opportunity to strengthen the proposal's climate resilience, investment readiness, financing strategy, and child-centred impact dimensions before submission.

desc: Support the strategic amplification of survey findings & and to document lessons learned&good practices from the survey process for replication and adaptation
full: UNICEF Malaysia has completed the National Youth Climate Change (NYCC) Survey, a nationwide survey capturing young people's experiences, perceptions and priorities related to climate change. The survey provides important evidence on how climate change is affecting young people in Malaysia and identifies opportunities to strengthen youth engagement in climate policy and action. Link to report: https://www.unicef.org/malaysia/reports/nurture-youth-create-change As UNICEF Malaysia moves into the dissemination phase, technical assistance is requested to support the strategic amplification of survey findings through communication channels and knowledge-sharing platforms, and to document lessons learned and good practices from the survey process for replication and adaptation by other country offices.

desc: Request guidance, review and advisory support to an assessment study on SRSP & climate-related, environmental, economic and other shocks
full: UNICEF Malaysia is supporting efforts to strengthen the evidence base on shock-responsive social protection (SRSP) in Malaysia. An assessment study is being undertaken to examine the extent to which existing social protection systems can anticipate, respond to and recover from climate-related, environmental, economic and other shocks, with particular attention to impacts on children and vulnerable households. To ensure the assessment reflects global good practices and provides actionable recommendations, UNICEF Malaysia seeks technical assistance and strategic advice throughout the study process. In line with UNICEF's Technical Assistance approach, this request is for expert guidance, review and advisory support.

desc: Technical advice on study design and methodology in the initial phases, and support for analysis and review of policy recommendations in later phases
full: UNICEF Malaysia is undertaking a study to understand how rising temperatures and extreme heat are affecting children. The study will examine children's exposure and vulnerability to heat, impacts on health and wellbeing, effects on learning and daily life, and whether existing policies and response measures adequately protect children. Findings will support child-responsive heat policies, school adaptation measures and climate resilience planning. This will be a 2 year study with an RFP to be prepared for recruitment of a consultancy firm. TA assistance is requested for technical advise on study design and methodology in the initial phases, and support for analysis and review of policy recommendations in later phases of the study.

desc: Request in-country mission to strengthen strategic positioning, knowledge exchange &cross-sectoral collaboration on climate, environment and DRR
full: UNICEF Malaysia is seeking technical assistance from the Centre of Excellence (CoE) through an in-country mission to strengthen strategic positioning, knowledge exchange and cross-sectoral collaboration on climate, environment and disaster risk reduction (CEDRR). The mission would support external engagement with partners and provide an opportunity to align priorities and approaches for the 2026-2027 programme cycle. Issmail Nnafie, CoE focal point for Malaysia has been identified to join in this mission. Scope of Technical Assistance Requested 1. Keynote participation at the Environmental Education Conference, Sarawak (27-28 October) Serve as a keynote speaker at the Environmental Education Conference. Share global and regional perspectives on climate change, environmental education and children's rights. Engage with government, academia, civil society and development partners to promote child-centred approaches to environmental education. 2. Strategic planning discussions with the Climate Team Facilitate discussions with the UNICEF Malaysia climate team to review progress, emerging priorities and opportunities. Provide technical advice on strategic direction and programme prioritization for 2026-2027. Share regional and global good practices relevant to Malaysia's climate, environment and DRR agenda. 3. Cross-sectoral discussions within UNICEF Malaysia Meet with sector leads across the Country Office to explore opportunities for integrating climate, environment and DRR considerations across programmes. Identify potential areas for joint programming and collaboration. Provide strategic guidance on strengthening climate mainstreaming and cross-sectoral approaches.

desc: Technical Review of Malawi WASH Accounts Products (Full Report, Policy Brief and Results Brief)
full: Technical Review of Malawi WASH Accounts Products (Full Report, Policy Brief and Results Brief) In late 2024 UNICEF and WHO along with Ministry of Finance and Ministry of Water & Sanitation commissioned a WASH accounts study in Malawi as first WASH accounts study of its kind. The work is now reaching finalization. Extensive support has already been provided by WHO HQ WASH accounts team. UNICEF Malawi is seeking rapid technical support to undertake a quality assurance review of the Malawi WASH Accounts products, including the full WASH Accounts report, policy brief, and results brief. The review should assess the technical robustness of the analysis, consistency of key messages, alignment with TrackFin/WASH Accounts methodologies, policy relevance, and suitability for high-level government engagement. The request is time-sensitive. The Ministry of Finance is currently advancing finalization of the products and stakeholder discussions are scheduled for 19 August 2026. To inform these engagements, consolidated technical feedback is requested by 17 August 2026 where possible. Objectives / Expected Results Strengthen Technical Quality Verify the technical soundness of the analysis, conclusions and recommendations. Assess consistency with WASH Accounts and TrackFin methodologies. Identify any methodological gaps, assumptions, or areas requiring clarification. Enhance Policy Relevance Ensure findings and recommendations are actionable for the Government of Malawi, particularly the Ministry of Finance, Ministry of Water and Sanitation, and development partners. Strengthen messages related to sustainable financing, equity, efficiency and financing gaps. Improve Communication Products Review the policy brief and results brief to ensure clear, concise and compelling communication of key findings. Confirm consistency of messages, data and recommendations across all products. Strengthen Child and SDG Impact Messaging Identify opportunities to strengthen the linkage between WASH financing, child outcomes, climate resilience, equity and achievement of SDG 6. Highlight implications for accelerating results for children through improved financing decisions. Expected Deliverables Technical Review Matrix Consolidated comments and recommendations on the full report, policy brief and results brief. Prioritization of critical, recommended and optional revisions. Annotated Documents Marked-up versions of the report and briefs using track changes and comments. High-Level Reviewer Note 2-3 page summary highlighting: key strengths; critical issues requiring attention before publication; recommendations for strengthening policy uptake and advocacy. Optional Debrief Session One virtual meeting with UNICEF Malawi and key partners to discuss findings and agree on final revisions before the 19 August discussions.

offer: Programme Offer to Governments and other Stakeholders
full: Technical Support from the UNICEF GPD for Post-Summit Implementation of the Dakar Declaration in Ghana Following the formal receipt of the Dakar Girls' Summit Declaration by the Governement of Ghana- Hon. Minister for Gender, Children and Social Protection, Dr. Agnes Naa Momo Lartey, on behalf of the President of the Republic of Ghana, the country has a significant opportunity to advance a comprehensive national agenda for adolescent girls. However, translating the commitments of the Dakar Declaration into measurable results presents several challenges. Existing interventions for adolescent girls remain fragmented across sectors, with limited coordination, inconsistent service delivery standards, and insufficient mechanisms for monitoring and accountability. In addition, Ghana currently lacks a nationally endorsed Minimum Service Package for Adolescents that defines the essential services and support that every adolescent girl should receive across health, nutrition, education, child protection, social protection, mental health, and economic empowerment. As the Government develops the National Adolescent Minimum Service Package, there is a need for high-level technical support from GPD to strengthen policy coherence, develop an integrated and costed implementation framework, establish a National Minimum Service Package for Adolescent, enhance multisectoral coordination, and build robust accountability and results-monitoring systems. Such support will be critical to ensuring that the Dakar Declaration commitments are translated into a coordinated, scalable, and sustainable national programme that delivers equitable outcomes for all adolescent girls, particularly those who are most vulnerable and marginalized.

desc: BVD response - Ebola research in Rwanda
full: the key question is : What’s going on in terms of Ebola Research pillar in other countries (than Rwanda) I understand not every country has a formal research pillar to start with… or even if they do, that it is not the most active pillar of the response… In our case, in Rwanda, the pillar 7 th is on Research and Strategic information and include a mix-and-match of activities which are really research related, and other which are more the “logistics” behind research (RNEC Approval, airtime for researchers, etc). Very few of those researches appear as partially funded for now. Only 2 actually. We had several meetings without Gov representatives… In the last meeting (last week), the government interest (at least from the focal point/lead) seems heavily focused on clinical trials, and epidemiological data, and he seems eager to “publish” … but currently, there is no case management data in Rwanda – only contact follow up data. We have discussed the attached powerpoint about having the protocols in Place (which I believe you or Edna may have contributed to) We (UNICEF) are also looking at what “other research” aka non-clinical ones – could look like, highlighted in red below (behavioural, IPC practices, etc) or even on the economic impacts of the borders restrictions, and also documentation of best practices or lesson learne d (potentially after action review, or evaluation of the response even). Waste water management, we have a proposal in the pipeline with the US Gov, but not sure where it is going at the moment… But all of these seems to be gaining little traction, despite some being clearly listed in the Gov plan… I would like to know what’s ongoing in the other countries to also see how to avoid duplication, and maybe work in synergies and how small pieces of learning (rather than big , expensive RCT /clinical trials) are being compiled.

desc: Request for Technical Assistance for the AI for Teachers Design Workshop (25-29 August 2026)
full: Subject: Request for Technical Assistance for the AI for Teachers Design Workshop (25-29 August 2026) Dear UNICEF Centres of Excellence and Global Learning Innovation Hub, The UNICEF Ghana Country Office respectfully requests technical assistance from the UNICEF Centres of Excellence and the Global Learning Innovation Hub to support the AI for Teachers Design Workshop , scheduled to take place from 25-29 August 2026 in Ghana. This workshop serves as the inaugural co-design convening for the AI-Powered Teacher Companion initiative. It will bring together key stakeholders, including the Ministry of Education, Ghana Education Service (GES), CENDLOS, Colleges of Education, teachers and teacher educators, technical and safeguarding experts, UNICEF representatives, and implementation partners , to develop a shared understanding of teachers' needs and collaboratively define the strategic direction of the Companion. The workshop will focus on exploring how the AI-Powered Teacher Companion can effectively support teaching and learning processes, including lesson planning, assessment, learner remediation, teaching practicum, continuous professional development, and classroom practice . In addition, the convening aims to generate the critical design inputs required for platform configuration, deployment planning, user onboarding, responsible and safe use, and broader implementation strategies. Given the expertise of the Centres of Excellence and the Global Learning Innovation Hub in digital learning innovation, human-centred design, and AI-enabled education solutions, we would greatly appreciate your technical support in facilitating the workshop, guiding the co-design process, and contributing to the development of a robust and contextually relevant AI-Powered Teacher Companion for Ghana. We look forward to your positive consideration of this request and to collaborating closely to advance innovative and equitable learning solutions for teachers and learners in Ghana. Teams Requested Education Innovation Teacher Professional Development **********Draft Training Plan attached for reference

desc: Technical Support on Integration of Child- and Youth-Sensitive Priorities into NDC 3.0 Processes
full: Assign CoE climate - Maria Osbeck Request for Technical Support on Integration of Child- and Youth-Sensitive Priorities into NDC 3.0 Processes Under the Climate BMI, UNICEF supported the integration of child- and youth-sensitive priorities into the third generation of nationally determined contributions (NDC 3.0) across the five Central Asian countries. The work aimed to strengthen recognition of children and young people as a climate-vulnerable group and to position child-responsive investments within national climate commitments and implementation frameworks. Technical support included policy analysis, stakeholder consultations, development of child-sensitive narrative and sectoral content, identification and costing of priority investments, and engagement with national NDC drafting processes. Across the region, UNICEF-supported inputs resulted in the inclusion of child- and youth-responsive climate actions spanning education, health, WASH, social protection, youth engagement, climate-resilient infrastructure, and disaster risk reduction. The process also generated a regional pipeline of child-sensitive climate investment opportunities estimated at approximately USD 6.9 billion across the five countries. As of June 2026, Kazakhstan, Kyrgyzstan, and Uzbekistan have formally submitted updated NDCs to the UNFCCC with UNICEF-supported child-sensitive provisions reflected in the final documents. Drafting and/or finalization processes in Tajikistan and Turkmenistan remain ongoing, with UNICEF continuing to provide technical support as requested by national counterparts and country offices.

desc: Technical assistance for scaling existing country office engagement and positioning with Gvt and donors
full: Implemented in partnership with the Ministry of Water Resources and Irrigation, Ministry of Education, International Fund for Saving the Aral Sea (IFAS), regional authorities, and with financial support from AFD, UKO water education programme has reached more than 67,000 children and adolescents, trained 1,773 teachers, established 55 school water clubs, developed over 570 educational resources, and introduced practical water-saving solutions across 55 schools. The initiative has recently received high-level recognition at the National Water Saving Coordination Council and has been positively acknowledged by the Minister of Water Resources and Irrigation as a promising platform for future scale-up. More about the programme is available here: More Than 100,000 Children in Kazakhstan and Uzbekistan Gain Water Conservation Knowledge and Skills As Kazakhstan faces growing water stress resulting from climate change, glacier retreat, increasing demand for water resources, and heightened risks to water security, the Government is prioritizing digitalization, artificial intelligence, satellite monitoring, automated water accounting, and other smart technologies to improve water management efficiency and forecasting. At the same time, major international financial institutions, including the World Bank, Asian Development Bank, and Islamic Development Bank, are strengthening their investments in the water sector.UNICEF Kazakhstan sees a strategic opportunity to align its water education programme with these national priorities and transform schools into hubs for innovation, data collection, citizen science, and climate action. The programme seeks to move beyond awareness-raising toward a comprehensive model that combines infrastructure, technology, education, behavioral change, and youth engagement to support sustainable water management. The KCO has also engaged youth through U report: Ю-Репорт Kazakhstan

desc: Request for Technical Support on Development of the Regional Green School Platform (RGSP) Framework and Regional Cooperation Mechanism
full: Assign CoE climate - Maria Osbeck Request for Technical Support on Development of the Regional Green School Platform (RGSP) Framework and Regional Cooperation Mechanism The Regional Green School Platform (RGSP) was developed under the Climate BMI as a regional mechanism to support climate-resilient, low-carbon, and child-centred education infrastructure and systems across Central Asia. The platform emerged from consultations with Country Offices, government counterparts, technical experts, and development partners, and was further advanced through preparations for the Regional Ecological Summit (RES). The RGSP is envisioned as a regional coordination and fund mobilisation mechanism that supports participating countries through development of common standards, technical guidance, knowledge exchange, project preparation, and resource mobilisation. During the reporting period, UNICEF coordinated the development of the RGSP concept, governance proposals, implementation roadmap, partnership outreach materials, and investment rationale. The platform received formal endorsement from Ministries of Education and Ministries of Environment/Ecology from the five Central Asian countries during the High-Level Session on Green Schools at RES in April 2026. The RGSP was subsequently reflected in the RES Declaration, providing a strong political foundation for future regional collaboration. A draft 6–12 month operationalisation roadmap (action plan), 10-year Roadmap and 4-page Concept Note has been developed and circulated with COs for review. Initial engagement has also been initiated with potential financing and technical partners, including the Islamic Development Bank, GPE and other development partners.

desc: CPD development TA - Kenya
full: CPD 2027-2032 development support (multi-sector) Request type: Technical assistance from the Centre of Excellence for the development of the UNICEF Kenya Country Programme Document 2027–2032. Background: UNICEF Kenya is initiating development of its next Country Programme Document for 2027–2032. The process will require focused technical support at key moments, including strategic framing, theory of change and strategy development, and review of draft programme documentation. The objective is to ensure that the new CPD is evidence-informed, strategically coherent, aligned with national priorities and UNICEF corporate guidance, and responsive to emerging risks and opportunities for children and adolescents in Kenya. The Kenya CPD will be approved at the June 2027 Board. Requested Support 1. Analysis, Theory of Change and strategy development — early to mid-September We request targeted CoE support for theory of change and strategy development for selected key themes and sectors where additional technical guidance would be most useful. This support would involve a few days of engagement with UNICEF Kenya sector teams in late August to mid-September, helping teams translate the framing analysis into clearer programme choices, causal pathways, strategic shifts and results logic. This work involves initial conversations with the prorgamme teams, then in person participation as follows: Wednesday 9 Sep – Education Thursday 10 Sep – CSD 1 (health, nutrition, WASH) Friday 11 Sep (half day) – CSD 2 (health, nutrition, WASH) Monday 14 Sep – CP Tuesday 15 Sep – SP Level of effort: several days of engagement with selected sector teams. 2. Strategic consultation meeting — 30 September We request CoE support for a half-day strategic consultation meeting in late September (30 th ), to review the evolving situation of children and adolescents in Kenya and identify the key strategic issues that should shape the CPD. This is with the resident Coordinator and his office, some UN agencies, and RO and COE staff. We would ideally like several COE technical colleagues to support the discussion, covering: social policy; strategic planning; climate and resilience; youth and adolescents; health; education; and child protection. In-person participation would be preferred where feasible, with remote participation possible for some sectors, such as education and child protection. Level of effort: half-day meeting, with preparation time as needed. 3. Document review and quality assurance — timing to be confirmed, likely late September into October. We also request technical review of draft CPD-related materials (e.g. Explanatory Notes) across UNICEF Kenya’s six programme sectors and cross-cutting issues, including whether sector strategies, theories of change, explanatory notes and related inputs are technically sound, coherent across sectors, and adequately reflect priorities such as equity, gender, disability inclusion, climate resilience, adolescent and youth engagement, and systems strengthening. Level of effort: approximately two to three days per reviewer or technical area, depending on the number of documents and depth of comments required. This is created for Mahboob Bajwa (Dep Rep Programmes); but would need to loop in James Hedges jhedges@unicef.org (Chief PME) as well as ESARO Chief PPM Behzad Noubary <bnoubary@unicef.org>.

desc: Climate Collaboration for Children (CC4C) Youth Engagement in Climate Action
full: Climate Collaboration for Children (CC4C) Youth Engagement in Climate Action: TA request from Kenya CO. The focal point for this initiative in Climate CoE is David Knaute. As confirmed with the Climate CoE, this is an exceptional TA request which includes a financial support. Kenya CO does not require a non-financial support under this TA. Kenya CO requests USD 10,000 to support the scale-up of youth-led land restoration under Green Rising Phase II in Kenya. Specifically, the TA will support the distribution and planting of indigenous tree and mangrove seedlings to young people through school environmental clubs, Kenya Scouts groups, and youth-led tree nurseries across Embu, Machakos, and Kilifi counties, covering both forestry/agroforestry and coastal landscape restoration. The activity will strengthen youth leadership in practical land restoration and sustainable landscape management, while generating evidence and a short impact story video to document the powerful peer-led model and replicable approaches to further scale youth-led land restoration and environmental stewardship in Kenya and beyond.

desc: TA to Advance Child-Responsive L&D Policy and Programming in South Africa
full: Technical Assistance to Advance Child-Responsive Loss and Damage Policy and Programming in South Africa. Provide technical assistance to support UNICEF South Africa and the Government of South Africa in advancing a child-responsive approach to addressing climate-related loss and damage. The support will strengthen national understanding of the Loss and Damage agenda, identify opportunities for accessing technical and financial support mechanisms (including the Santiago Network, Country Support System, FRLD, and related climate finance channels), and support the development of a strategic roadmap for integrating loss and damage considerations into national institutional climate frameworks, systems and planning processes.
