TA Request Title Technical Assistance to Strengthen Child Protection Financing and Public Financial Management in Türkiye Background and Rationale Following the Child Protection Public Financial Management (CP-PFM) training conducted in June 2026, UNICEF Türkiye Country Office (TCO) seeks to build on the momentum generated and translate learning into a strategic agenda for strengthening child protection financing in Türkiye. While significant progress has been made in strengthening child protection systems, there is a need to further understand how public resources are allocated, executed, tracked and monitored across child protection interventions, and to identify opportunities to improve the adequacy, efficiency, equity and sustainability of financing for child protection services. Strengthening child protection financing is critical to ensuring that prevention and response services are adequately resourced, prioritized within national and local budgets, and positioned to achieve sustainable results for vulnerable children and families. To support this process, TCO is requesting technical assistance from a Social Policy/Child Protection Financing expert to help identify priorities, scope opportunities for engagement, and develop a roadmap for advancing child protection financing and CP-PFM work in Türkiye. Objective of the Technical Assistance To provide technical support to UNICEF Türkiye in identifying strategic priorities, entry points and a roadmap for strengthening child protection financing and public financial management, building on the outcomes of the June 2026 CP-PFM training and contributing to more effective, equitable and sustainable financing of child protection services. Expected Results A clear assessment of opportunities and priority areas for strengthening child protection financing and public financial management in Türkiye. Enhanced understanding of the child protection financing landscape, including existing financing mechanisms, budget allocation processes and potential gaps or bottlenecks. Identification of strategic entry points for UNICEF engagement with relevant government counterparts, particularly the Ministry of Family and Social Services and other financing and planning actors. A proposed roadmap for advancing child protection financing work, including short-, medium- and longer-term priorities. Strengthened collaboration between Child Protection and Social Policy teams to advance an integrated approach to child protection financing and systems strengthening. Proposed Deliverables Deliverable 1: Review and Scoping Review available documentation, including outputs from the June 2026 CP-PFM training. Conduct consultations with UNICEF Child Protection and Social Policy teams and relevant government counterparts. Map existing child protection financing initiatives, opportunities and challenges. Deliverable 2: Child Protection Financing Scoping Note Develop a concise scoping note outlining: Current child protection financing context. Key financing challenges and opportunities. Potential areas for UNICEF technical engagement. International good practices relevant to the Türkiye context. Deliverable 3: Strategic Recommendations Identify priority actions to strengthen child protection financing and public financial management. Recommend approaches to improve budget adequacy, efficiency, equity, transparency and sustainability. Explore opportunities for strengthening expenditure tracking, budget analysis and financing for preventive child protection services. Deliverable 4: Roadmap for Engagement Develop a roadmap outlining: Strategic objectives. Priority interventions. Key partners and stakeholders. Proposed milestones and next steps. Opportunities for joint Child Protection and Social Policy programming. TA Hub Outcome Statement UNICEF Türkiye has a clear strategic direction and roadmap for strengthening child protection financing and public financial management, enabling more sustainable, equitable and effective investment in child protection systems and services for children and families.

North Macedonia is currently facing a number of incidents of violence in schools, including several cases involving severe forms of violence. These developments have increased public concern and highlighted the need to further strengthen both preventive measures and response mechanisms within the education system. The Ministry of Education and Science, together with other relevant institutions, is exploring opportunities to enhance school-based violence prevention, early detection, reporting, referral, and response systems. UNICEF North Macedonia is seeking technical support to better understand international good practices and innovative approaches that have been successfully implemented in other countries to address violence against children in and around schools. Particular interest is placed on approaches that promote integrated and child-centered protection systems, strengthen collaboration between education and child protection sectors, and support schools in creating safe and inclusive learning environments. The request also comes in the context of exploring potential opportunities to support the Government in developing future interventions and investment proposals aimed at strengthening violence prevention and response systems. UNICEF will be engaging with the Ministry of Education and Science and the Ministry of Social Policy, Demography and Youth to identify priority areas for action and possible entry points for strengthening school-based child protection mechanisms. The technical assistance is expected to provide: Examples of effective school-based violence prevention programmes and Safe to Learn initiatives implemented in other countries; Innovative approaches for prevention, early identification, reporting, referral, and case management of violence affecting children; Lessons learned and evidence on what works in strengthening school safety and child protection systems; Examples of cross-sectoral coordination mechanisms between education, social welfare, child protection, and other relevant sectors; Recommendations on potential interventions that could be adapted to the North Macedonian context. The objective of this support is to inform ongoing discussions with government counterparts and contribute to the development of more effective and evidence-based approaches for preventing and responding to violence against children in schools.

desc: Request technical assistance to conduct an independent review of a collaborative design initiative for HPV vaccination
full: Request technical assistance to conduct an independent review of a collaborative design initiative for HPV vaccination (VPH) currently being implemented in Venezuela in partnership with a private sector company. The review should assess the design process, methodology, quality of products and interventions developed, application of human-centered design principles, community participation mechanisms, alignment with UNICEF Social and Behaviour Change (SBC) standards, and the initiative's potential to contribute to intended outcomes related to HPV vaccination uptake among children, adolescents, caregivers and communities. The review is expected to provide actionable recommendations to strengthen the design, implementation, scalability, sustainability and measurement of results of the initiative. Objectives / Expectations Conduct an independent technical review of the collaborative design process and methodology used throughout the initiative. Assess the extent to which human-centered design and participatory approaches have been applied and whether target audiences have been meaningfully engaged in the design and testing process. Review the quality, relevance, cultural appropriateness, inclusiveness and usability of the products, tools and communication materials developed. Evaluate the integration of SBC principles and behavioural insights within the initiative and its alignment with UNICEF’s SBC framework and global guidance. Identify strengths, gaps, risks and opportunities to improve the effectiveness of the initiative in addressing barriers and drivers related to HPV vaccination. Assess the potential for scale-up, sustainability and adaptation of the initiative in other contexts. Provide recommendations to strengthen monitoring, learning and evidence generation to measure outcomes and document lessons learned. Expected Deliverables Inception Meeting and Review Plan Review methodology, timeline and key assessment criteria agreed with UNICEF and partners. Technical Review Report Assessment of the collaborative design process. Analysis of human-centered design and community engagement approaches. Review of alignment with SBC and behavioural science principles. Identification of strengths, gaps and recommendations. Review of Project Outputs Technical feedback on communication materials, prototypes, engagement tools, campaigns, user journeys and other products generated through the initiative. Recommendations and Improvement Roadmap Prioritized actions to strengthen quality, implementation, scale-up and sustainability. Final Presentation Presentation and discussion of findings and recommendations with UNICEF and relevant stakeholders. desc: WHO–UNICEF–Gavi Joint Mission and Immunization Programme Strengthening Support for Cameroon
full: Technical Support for WHO-UNICEF-Gavi Joint Mission to Cameroon (24-28 August 2026): Participated in a joint mission to monitor preparedness for the Measles-Rubella (MR) campaign and the HPV Multi-Age Cohort (MAC) introduction, and provided support for the Gavi 6.0 application process following receipt of the country's cash confirmation letter. Short Description of the Request Provision of technical and coordination support to facilitate the WHO-UNICEF-Gavi joint mission to Cameroon from 24-28 August 2026. The mission aims to strengthen alignment among partners and the Ministry of Public Health on key immunization priorities, including Gavi 6.0 vaccine and cash support allocations, reprogramming of Health System Strengthening (HSS) funds, preparedness for the September 2026 Measles-Rubella (MR) campaign and October 2026 HPV Multi-Age Cohort (MAC) introduction, finalization of HPV vaccine transfer arrangements from Burkina Faso, and follow-up on ongoing programmatic priorities including audit recommendations and Cameroon’s replenishment contribution. Objectives / Expected Results Objective 1. Strengthen partner understanding of the Expanded Programme on Immunization (EPI/PEV) in Cameroon Expected Result: WHO, UNICEF, and Gavi mission participants have a shared understanding of the country's immunization landscape, key stakeholders, achievements, challenges, and priorities. Objective 2. Facilitate strategic discussions on Gavi 6.0 support and HSS reprogramming Expected Result: Consensus reached on vaccine and cash budget allocations under Gavi 6.0 and key directions for reprogramming HSS support to address priority immunization system gaps. Objective 3. Review readiness for upcoming immunization interventions Expected Result: Critical actions identified and agreed upon to ensure successful implementation of the September 2026 MR campaign and October 2026 HPV MAC introduction. Objective 4. Support resolution of operational and programmatic issues Expected Result: Clear roadmap and responsibilities agreed for HPV vaccine transfer from Burkina Faso to Cameroon, implementation of audit recommendations, and follow-up of other key immunization workstreams. Objective 5. Strengthen coordination and accountability among partners Expected Result: Agreed mission recommendations, action points, timelines, and responsible parties documented and endorsed by key stakeholders. Key Deliverables Mission briefing package prepared and shared with mission participants, including: Overview of PEV performance and key indicators. Stakeholder mapping. Summary of ongoing Gavi-supported activities and priorities. Facilitation of mission meetings and field discussions with government and partner stakeholders. Technical review of Gavi 6.0 allocations and HSS reprogramming options , including documentation of agreed priorities and next steps. Assessment of preparedness for the MR campaign and HPV MAC introduction , with a list of identified gaps, risks, and mitigation actions. Documentation of agreed arrangements for HPV vaccine transfer from Burkina Faso to Cameroon, including operational next steps and responsible parties. Mission report summarizing: Key findings. Agreements reached. Recommendations. Action tracker with timelines and responsible stakeholders. Post-mission follow-up matrix to monitor implementation of agreed actions related to: HSS reprogramming. Campaign preparedness. HPV vaccine transfer. Audit recommendations. Other priority immunization workstreams. Suggested TA Outcome Statement Enhanced alignment between the Ministry of Public Health, WHO, UNICEF, and Gavi on strategic immunization priorities, resulting in clear next steps for Gavi 6.0 implementation, HSS reprogramming, campaign readiness, and strengthening of Cameroon’s immunization programme performance.

UNICEF Cox's Bazar Field Office in Bangladesh is currently in the process of implementing a SMART survey in Cox Bazar refugee camps and Bashan Char. ACF Canada has been hired to conduct the survey on behalf of UNICEF/Nutrition sector. The main aim of the survey is to generate high-quality, representative data on the nutritional status of children and other key indicators to inform programming, monitoring, and evidence-based decision-making. While the Nutrition team is able to provide oversight to the entire survey process, the team is currently operating with limited human resources and is simultaneously managing multiple ongoing programmatic and sector priorities. Given the complexity and technical rigor required for the SMART survey, we are requesting Technical Assistance (TA) from the Centre of Excellence to support the UNICEF team in ensuring we have accurate and quality survey results that will be acceptable by all stakeholders. The TA will ensure adherence to global SMART standards and UNICEF quality assurance requirements throughout all phases of the survey. The expert will provide critical support in methodology/protocol review, review of the questionnaire, participate in training of data collectors, data collection supervision, data validation, analysis, and review of all stated survey deliverables and preparation for dissemination.

Technical Assistance Request: Review and Strategic Positioning of the SRSG-VAC Visit and Associated Technical Discussions UNICEF Sierra Leone seeks technical support to review and strengthen the strategic framing, objectives, messaging, advocacy opportunities, and follow-up actions related to the forthcoming visit of the Special Representative of the Secretary-General on Violence Against Children (SRSG-VAC) in 2026. The support would help ensure that the visit contributes to accelerated action on ending violence against children, strengthens national child protection systems, influences policy and financing discussions, and positions Sierra Leone to advance commitments ahead of global EVAC platforms. Proposed Objectives Strengthen the strategic positioning of the visit Ensure alignment with global EVAC priorities, UNICEF Child Protection Strategy, and national child protection reforms. Also possible follow-up on the DWG 2025 Identify opportunities for the visit to catalyze policy, systems, and financing commitments. Maximize advocacy and influence opportunities Refine key messages and priority asks for Government, development partners, civil society, and donors. Identify opportunities to increase political visibility and accountability for ending violence against children. Accelerate implementation of child protection reforms Link the visit to key implementation priorities, including the Child Rights Act 2025, child protection systems strengthening, social service workforce development, and child participation. Expected Results Clearly articulated strategic objectives and desired outcomes for the visit. High-level advocacy messages tailored to key stakeholders. Identification of concrete commitments, policy opportunities, and financing asks. A set of recommended follow-up actions and accountability mechanisms. Enhanced positioning of Sierra Leone as a country advancing implementation of EVAC commitments. Potential Deliverable Technical Review Note available for sharing with SRSG office, including support for discussions on DWG

Strengthening Integrated Approaches to Address Harmful Practices: Exploring the Interlinkages between Female Genital Mutilation, Child Marriage, and Trafficking in Persons Request Description UNICEF Sierra Leone seeks technical assistance to review and strengthen the conceptual framework, evidence base, and strategic positioning of emerging work on harmful practices, with a specific focus on the interlinkages between female genital mutilation (FGM), child marriage, and trafficking in persons (TIP). While these issues are often addressed through separate policy, legal, and programme frameworks, there is increasing recognition that they share common drivers, vulnerabilities, social norms, gender inequalities, protection risks, and implementation challenges. An integrated understanding of these interlinkages could strengthen prevention, protection, and response efforts while supporting more coherent programming, advocacy, and policy engagement. The request would support UNICEF Sierra Leone in identifying opportunities to move towards a more integrated harmful practices agenda that advances children's rights, addresses underlying risk factors, and accelerates progress towards the elimination of harmful practices and violence against children.

I would appreciate technical support in developing a comprehensive strategy to engage children in Panorama Prison in North East Syria through Child Protection activities, particularly recreational interventions. As this will be the first Child Protection engagement with these children, it is essential to establish a structured, safe, and context-sensitive approach that promotes trust-building, meaningful participation, and psychosocial well-being while adhering to Child Protection principles and standards. The strategy should include a clear framework for initiating engagement with the children, as well as a detailed plan for the initial sessions, outlining their objectives, content, methodologies, and facilitation approaches. Given the highly sensitive nature of working with children in this setting, the proposed approach should be technically robust, trauma-informed, and grounded in best practices to ensure that interventions are safe, age-appropriate, and responsive to the children's needs, vulnerabilities, and circumstances.

desc: Child-responsive Climate Change Policy - Sokoto State
full: UNICEF Nigeria seeks technical assistance to support the Government of Sokoto State in developing and finalizing a comprehensive, evidence-based, and child-responsive Climate Change Policy. The assignment will provide strategic and technical guidance to state government institutions and stakeholders to strengthen climate governance, integrate climate resilience into key social sectors, and align the policy with national climate commitments, including Nigeria's Climate Change Act, National Adaptation Plan, Nationally Determined Contributions (NDCs), and relevant state development priorities. The process will ensure that the policy reflects the needs of children and vulnerable communities and provides a practical framework for climate adaptation, mitigation, resilience, and sustainable development. The technical assistance will aim to: Support the review and assessment of existing climate-related policies, strategies, plans, and institutional arrangements within Sokoto State and identify key policy gaps and opportunities. Integrate child-centred climate resilience considerations into priority sectors, including WASH, health, education, nutrition, social protection, agriculture, disaster risk management, and environmental sustainability. Expected Results Upon completion of the assignment: A technically sound and government-endorsed Climate Change Policy for Sokoto State is finalized. Climate risks affecting children, youth, and vulnerable populations are adequately reflected in the policy. Priority adaptation and resilience actions are identified across key sectors. Institutional roles and coordination mechanisms for climate action are clearly defined. Stakeholders demonstrate increased understanding and ownership of the policy. An implementation and monitoring framework is established to support operationalization of the policy. Sokoto state has established a technical working group (TWG) and initial evidence synthesis work is led by this TWG. An expert guidance and high-level technical support is needed to ensure that evidence synthesis and policy drafted by the TWG meets quality standards and child focus.

desc: AI, Innovation Portfolio and Ecosystem
full: UNICEF Rwanda is developing a coordinated agenda on child-centred digital transformation, artificial intelligence (AI) and technology for development, in close collaboration with the Ministry of ICT and Innovation (MINICT) and relevant national institutions. The initiative includes development of a UNICEF-MINICT joint workplan, prioritization of AI and digital opportunities, strengthening national child online protection efforts, and building UNICEF Rwanda's internal capacity to support digital transformation. The technical assistance will support UNICEF Rwanda to translate this agenda into a coherent, actionable partnership framework aligned with Rwanda’s national digital transformation priorities and the emerging institutional architecture for AI, including the MINICT AI Agency and national AI policy priorities. The TA is intended to provide targeted technical support from the Digital Impact Division (DID ) and the Office of Innovation (OOI) to clarify UNICEF Rwanda's digital transformation function, strengthen internal capacity and governance, and establish a systematic approach to identifying, assessing, prioritizing and scaling digital and AI opportunities. The TA will comprise two complementary areas of support: 1. Office of Innovation (OOI) – AI, Innovation Portfolio and Ecosystem OOI support is requested to establish a more systematic approach to AI and innovation portfolio development and management, including: Support AI and digital opportunity prioritization, building on the existing mapping of UNICEF Rwanda's digital and AI initiatives and identifying a limited number of high-value opportunities for further development. Assess the readiness, feasibility and scale potential of priority innovations, including technical feasibility, user needs, evidence of impact, institutional readiness, scalability, sustainability, cost and potential risks. Support innovation governance and portfolio management, including criteria and processes for screening, prioritizing, monitoring and making decisions on innovation initiatives at different stages of maturity. Develop a practical innovation pipeline, distinguishing between emerging opportunities, proof-of-concept/pilots, innovations ready for scale and initiatives requiring further evidence or investment. Provide innovation ecosystem and partnership support, including identification of relevant government entities, technology companies, innovators, academia, development partners and other strategic partners. Advise on pathways from innovation to scale, including opportunities for government adoption, financing, partnerships and integration into national systems. Provide technical guidance on responsible AI and innovation, including child rights, safety, privacy, data protection, accessibility, inclusion, responsible AI and safety-by-design considerations. Expected OOI outputs: Prioritized AI and digital opportunity portfolio, with clear criteria and rationale for prioritization. Readiness/feasibility assessment of priority innovations and recommendations for next steps. Proposed innovation governance and portfolio management framework. Innovation partnership/ecosystem map and recommendations for strategic engagement. Recommendations for taking priority innovations from proof-of-concept to sustainable scale. Support for Resource Mobilization to enhance Country Office Capacity.

full: Digital Impact Division (DID) – Digital Transformation Architecture and Capacity UNICEF Rwanda is developing a coordinated agenda on child-centred digital transformation, artificial intelligence (AI) and technology for development, in close collaboration with the Ministry of ICT and Innovation (MINICT) and relevant national institutions. The initiative includes development of a UNICEF-MINICT joint workplan, prioritization of AI and digital opportunities, strengthening national child online protection efforts, and building UNICEF Rwanda's internal capacity to support digital transformation. The technical assistance will support UNICEF Rwanda to translate this agenda into a coherent, actionable partnership framework aligned with Rwanda’s national digital transformation priorities and the emerging institutional architecture for AI, including the MINICT AI Agency and national AI policy priorities. The TA is intended to provide targeted technical support from the Digital Impact Division (DID ). The TA will comprise the following areas of support: 1. Digital Impact Division (DID) – Digital Transformation Architecture and Capacity DID support is requested to: Review and advise on the T4D/Digital Transformation position TOR, including the scope, competencies, reporting arrangements and strategic functions required to support UNICEF Rwanda's evolving digital agenda. Technology for Development (T4D) and Artificial Intelligence (AI) Technical Specialist Kigali, Rwanda.docx Advise on UNICEF Rwanda's digital programming approach, including how digital technologies can be systematically integrated across programme sectors and the programme cycle rather than pursued as stand-alone initiatives. Provide technical advice on interoperability and digital architecture, including linkages with government digital systems, data exchange, standards, platforms and opportunities to leverage existing national digital public infrastructure. Advise on digital governance and implementation arrangements, including roles and responsibilities, quality assurance, risk management, data governance, sustainability and alignment with UNICEF and Government requirements. Assess and recommend options for strengthening the Country Office's digital capacity, including the appropriate combination of technical staffing, skills development, internal coordination mechanisms and access to specialized expertise as well as funding. Advise on UNICEF Rwanda's engagement with MINICT and relevant national digital/AI institutions, ensuring that UNICEF's digital programming is aligned with Rwanda's national digital transformation and AI priorities and does not create parallel systems. Expected DID outputs: Review and recommendations on the T4D/Digital Transformation TOR. Assessment of the current UNICEF Rwanda digital programming and capacity model, with identified gaps and opportunities. Recommendations for digital governance, interoperability and implementation arrangements. A proposed digital capacity-strengthening roadmap for the Country Office. Request for UNICEF Support: Nurturing Care Framework (NCF) Training Background and Request The Ministry of Health is planning to conduct a Nurturing Care Framework (NCF) Training for 35 officers drawn from key sectors supporting Early Childhood Development (ECD), including: Child Health/ECD Officers Nutrition Officers Environmental Health Officers Mental Health Officers Rehabilitation Officers Education ECD Officers Home Economics Officers The training aims to strengthen participants' capacity to promote and implement the Nurturing Care Framework through integrated, multisectoral approaches that support the health, nutrition, early learning, protection, and well-being of young children. The Ministry has formally requested UNICEF to provide technical facilitation for the training through qualified NCF facilitators. The proposed training dates are: 12–16 October 2026 , or 19–23 October 2026 The final dates will be confirmed based on the availability of the UNICEF facilitators. Cost Sharing Arrangement The Ministry of Health will cover all training and conference-related costs , including the venue, accommodation, meals, and participant conference fees. UNICEF is requested to support the training by: Providing qualified facilitators to deliver the Nurturing Care Framework training; and Covering the transportation costs of the facilitators to and from the training venue. Expected Results Increased knowledge and skills of 35 frontline and supervisory officers on the Nurturing Care Framework. Improved multisectoral coordination and integration of nurturing care interventions for young children and their caregivers. Enhanced capacity of government officers to support the implementation and scale-up of NCF-aligned ECD services nationwide. Justification The Nurturing Care Framework is a key global framework for advancing holistic early childhood development. Building the capacity of officers across health, nutrition, education, rehabilitation, mental health, and social sectors will contribute to stronger, more integrated services for young children and their families, supporting Botswana's ECD priorities and UNICEF's commitments to ensuring every child survives, thrives, and reaches their full potential

desc: Technical assistance to strategically position SBC within the development of the new CPD (2027-2032)
full: The UNICEF Kenya Country Office is seeking technical assistance to strategically position SBC within the development of the new CPD (2027-2032). The support will help articulate SBC's contribution as a cross-sectoral accelerator for achieving child outcomes, strengthening policy implementation, promoting social accountability, addressing harmful social norms, and enhancing community resilience. The consultation will support evidence-based positioning, development of strategic narratives, identification of results pathways, and integration of SBC approaches across programme outcomes and enabling environments. This request will contribute to ensuring that SBC is appropriately reflected in the CPD strategic framework, explanatory notes, Theory of Change discussions, and programme design processes. Objectives/Expected Results Objective 1 Provide strategic advice on positioning SBC as a cross-cutting accelerator and systems-strengthening function in the Kenya CPD 2027-2032. Expected Result Clear and compelling SBC value proposition linked to UNICEF's mandate, the Kenya context, the CPE findings, and child outcomes. Objective 2 Support the integration of SBC approaches across priority programme outcomes and cross-sectoral programming. Expected Result SBC contributions are reflected within priority pathways, causal analyses, and Theory of Change discussions across sectors. Objective 3 Develop evidence-based arguments and strategic messaging demonstrating how SBC contributes to policy implementation, social accountability, community engagement, behaviour change, and norm transformation. Expected Result Strong positioning narrative and advocacy package that can be used during CPD consultations and drafting processes. Objective 4 Provide recommendations on organisational positioning, measurement, and CPD architecture to ensure SBC's visibility and contribution to results. Expected Result Practical options for integrating SBC into CPD outcomes, outputs, indicators, and implementation arrangements. Objective 5 Strengthen the identification of innovative SBC approaches that can accelerate results for the most vulnerable children and adolescents. Expected Result Clear recommendations on strategic accelerators, innovation opportunities, and partnerships that can be incorporated into CPD design. Proposed Deliverables Inception Consultation Brief review of Kenya CPD timelines, CPE findings, SitAn insights, and strategic priorities. Consultation with SBC team and CPD focal points. SBC Positioning Paper (5-10 pages) Strategic rationale for SBC in the next CPD. Value proposition and comparative advantage. Recommended positioning options. Global good practices and examples from other country programmes. Strategic Messaging Package Key messages for senior management and CPD discussions. Talking points for consultations and workshops. Elevator pitch on SBC's contribution to child outcomes. Technical Review and Inputs Review of explanatory notes and relevant CPD draft sections. Recommendations for integration of SBC language and results pathways. Facilitated Technical Session Participation in selected CPD workshops, Theory of Change discussions, or CPD retreat sessions. Presentation of positioning recommendations and strategic options. Final Recommendations Note Summary of priority actions. Recommendations on governance, measurement, partnerships, capacity strengthening, and sustainability. Strategic Accelerators for High-Impact Results The TA could specifically explore how SBC contributes to the following UNICEF strategic accelerators: 1. Social Norms Transformation Addressing drivers of: Child marriage FGM Violence against children Gender inequality Harmful caregiving practices 2. Technical Assistance Request: Accelerating the First Foods Agenda for Children in Somalia UNICEF Somalia seeks technical assistance to accelerate the First Foods Agenda as a strategic child nutrition and food systems initiative. The support will help translate recent landscape analysis findings into a national implementation roadmap that increases the availability, affordability, acceptability, and consumption of nutritious first foods for infants and young children aged 6-23 months. The TA will support policy development, market-based solutions, private sector engagement, behavior change strategies, and multi-sectoral coordination to advance sustainable, locally driven approaches to preventing child malnutrition in Somalia. This work builds on ongoing efforts to identify nutritious local foods, strengthen food systems, and develop scalable solutions for improving complementary feeding practices. Specific areas of TA support include: Review the landscape analysis Draft report on locally available, affordable and nutrient-rich foods for young children across Somalia. Provide guidance for the development of a UNICEF Somalia First Foods Roadmap: Support development of a clear, multisectoral roadmap with priority actions, partnerships, milestones and opportunities for scale-up Guide on a practical approach to nutrient profiling of locally available foods to identify the best First Foods for children 6–23 months. Guide on translating the findings into simple, affordable and culturally appropriate recipes using locally available foods for young children. Provide technical assistance to identify and engage local producers and businesses, including opportunities to strengthen product quality, availability and affordability. Ensure linkage with UNICEF Supply Division as appropriate Develop a practical First Foods orientation package for programme staff, strengthening integration across Nutrition, Health, WASH, Social and Behaviour Change, and other relevant programmes. Develop simple, compelling messages and advocacy materials tailored to partners, donors, policymakers and relevant Government ministries to build ownership and investment in the First Foods agenda. Explore how the landscape analysis findings can also inform actions to improve the quality and diversity of diets for pregnant and breastfeeding women.

Dear Frank and Auken, As you know, throughout this year Serbia CO has been supporting government institutions in developing a strategic approach to the digitalization of education. One of the key issues that has emerged is AI in education. The main question we are receiving is what are key considerations when it comes to legal regulation of AI - what should be regulated, how it should be regulated, and at what legislative level. In this regard, the Institute for the Improvement of Education and Upbringing (the country's leading expert institution for education) asked us to prepare a brief comparative overview of relevant legislation and define key considerations for Serbia. We started with a short review, but ultimately ended up producing a comprehensive study which, it seems to us, could be highly valuable for UNICEF at the global level. Title of the study is: ARTIFICIAL INTELLIGENCE IN EDUCATION - Comparative review of the legal, ethical and pedagogical framework for the safe and responsible application of AI in education You will see that we have examined the approaches taken in Danmark, Ireland, Latvia, New Zealand, Italy, Türkiye, the United States, Brazil, Mexico, Peru, Chile, Japan, South Korea, China, Spain, Australia, India, and others. If you think it could be useful globally, we could also prepare two separate documents: one with a global focus and another specifically tailored to Serbia. That would not require a significant amount of additional work on our side. Comparative review of AI in education.docx It is machine translation; original is in Serbian. It would be extremely helpful if one of you could review the document and share any suggestions or comments so that we can finalize it. Please let us know if we should open a new CoE ticket for this. Thank you and kind regards, Tanja

desc: Support CO for Digital Innovators Summit
full: Background and context UNICEF Lesotho has been invited to deliver a 30-minute presentation at the Digital Innovators Summit, taking place on 28 August 2026 at the National Health Training College in Lesotho. The wider Summit theme is “Digital Health Innovation: Transforming Healthcare Delivery, Access and Patient Outcomes in Lesotho.” UNICEF’s session will focus on “AI FOR EVERY CHILD – Building a Safer, Healthier Digital Future.” The invitation is attached. The organizers have requested UNICEF to bring a child-centred perspective to the Summit’s discussion, exploring the opportunities and considerations surrounding artificial intelligence and emerging technologies in shaping safer, healthier and more inclusive digital futures for children and young people. The session should connect technological innovation with children’s wellbeing, safety, inclusion and future opportunities. The audience is expected to include representatives of government, academia, the private sector, media, technology practitioners, students and young people. Previous editions of the Summit have addressed issues including artificial intelligence, digital literacy, misinformation, online ethics and inclusive digital transformation. Technical assistance requested UNICEF Lesotho is requesting technical guidance and rapid content support to develop a professional and engaging presentation for the Summit. Specifically, support is requested to: Propose a clear storyline and structure for a 30-minute presentation that balances the opportunities presented by AI with the risks to children and the safeguards required. Provide key evidence, messages and examples that can be adapted for the Lesotho context, drawing on UNICEF’s latest global guidance and experience on AI and children. Identify practical examples of opportunities for children and young people, particularly in: health and wellbeing; education and personalized learning; accessibility and inclusion of children with disabilities; access to information and services; protection and early identification of risks; creativity, participation, skills development and future employment opportunities. Articulate the principal risks and considerations , including privacy and use of children’s data, misinformation, harmful content, bias and discrimination, online exploitation, unequal access, over-reliance on automated systems, and the need for human oversight. Develop practical recommendations for government, technology companies, educators, parents and caregivers, communities, and children and young people. Suggest one or two interactive elements suitable for a mixed audience, such as an opening audience poll, a short scenario, a myth-versus-reality exercise, or questions for audience reflection. Advise on relevant UNICEF resources, examples, graphics or existing slides that may be adapted while maintaining UNICEF branding and messaging. The presentation should be balanced, forward-looking and solutions-oriented. It should not position technology as inherently positive or negative, but demonstrate how innovation can be guided by children’s rights, safety, inclusion and best interests. The content should be aligned with UNICEF’s latest child-centred AI guidance, which addresses safety, privacy, non-discrimination, transparency, accountability, inclusion, children’s development and wellbeing, AI skills, and an enabling governance environment. Expected deliverables By completion of the TA, UNICEF Lesotho would appreciate receiving: A recommended presentation flow or slide-by-slide outline for a 30-minute session. Key messages and evidence for each section. Suggested UNICEF examples, resources and existing materials that can be adapted. Recommendations for strengthening the child protection, health and inclusion dimensions. One or two practical audience engagement activities. If feasible, review and technical comments on the draft presentation prepared by the Country Office. The Country Office will lead the final development, contextualization, design and delivery of the presentation, with support from the Communications, Child Protection, and T4D colleagues. Urgency and requested completion date As the Summit will take place on Friday, 28 August 2026 , the Country Office would appreciate receiving the initial technical inputs and proposed storyline by close of business on Tuesday, 25 August 2026 , if feasible. This would allow time for contextualization, design, internal review and rehearsal before the event. I sincerely apologize for the short turnaround time, and your support is sincerely appreciated.

Technical Assistance Request: Child Online Protection UNICEF Rwanda is developing a more coordinated and strategic approach to digital transformation, AI and innovation to strengthen programme results and position the Country Office to engage effectively with the Government of Rwanda, particularly the Ministry of ICT and Innovation (MINICT), and the wider national digital and AI ecosystem. The TA is intended to provide targeted technical support from Child Protection to strengthen UNICEF Rwanda's contribution to Rwanda's Child Online Protection (COP) agenda, ensuring that national policy, regulatory frameworks and implementation are informed by global evidence, emerging risks and international good practice. As Rwanda accelerates its digital transformation and AI agenda, children are increasingly engaging with digital platforms, AI-enabled tools and online services. While these developments create significant opportunities for learning, participation and innovation, they also increase exposure to online harms including cyberbullying, online sexual exploitation and abuse, harmful content, privacy breaches, misinformation and emerging AI-related risks. Strengthening Child Online Protection is therefore critical to ensuring that Rwanda's digital transformation remains safe, inclusive and rights-based for children. The TA will also support UNICEF Rwanda to identify and mobilize resources and strategic partnerships to advance priority COP interventions. The TA will focus on four complementary areas: 1. Review and Strengthen the Child Online Protection Strategy and Implementation Review the existing Child Online Protection strategy, implementation approach and priority interventions. Assess alignment with Rwanda's evolving digital landscape, national digital and AI priorities, and emerging risks facing children online. Assess institutional readiness, technical capacity and resource requirements for implementation of Child Online Protection measures across relevant government institutions and partners. Identify implementation gaps, institutional roles and opportunities to strengthen coordination among Government, UNICEF and other stakeholders. Map key stakeholders involved in Child Online Protection, including MINICT, RISA, the National Cyber Security Authority, Rwanda Investigation Bureau, NCDA, NCPD, Ministry of Education, telecommunications operators, technology companies, academia, civil society organizations, and children and young people. Identify evidence based priority capacity-building needs for policymakers, regulators, law enforcement, educators, social service workers and child protection practitioners to strengthen implementation of Child Online Protection measures. Develop a prioritized implementation roadmap, including key actions, milestones, responsibilities and indicators. Strengthen integration of child rights, gender, disability inclusion, age-appropriate approaches and child participation within the COP agenda. 2. Support Development of Regulatory and Policy Guidance Provide technical advice to strengthen Rwanda's policy and regulatory framework for child online safety, drawing on international standards and emerging global practice. Review relevant existing and proposed policies, legislation, regulations and guidelines and identify gaps or areas requiring strengthening. Develop or strengthen practical guidance on safety-by-design, age-appropriate digital services, online harms, privacy and data protection, responsible AI, child rights impact assessments, age assurance approaches, reporting and response mechanisms, and platform accountability. Provide technical advice on child rights and AI governance, including algorithmic accountability, transparency, mitigation of AI-enabled harms, protection from deepfakes and synthetic media, and safeguards relating to generative AI systems used by or affecting children. Support alignment of Child Online Protection with Rwanda's broader digital transformation and AI policy environment and UNICEF's global child rights mandate. 3. Global Evidence, Learning and Technical Expertise Collate and synthesize global evidence, research, tools and lessons learned on child online safety, with particular attention to approaches relevant to Rwanda and other low- and middle-income country contexts. Identify emerging and future risks associated with children's use of digital technologies, including AI-enabled risks and opportunities. Facilitate access to relevant global technical expertise, peer learning and UNICEF resources, including examples of effective policy, regulatory, prevention and response approaches. Establish a practical evidence and knowledge base to inform UNICEF Rwanda's policy dialogue, programming and engagement with Government and partners. 4. Resource Mobilization and Strategic Partnerships Support UNICEF Rwanda to identify and articulate priority investment opportunities arising from the COP strategy and implementation roadmap. Develop or strengthen a resource mobilization proposition for Child Online Protection, including potential funding areas, investment cases and results narratives. Map and engage potential bilateral, multilateral, philanthropic and private-sector partners interested in child online safety, responsible technology and digital rights. Provide technical inputs to concept notes, proposals and donor engagement materials to mobilize resources for priority COP interventions. Identify opportunities for strategic partnerships and co-investment with Government, technology companies, academia, civil society and other actors in Rwanda's digital ecosystem. Expected outputs The TA would support UNICEF Rwanda to deliver: A strengthened Child Online Protection strategy and implementation roadmap, with clear priorities, actions, responsibilities, milestones and indicators. Recommendations and/or draft policy and regulatory guidance to strengthen Rwanda's child online safety framework. A synthesized global evidence and learning package highlighting international practice, emerging risks and relevant technical tools. A Child Online Protection resource mobilization and partnership proposition, identifying priority investment areas, potential funding partners and opportunities for collaboration. Targeted technical inputs to resource mobilization efforts, including concept notes, proposals and donor engagement. Recommendations for sustained technical capacity and coordination among UNICEF, Government and key stakeholders to strengthen child online safety in Rwanda. Based on the child online protection research, a stakeholder and institutional mapping analysis identifying key actors, roles, responsibilities, coordination mechanisms and capacity gaps across government, private sector, academia, civil society and development partners involved in Child Online Protection. A costed Child Online Protection implementation roadmap and investment case identifying priority interventions, financing requirements and opportunities for resource mobilization and strategic partnerships.

Request summary The UNICEF Haiti Country Office requests technical support from the Centre of Excellence to strengthen adolescent and youth livelihoods programming, with a focus on vocational training, market-relevant skills, employability, entrepreneurship and pathways from learning to earning. The request will support implementation of Outcome 2 of the HCO Adolescent Strategy, including Output 2.1 on access to education, learning-to-earning, employability and entrepreneurship opportunities, and Output 2.2 on systems and platforms that facilitate transitions from education to skills development, employment and entrepreneurship. Background and rationale Adolescents and young people in Haiti face disrupted education pathways, limited access to vocational training and scarce formal employment. Existing training opportunities are limited in scale, difficult to access in insecure areas and not always aligned with labour -market demand. Adolescent girls, displaced and out-of-school adolescents, young people with disabilities, and those at risk of recruitment by armed groups face additional barriers. UNICEF Haiti already has relevant entry points, including vocational training pilots, life-skills and psychosocial support, cash-for- skills and cash-plus approaches, PREJEUNES, U-Report, UPSHIFT and potential Generation Unlimited partnerships. However, these efforts need stronger coherence, prioritization and links to realistic economic opportunities. 3. Objective To help UNICEF Haiti define a practical, inclusive and context-appropriate approach for implementing the learning-to-earning and livelihoods components of the Adolescent Strategy. 4. Technical support requested Conduct a rapid review of the Haiti context, existing initiatives, priority groups and operational constraints. Identify partnership opportunities with government, vocational training institutions, youth-led organizations, the private sector, diaspora networks and Generation Unlimited. desc: Safe to learn benchmarking assessment
full: The Guatemala Country Office seeks Technical Assistance (TA) support to conduct a benchmarking study under the Safe to Learn Initiative. The assignment should analyze global, regional, and country-level evidence on preventing violence against children in and around schools, promoting safe and inclusive learning environments, and strengthening multi-sectoral approaches to child well-being and learning. desc: Support to conduct a Gender Programmatic Review to inform CPD development
full: Request technical support from Gender Equality Team GPD to accompany the Costa Rica Country Office throughout the Gender Programmatic Review process. While an external consultant will lead the review, the Gender Programme Specialist, GPD will provide technical guidance, quality assurance, and strategic advice to ensure the review is aligned with UNICEF Gender Eqaulity Action Plan priorities, reflects gender-responsive approaches, and generates actionable recommendations that strengthen programme effectiveness and results for children. Objectives Objective 1: Provide Technical Guidance Throughout the Review Process Advise the Country Office and consultant on the review scope, methodology, analytical framework, and expected standards. Ensure alignment with UNICEF gender policies, guidance, and global good practices. Support the identification of priority gender issues and strategic entry points across programme areas. Objective 2: Ensure Quality Assurance of Review Outputs Review and provide technical feedback on key deliverables produced by the consultant, including the inception report, draft findings, and final report. Ensure that recommendations are evidence-based, practical, and aligned with country programme priorities. Promote a gender-transformative and intersectional approach throughout the review. Objective 3: Strengthen Internal Ownership and Use of Findings Facilitate reflection and discussion with programme teams and management on emerging findings and recommendations. Support the prioritization of actions that can be integrated into programme planning, implementation, monitoring, and future strategic processes. Help position the review as an opportunity to strengthen organizational capacity and accountability for gender results. Objective 4: Support Translation of Findings into Action Advise on the development of an actionable roadmap based on review recommendations. Identify opportunities for strengthening programme effectiveness, partnerships, evidence generation, and resource mobilization related to gender equality outcomes. Support integration of recommendations into existing planning and reporting mechanisms. Expected Deliverables from the Regional Gender Specialist Technical input into the Terms of Reference for the consultant , including review methodology and expected standards. Participation in key review milestones , including: Inception meeting. Mid-point reflection or validation discussion. Final presentation of findings and recommendations. Technical review and quality assurance of: Inception report. Draft Gender Programmatic Review report. Final report and recommendations. Proposed management response/action plan. Strategic guidance note or feedback memo summarizing key priorities and opportunities for strengthening gender-transformative programming. Facilitation or participation in a validation workshop with Country Office management and programme teams to support prioritization and uptake of recommendations. Other Global Practices to Potentially Engage To ensure recommendations are actionable and integrated across sectors, the Regional Gender Specialist may identify the need for inputs from: Social Policy Child Protection Education Health Nutrition WASH Adolescent Development and Participation (ADAP) Disability Inclusion Monitoring and Evaluation/Data & Analytics Planning and Programme Effectiveness teams Their involvement would be targeted and based on findings emerging from the review. Strategic Accelerators for Results for Children The Regional Gender Specialist could help identify opportunities to leverage: Gender-transformative social and behavior change approaches. Adolescent girls' empowerment and leadership. Increased use of disaggregated data and gender evidence. Cross-sectoral programming to address multiple deprivations. Gender-responsive financing and budgeting. Strategic partnerships with women's rights organizations, youth networks, academia, and government. Systems strengthening and institutionalization of gender-responsive approaches. Intersectional approaches targeting the most vulnerable children and adolescents. Through technical accompaniment from the Regional Gender Specialist, the Country Office will ensure that the Gender Programmatic Review is implemented in line with UNICEF standards and global good practices, resulting in high-quality, actionable recommendations and a clear roadmap to strengthen gender-transformative programming and accelerate equitable results for children and adolescents.

desc: CPD development TA - Lebanon
full: Details/ Description: The Lebanon Country Office is initiating the development of its Country Programme Document (CPD) for the period 2028–2032 (timeline of 5 years yet to be confirmed at the UNCT), as such the LCO requests technical assistance and engagement from HQ, the ECAMENA RO, and relevant colleagues/ advisors from the Centres of Excellence (CoEs) throughout the CPD development process. The requested support aims to strengthen the quality of the situation analysis, strategic positioning, results framework development, and overall programme design, while ensuring alignment with UNICEF corporate priorities, regional priorities, and the evolving context in Lebanon. Requested Support 1. Ongoing Technical Support from Regional Advisors and Centres of Excellence: LCO requests long-distance and, where feasible, in-country technical support from RO and relevant Centres of Excellence Advisors to programmes and operational sections, including: Technical guidance on sectoral and cross-sectoral programme design. Review and feedback on analytical products and draft CPD components – including the Evidence Synthesis and Inter-Agency Foresight. Advice on emerging priorities, innovation, evidence generation, and programme effectiveness. Participation in key milestones and consultations as required. 2. Strategic Exchange between the Regional Director and the Country Office Representative: As previously discussed with MENARO, LCO requests support in facilitating an early strategic exchange between the Regional Director (RD) and the UNICEF Lebanon Representative, with the engagement provisionally planned for mid-September 2026 and would provide an opportunity to: 1) Discuss the strategic direction and ambition of the CPD 2028–2032; 2) Align expectations regarding regional and global priorities; 3) Identify key areas of focus and opportunities for transformational programming; and 4) Provide early strategic guidance ahead of the Strategic Moments of Reflection (SMRs). 3. Participation of HQ/RO/CoE Colleagues in the First Strategic Moment of Reflection (SMR): LCO requests the participation and support of HQ, RO and relevant CoE colleagues in the first Strategic Moment of Reflection (SMR), planned through two workshops: 1) All Staff: October 2026; and 2) Workshop with some external stakeholders: November 2026. This first SMR will serve as the primary visioning exercise for the CPD 2028–2032 and will help shape the strategic direction of the next programme cycle. Support requested includes: Virtual and/or in-person participation of HQ, RO, and CoE advisors. Technical inputs on global and regional trends, UNICEF strategic priorities, and innovative programming approaches. Facilitation and technical contributions during discussions on strategic choices and programme positioning. Consideration of in-country missions by selected CoE advisors, particularly to support the internal SMR workshop and discussions on programme vision and strategic focus. 4. Participation of HQ/RO/CoE Colleagues in the Second Strategic Moment of Reflection (SMR): LCO also requests the participation of HQ, RO and relevant CoE colleagues in the second Strategic Moment of Reflection, planned for January 2027 (or February 2027) with the Government of Lebanon. This SMR is expected to take place once an initial CPD draft and preliminary programme framework have been developed and will focus on: Validation of the emerging CPD strategic framework. Review of programme priorities, outcomes and results. Assessment of coherence across programme areas. Strategic quality assurance and recommendations before finalization of the CPD. The presence and engagement of HQ, RO and CoE colleagues would be highly valuable in ensuring that the draft CPD reflects UNICEF’s strategic ambitions and meets corporate quality standards. (We might want to invite also the RD and/or ECAMENA DRDs depending on their availability to the SMR II; would also suggest to have some representation from Operations). Expected Outcome: The requested technical assistance will contribute to the development of a high-quality, evidence-based and forward-looking CPD 2028–2032 for Lebanon, ensuring strong strategic alignment with UNICEF regional and global priorities while responding effectively to the evolving needs and opportunities for children and adolescents in Lebanon.

desc: Joint UNICEF Centre of Excellence Mission for Gavi 6.0 Preparation and Polio–Immunization Integration Support in Madagascar
full: Cette mission d'assistance technique du Centre of Excellence (CoE) de l'UNICEF s'inscrit dans le cadre de l'appui stratégique au Gouvernement de Madagascar et aux partenaires du Programme Elargi de Vaccination (PEV) pour la préparation de la soumission Gavi 6.0. La mission revêt une importance particulière à un moment clé du processus de planification du programme d'immunisation pour la période 2026-2030. Elle permettra d'apporter un soutien technique de haut niveau aux équipes nationales dans l'analyse des priorités, la définition des investissements stratégiques et l'élaboration d'une demande de financement solide, alignée sur les orientations de Gavi 6.0 ainsi que sur les priorités nationales du secteur de la santé. La mission contribuera également à renforcer l'intégration des interventions Polio et Immunisation afin d'améliorer les performances globales du programme de vaccination. Cette approche est particulièrement pertinente dans le contexte de la persistance du risque de transmission du poliovirus dérivé d'une souche vaccinale circulante (cVDPV) à Madagascar. L'appui conjoint UNICEF-OMS permettra d'identifier les opportunités d'intégration, de renforcer la coordination entre les acteurs et de promouvoir des stratégies visant simultanément l'amélioration de la couverture vaccinale de routine, la qualité des campagnes de vaccination et l'interruption durable de la transmission du poliovirus. Les objectifs spécifiques de la mission sont les suivants : Appuyer le processus d'élaboration de la soumission Gavi 6.0 en collaboration avec le Ministère de la Santé, le PEV, l'OMS et les autres partenaires techniques et financiers ; Faciliter les discussions stratégiques avec les parties prenantes sur les priorités d'investissement et les approches programmatiques pour la période Gavi 6.0 ; Évaluer les opportunités de renforcement de l'intégration Polio-Immunisation aux niveaux national et infranational ; Identifier les actions prioritaires permettant d'améliorer la performance du programme de vaccination et de contribuer à l'arrêt de la transmission du cVDPV ; Renforcer la coordination entre le Gouvernement, l'UNICEF, l'OMS et les partenaires impliqués dans l'immunisation et l'éradication de la poliomyélite. La mission est prévue du 14 au 18 septembre 2026 et bénéficiera de la participation des experts du Centre of Excellence de l'UNICEF ainsi que des partenaires concernés, offrant ainsi une opportunité unique de renforcer la qualité technique de la soumission Gavi 6.0 et d'accélérer les progrès vers les objectifs d'immunisation et d'éradication de la poliomyélite à Madagascar.

Please find the tentative agenda attached for your reference. I have informed our UNDP colleague, the UN’s focal person working with MEA, that UNICEF would be pleased to contribute a presentation on "Working Across Sectors to Protect Children from Air Pollution ." This topic places children at the center of the discussion, and I have suggested that it be included in the morning session of the conference. I has reached out to Abheet Solomon (Climate resilience) and he has kindly agreed to deliver this presentation; and I will continue to follow up with UNDP and WHO colleagues and keep you updated on our proposal. Regarding the afternoon session on Data Sharing and AI for Addressing the Health Impacts of Air Pollution , I would appreciate your views on UNICEF's potential engagement. Do we have relevant experiences, good practices, or lessons learned related to children data, AI and or DX that could be shared during this session? Thank you, and I look forward to receiving your comments and advice. Best regards,

Subject: Request for technical assistance on community engagement, SBC, and gender-responsive digital literacy under the Pandemic Fund UNICEF Honduras would like to request technical assistance from the Centre of Excellence to support the implementation of the community engagement component of the Pandemic Fund programme. We propose an in-country technical mission from 26 to 30 October 2026 (dates negotiated with government counterparts), with the participation of a Social and Behaviour Change (SBC) specialist and complementary expertise in digital literacy and gender-responsive programming. The requested technical assistance will support national partners and the Pandemic Fund implementation team to strengthen inclusive, community-centred approaches for pandemic prevention, preparedness, and response. The mission would focus on the following areas: Review the existing community engagement and SBC approach under the Pandemic Fund and identify implementation gaps and opportunities. Support the development or refinement of an evidence-based SBC and community engagement strategy. Strengthen the capacity of government institutions, implementing partners, and community actors to design and deliver inclusive interventions. Integrate digital literacy and digital inclusion into community engagement activities, particularly for populations with limited access to trusted health information and digital platforms. Apply a gender lens to identify and address barriers affecting women, adolescent girls, persons with disabilities, Indigenous and Afro-descendant communities, rural populations, and other groups at risk of exclusion. Strengthen mechanisms for community participation, two-way communication, social listening, feedback, and accountability. Develop practical recommendations, indicators, and an initial action plan for integrating SBC, digital literacy, and gender-responsive approaches throughout Pandemic Fund implementation. Expected outputs (proposal) The mission is expected to deliver: A rapid assessment of the current community engagement and SBC component (prior to the mission) Recommendations for integrating SBC, digital literacy, gender equality, and social inclusion within community engagement component. A facilitated technical workshop with government counterparts, implementing partners, and relevant stakeholders. A draft action plan outlining priority activities, responsible actors, timelines, and monitoring indicators. A brief mission report documenting key findings, agreements, and recommended next steps. Spanish speakers is required, considering Government counterparts do not speak english.

Malawi Country Office under Gender and Health is requesting technical Assistance request on the development of a Gender Training Package for the Health Sector and capacity building of the health sector in gender transformative programming under Pandemic Fund. Despite progress in strengthening health systems, gender-related barriers continue to influence access to, utilization of, and outcomes of health services among women, men, girls, and boys. Health workers often have limited practical skills and tools to identify, analyze, and address gender inequalities within service delivery, emergency preparedness, health promotion, and community engagement. To strengthen gender-responsive and gender-transformative health programming, there is a need to develop a standardized training package that equips health personnel with the knowledge, competencies, and practical tools required to integrate gender equality, social inclusion, safeguarding, and equity considerations across health interventions. This initiative aligns with ongoing efforts to strengthen health workforce capacity and institutionalize gender-responsive approaches within the health sector. The Objective is to provide technical support for the development, validation, and rollout of a competency-based Gender Training Package for Health Personnel and to strengthen the capacity of health workers to integrate gender-transformative approaches in health programming and service delivery. The expected outcome/results are as follows -. Standardized national Gender Training Package for Health Personnel developed and approved - Increased knowledge and skills of health workers on gender-responsive and gender-transformative health programming. - Enhanced capacity of health facilities and district health management teams to address gender barriers in service delivery. - Strengthened integration of gender equality, safeguarding, equity, and inclusion in health programmes. - Established pool of certified trainers capable of sustaining future capacity-building efforts.

MCO experiences emergencies due to natural disasters and disease outbreaks. These exacerbates vulnerabilities among women and adolescent girls. While Malawi has made some progress in mainstreaming gender, GBV and PSEA across humanitarian and development programming, challenges in ensuring consistent integration, implementation and reporting across sectors during emergency response. MCO has therefore planned to have emergency focal points and some IPs get trained to have the knowledge, tools and practical skills to effectively identify and address gender inequalities, GBV risks, safeguarding concerns and PSEA obligations in all phases of emergency programming. UNICEF Malawi Country Office therefore kindly requests technical assistance from the Centre of Excellence to strengthen the capacity of Emergency Focal Points and key implementing partners on the integration of Gender, Gender-Based Violence (GBV), and Prevention of Sexual Exploitation and Abuse (PSEA) in emergency preparedness and response. Specifically, the requested technical assistance would support: Capacity Building: Training emergency focal points and sector leads on gender-responsive and survivor-centred emergency programming; Strengthening understanding of GBV risk mitigation and safe programming across sectors and enhancing knowledge of PSEA minimum standards, accountability to affected populations, and referral pathways. Technical Guidance and Tools: Development/adaptation of practical guidance, checklists and tools for integrating gender, GBV and PSEA into emergency assessments, planning, implementation and monitoring; and support for harmonized reporting on agreed Gender, GBV and PSEA indicators across sectors. Follow-up Support: Ongoing technical coaching to emergency focal points during preparedness and response activities and supporting in institutionalizing gender, GBV and PSEA considerations within emergency coordination mechanisms and contingency planning processes. Preferred Modality: Hybrid (virtual and in-person) Expected Outputs Emergency focal points and relevant implementing partners capacitated on Gender, GBV and PSEA integration in humanitarian action. Strengthened sectoral capacity to identify, mitigate and monitor GBV and safeguarding risks in emergencies. Improved reporting against agreed Gender, GBV and PSEA indicators. Enhanced accountability and protection outcomes for women, girls, boys and other at-risk populations affected by emergencies. We would greatly appreciate the Centre of Excellence's support in strengthening UNICEF Malawi's capacity to deliver gender-responsive, safe and accountable emergency programming. Kind regards, Christobel Chakwana Gender Programme Specialist UNICEF Malawi Country Office

UNICEF Mali is seeking technical assistance to support the finalization and implementation of a national study on the Behavioral and Social Drivers (BeSD) of Vaccination in Mali , developed in collaboration with a multidisciplinary team of national researchers and immunization stakeholders. The study aims to generate actionable evidence on the social, behavioral, community, and service-related factors influencing vaccine uptake, with a particular focus on zero-dose and under-vaccinated children. The requested support will include: An independent technical review of the draft research protocol, methodology, data collection tools, analysis framework, and budget to ensure alignment with the WHO BeSD framework, scientific rigor, operational feasibility, ethical standards, and value for money. Recommendations to strengthen the coherence between the research questions, sampling strategy, mixed-methods design, implementation plan, expected outputs, and budget assumptions. Ongoing technical accompaniment of the research team throughout the research process, including protocol finalization, tool development, training, data collection, analysis, interpretation of findings, and formulation of actionable recommendations for immunization programming and SBC interventions. Periodic technical consultations with UNICEF and the research team to address emerging methodological questions, quality assurance issues, and implementation challenges during the study lifecycle. The overall objective is to ensure that the study produces high-quality, policy-relevant evidence that can directly inform immunization demand generation, community engagement strategies, and efforts to reach zero-dose and under-vaccinated children in Mali.
