desc: Pandemic Fund Proposal Development Technical Assistance
full: Technical Review and Strategic Guidance for Uganda's Pandemic Fund Round 4 Proposal Development Uganda has been selected among the countries eligible to benefit from the Pandemic Fund Fourth Call for Proposals. UNICEF Uganda requests targeted technical assistance to support the review, strengthening, and strategic positioning of the national Pandemic Fund proposal. The TA will provide technical expertise and quality assurance throughout proposal development to ensure alignment with Pandemic Fund priorities, strengthen the investment case, identify opportunities to maximize impact for children and communities, and increase the likelihood of a successful submission. The support will also facilitate integration of child-sensitive and equity-focused approaches across prevention, preparedness, and response (PPR) systems strengthening. Objectives / Expectations Objective 1: Technical Quality Assurance of the Proposal Provide expert technical review of the draft proposal to ensure alignment with Pandemic Fund requirements, investment priorities, and assessment criteria. Expected Results Proposal demonstrates strong technical quality and strategic coherence. Clear articulation of outcomes, results framework, and implementation arrangements. Strong evidence base and justification for proposed investments. Objective 2: Strengthen Child-Centered and Equity-Focused PPR Investments Ensure proposed interventions maximize benefits for children, adolescents, women, and vulnerable populations within Uganda's health security agenda. Expected Results Child-sensitive and equity considerations integrated throughout the proposal. Investments linked to improved resilience of essential health services, community systems, and disease surveillance. Strong focus on reaching underserved populations. Objective 3: Enhance Multisectoral and Systems Strengthening Approaches Support identification of opportunities to strengthen collaboration across sectors and partners while building sustainable national capacities. Expected Results Proposal reflects a One Health and multisectoral approach. Strong linkages between health systems strengthening and pandemic preparedness. Clear roles of government, implementing entities, and partners. Objective 4: Improve Proposal Competitiveness Provide strategic advice to enhance the proposal's overall competitiveness and alignment with global best practices and lessons learned from previous Pandemic Fund rounds. Expected Results Proposal addresses key review criteria and demonstrates value for money. High-impact, scalable, and sustainable interventions prioritized. Risks, assumptions, and implementation feasibility adequately addressed. Proposed Deliverables Inception Meeting and Workplan Brief discussion with UNICEF Uganda and partners to confirm scope, timelines, and support needs. Technical Review Report Detailed assessment of draft proposal. Identification of strengths, gaps, risks, and recommendations for improvement. Strategic Advisory Support Ongoing technical feedback during proposal refinement. Support to ensure coherence among technical sections, budget, and results framework. Child and Equity Lens Assessment Recommendations for strengthening child-focused, gender-responsive, and equity-oriented interventions. Review of Results Framework and Indicators Validation of indicators, targets, and monitoring approaches. Alignment with Pandemic Fund expectations and country priorities. Final Proposal Quality Assurance Review Comprehensive review of near-final submission package. Recommendations to improve clarity, consistency, and competitiveness. Knowledge Note/Brief Summary of key recommendations and strategic considerations for implementation readiness following approval. Global Practice and Technical Teams to Involve The HEPR Team , responsible for the Pandemic Fund Portfolios, is expected to lead the provision of this TA. As may be required, given the multidimensional nature of Pandemic Fund investments, the HEPR team will coordinate with the required Global Practices and technical teams that should be engaged. Justification Technical assistance is requested to provide specialized technical review and strategic advisory support for Uganda's Pandemic Fund Round 4 proposal development. The support will ensure the proposal meets Pandemic Fund technical and quality standards, incorporates child-focused and equity-driven investments, reflects global best practices in pandemic preparedness and response, and maximizes Uganda's chances of securing funding while delivering sustainable results for children and vulnerable populations.

Request for Technical Assistance for the 5th International Colloquium on Children's Rights We would like to request technical assistance for the 5th International Colloquium on Children's Rights , which will take place in Mozambique on 10-11 September 2026 . The event is organized by the Supreme Court of Mozambique , with the support of UNICEF Mozambique , as part of the judiciary's ongoing efforts to strengthen dialogue, reflection, and action on children's rights and access to justice. The Colloquium will bring together a diverse range of stakeholders, including representatives from the justice sector, government institutions, academia, development partners, civil society organizations, and international experts. While the agenda encompasses important legal and normative aspects of children's rights, the event also presents a valuable opportunity to promote a more practical and action-oriented discussion. In particular, it seeks to bridge global and regional standards with concrete measures that can support the advancement of justice reforms and improve outcomes for children. In this context, we would like to invite Ms. Grace Agcaoli, Specialist in Juvenile Justice and Legal Reform , to deliver a Virtual/Online presentation on key international and regional legal instruments for the protection of children's rights . The presentation would highlight the linkages between international and regional standards, while also exploring their practical application in strengthening child justice systems and informing justice sector reforms. We believe Ms. Agcaoli's expertise and experience would make a valuable contribution to the Colloquium's objectives and enrich the discussions among participants. We would be grateful for your consideration and support of this request.

Dear Fatima. Greetings from Kyiv. May I kindly request to review the request of the MOH on vaccine procurement for Ukraine. The Public Health Center (PHC) has requested Gavi’s support for urgent adjustments under Fragility 2.0, based on updated vaccine utilization, stock levels, and forecasting. The slower-than-anticipated transition to the updated National Immunization Schedule has resulted in lower-than-forecast pentavalent and IPV utilization, while demand for DTP and Hib vaccines remains higher than expected, creating a potential shortage risk compounded by the current inability of the national procurement agency to procure these vaccines through routine mechanisms. Your kind feedback will be highly appreciated. Thank you and kind regards, Serhii.

desc: Mental Health and Psychosocial Support Capacity Strengthening, Quality Assurance and Scale-Up Support for the State of Palestine
full: Technical Assistance Request for State of Palestine: MHPSS Capacity Strengthening and Quality Assurance in Gaza and the West Bank Short Description Request technical assistance from the MHPSS team to support quality assurance, capacity strengthening, supervision, and strategic scale-up of key UNICEF-supported MHPSS interventions in Gaza and the West Bank. The support would include an in-country mission covering both contexts, followed by ongoing remote supervision and mentoring for trainers, counsellors, and facilitators. Areas of focus include Teaching Recovery Techniques (TRT), Play to Heal, Tammani Annak, disability-inclusive parenting, psychosocial support for injured children, and strengthening supervision and monitoring systems. Objectives and Expectations Gaza Strip Conduct advanced refresher training and technical supervision for TRT and Play to Heal trainers and facilitators. Strengthen quality assurance and fidelity of implementation for Play to Heal and TRT. Provide technical guidance on psychosocial pain management and psychosocial rehabilitation support for children with conflict-related injuries and disabilities. Support integration of disability-inclusive approaches within parenting and caregiver support programmes. West Bank Deliver a TRT Training of Trainers (ToT) for specialized counsellors and MHPSS core trainers in the North and Central/South West Bank. Review implementation of Play to Heal following rollout in East Jerusalem and the West Bank and provide recommendations for strengthening quality and supervision. Facilitate consultation sessions on Tammani Annak following piloting and rollout, including recommendations for scale-up, sustainability, organizational self-care policies, and adaptation for adolescents. Support UNICEF, partners, and the MHPSS Technical Working Group in strengthening capacity-building, monitoring, supervision, and quality assurance structures for MHPSS services. Gaza and West Bank Provide technical assistance to UNICEF State of Palestine in designing and establishing a structured supervision and mentoring framework for trainers and facilitators implementing MHPSS interventions. Support UNICEF and partners in strengthening national capacity to sustain high-quality delivery of evidence-based MHPSS interventions through training, supervision, and quality assurance mechanisms. Provide recommendations and practical guidance to UNICEF on scaling up multi-layered MHPSS services for children and adolescents while maintaining quality, safeguarding, and implementation standards. Support the development of a roadmap for ongoing supervision, mentoring, and workforce development that can be implemented and managed by UNICEF and partners.

desc: COE Digital Expert Support for GCRI Roadmap Phase: Application Review, Transition Decisions & System Rationalization
full: The Global Cyber Resiliency Initiative (GCRI) has completed the Assessment Phase, identifying 1,900+ digital systems across country offices, including T4D initiatives, fundraising platforms, and custom operational systems. Assessment results reveal critical issues requiring expert evaluation during the Roadmap Phase, such as: Fragmented system landscape; many systems built outside governance pathways. High‑risk systems lacking maintenance contracts, proper hosting, authentication, or classification. Need for programmatic validation to determine whether a system should be updated, transitioned, or decommissioned. UNICEF lacks sufficient specialized digital expertise—particularly in product viability, architectural fitness, modernisation pathways, and field‑programme relevance—to ensure high‑quality decisions in the Roadmap Phase. TAHUB / COE Digital engagement is required to ensure safe, sustainable, and programmatically aligned decisions globally.

desc: Establish a national, child-centred DRM policy embedding resilience, early warning, and climate adaptation across sectors.
full: Module A — DRM Policy co-design & consultation (≈ 10–12 weeks) What CoE does: Provide policy drafting support (structure, content, inter-ministerial roles) and facilitate a concise consultative process at national and zoba levels; prepare an operationalization plan (governance, SOPs, early warning, preparedness drills, financing hooks). What it strengthens: A child-centred DRM Policy, validated and ready for adoption, with a clear action plan and role handshakes. Standards/tools: UNICEF CEED/DRR guidance; consultation playbook; operational plan templates. Module B — Light vulnerability profiling (2–3 zobas) What CoE does: Apply a rapid, indicator-based profile (hazard exposure, WASH/health/nutrition access, school resilience, protection risks); map existing assets (solar water systems, catchments, early warning practices). What it strengthens: Practical evidence to prioritize resilience investments and preparedness routines. Standards/tools: Rapid profiling toolkit; simple geotag forms; child risk lens (LNOB/HRBA). Module C — Programme integration: shock-resilience & climate adaptation What CoE does: Run short design clinics with WASH/Health/Nutrition/Education/Child Protection to embed resilience add-ons (e.g., climate-resilient WASH O&M, school safety/continuity, nutrition continuity, protection case-management contingencies). What it strengthens: Realistic resilience features inside ongoing activities; documented add-ons and quick wins. Standards/tools: Resilience add-on menu; preparedness SOPs; continuity checklists. Module D — Early warning & preparedness routines (lite) What CoE does: Set up simple early warning triggers and action protocols in pilot zobas; support quarterly preparedness drills; create a one-page dashboard for PMT/CMT. What it strengthens: Predictable preparedness and faster response; leadership visibility on risk status. Standards/tools: EW trigger table; drill playbook; dashboard template.

desc: Transition to proactive, child-centred shock-responsive systems ensuring continuity of services amid climate hazards.
full: UNICEF seeks technical support to advance the Shock-Responsive Systems (SRS) approach across all sectors, strengthening early anticipatory action planning and ensuring coordinated internal strategic planning to address systemic bottlenecks in emergency preparedness and response. Assistance is required to work with government counterparts to reinforce governance structures, enhance ex-ante and post-ante disaster financing, and improve risk data analysis. This support will also strengthen programming delivery before and after disasters, ensuring continuity of essential services and building resilience. The initiative aims to embed proactive, integrated approaches that safeguard children and communities against escalating climate and disaster risks.

desc: Develop structured guidance on solar system design principles and implementation planning to improve consistency and reduce risk.
full: The Government of Comoros has requested UNICEF’s technical support to develop a national SOP for climate-resilient solar assets, focusing on health and education facilities across the islands. The SOP will provide clear standards and procedures for the design, procurement, installation, operation, maintenance, and monitoring of solar PV systems. It will be tailored to Comoros’ specific climate risks, including cyclones, strong winds, heavy rainfall, flooding, humidity, salt corrosion, and lightning. The aim is to ensure that solar systems installed in schools and health facilities are safe, durable, climate-resilient, and able to support essential services during and after climate shocks. The SOP will also help harmonise standards across the country and guide government, UNICEF, contractors, and facility teams on quality assurance, O&M responsibilities, asset management, and post-disaster response.
